Against baselines with a single pass (Category A), multi-agent accuracy differences are negative overall and near zero when omitting the largest contributing study. When evaluated against baselines matched on sample count (Category B) or resource budget (Category C), multi-agent systems average -0.042 in accuracy, and multilevel random effects modeling
se07c9a1525.summary: An arXiv paper synthesizes 516 multi-agent LLM configurations to separate the effects of coordination, ensembling, and test-time compute on accuracy.
se07c9a1525.why: Multi-agent gains may come mostly from extra samples or compute rather than coordination, which affects how teams benchmark agent architectures.

saba8fc79bb.title: LLM-Guided Cluster Lifecycle Management: Deciding When and How to Evolve Behavioral Clusters
saba8fc79bb.description: arXiv:2611.17616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Behavioral clusters learned over user or item interactions drift as behavior evolves: some fragment into sub-behaviors, some converge, some disappear, and new patterns emerge. Two paradigms dominate the maintenance of evolving clusterings. Threshold triggers fire a pre-specified action when a hardcoded statistic crosses a cutoff; refit-and-track (MONIC-style) re-clusters every window and infers transitions from how the new clusters align with the previous window's. Both hardwire the decision into a threshold or a re-clustering rule. We study an alternative in which a large language model (LLM) makes the lifecycle decision in place. Given a threshold-free, whole-population view of the current cluster set (statistical health, labels, member tex
saba8fc79bb.summary: An arXiv paper studies using an LLM to decide when and how to evolve behavioral clusters as user or item patterns drift over time.
saba8fc79bb.why: Offers an alternative to fixed threshold triggers and refit-and-track rules for maintaining evolving clusterings in production systems.

s3999cbf15f.title: Safety Side Effects of Preventative Persona Steering: An Empirical Audit
s3999cbf15f.description: arXiv:2611.17620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-level behaviors such as sycophancy and hallucination correspond to directions in a model's activation space (Chen et al., 2025). These directions, known as persona vectors, can suppress undesirable traits either at inference time, subtracting the vector during generation, or through preventative steering, adding the vector during fine-tuning, so the optimizer never needs to encode the trait in weights, then removing the vector at evaluation. Chen et al. (2025) recommend preventative steering because it preserves Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) accuracy, but validations of this recommendation have measured capability alone. s3999cbf15f.summary: An arXiv paper audits safety side effects of preventative persona steering, which adds persona vectors during fine-tuning to suppress traits like sycophancy and hallucination.
s3999cbf15f.why: Engineers using activation steering to curb model traits should check whether preventative steering introduces unintended safety regressions before adopting it.

sc82788cf56.title: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs
sc82788cf56.description: arXiv:2611.17621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kernel optimization is essential for efficient large language model (LLM) training and inference on Ascend NPUs. Existing Ascend kernel benchmarks primarily focus on kernel generation, with less emphasis on the ability of agents to optimize existing implementations under input configurations drawn from real workloads. To address this requirement, we introduce AscendGYM, a benchmark whose initial suite comprises 48 kernels across three difficulty levels. Each kernel is paired with test cases whose data types and tensor shapes are collected from real-world training and inference tasks. sc82788cf56.summary: Researchers introduced AscendGYM, a benchmark of 48 kernels on Ascend NPUs testing whether agents can optimize existing kernels using real-workload input configurations.
sc82788cf56.why: Teams optimizing LLM workloads on Ascend hardware get a realistic benchmark for evaluating agent-driven kernel optimization.

sae9c0fa97d.title: Generated Evaluation Suites as Diversity-Driven Search for Real Agent Regressions
sae9c0fa97d.description: arXiv:2611.17632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating an evaluation suite from an agent's specification is diversity-driven search: a generator fills a descriptor space (requirements $\times$ personas $\times$ scenario kinds), and the suite it emits is an archive, then scored like a benchmark by its mean pass rate, which throws away the search's product. We inject 7 controlled defects into a $\tau^2$-bench agent across two domains. sae9c0fa97d.summary: A paper proposes treating generated evaluation suites for LLM agents as diversity-driven search, injecting controlled defects into a tau-squared-bench agent to test regression detection.
sae9c0fa97d.why: It suggests a better way to build agent regression suites than scoring them by mean pass rate, which discards search results.

s3651f26c3a.title: What LLM Agents See and What Users Say
s3651f26c3a.description: arXiv:2611.17639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Before an LLM agent cancels a reservation or deletes a folder for a user, what stops it from acting on a false assumption: what its tools show, or what the user says? In this work, we study this gap with presupposition theory from linguistics: an agent may act only if each claim behind the act (e.g., one reservation fits the name) is seen to hold, answered by the user, or disclosed while the act can be undone. A simple bound shows that when lookups cannot tell one record from two, any agent acts without asking first as often with two records as with one. s3651f26c3a.summary: A paper uses presupposition theory to study when LLM agents act on false assumptions about tool outputs versus user statements before cancelling reservations or deleting files.
s3651f26c3a.why: Agents taking irreversible actions need checks that verify tool-observed facts against user claims before acting, not after.

s644fcb9d3f.title: Learn then Bet: Learning Interpretable Rules for Reliable Agent Intervention
s644fcb9d3f.description: arXiv:2611.17662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agents now run for hundreds of steps with little or no human supervision. In practice, practitioners use runtime monitors such as turn limits and keyword filters to decide when a run should be stopped, upgraded, or assisted. However, these heuristics may stop runs that would otherwise succeed or allow failing runs to continue. To address this limitation, we introduce LeBet (Learn then Bet), a statistical learning framework that derives its learning objective from sufficient conditions for valid and powerful intervention. In particular, LeBet learns an interpretable OR-of-AND monitor and accumulates evidence through a fixed betting statistic, intervening when the evidence reaches a prescribed threshold. Under finite within-class exc
s644fcb9d3f.summary: Researchers introduce LeBet, a statistical framework that learns interpretable rules for deciding when to stop, upgrade, or assist long-running autonomous agents.
s644fcb9d3f.why: Replacing crude turn limits and keyword filters with learned intervention rules could reduce both wrongly stopped and wrongly continued agent runs.

s1e8698734e.title: Aligned, Conflicting, or Unspecified? A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multimodal Time Series Forecasting
s1e8698734e.description: arXiv:2611.17680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) systems increasingly combine sensed time series with external text such as expert reports and news, yet how reliably models use text that agrees or conflicts with the sensed history remains unclear. We introduce the first real-world diagnostic benchmark organized by text-history relationship: 1,762 text-window pairs across sensor telemetry (Weather), web-service traffic (Wikipedia), and market data streams (Finance), each labeled Aligned, Conflicting, or Unspecified by whether the text's direction agrees with the historical trend, opposes it, or is not stated. Across ten pretrained models evaluated zero-shot, we investigate text selection and combination under text-history relationships (RQ1) and error
s1e8698734e.summary: A benchmark of 1,762 text-window pairs tests how multimodal forecasting models use text that aligns, conflicts with, or is unrelated to sensed time series.
s1e8698734e.why: Shows whether forecasting models with text inputs actually weigh conflicting text reliably, which matters for AIoT deployments.

s1dd73289bc.title: OCTAVE: A Capability-Resolved Benchmark for End-to-End HTML5 Game Generation
s1dd73289bc.description: arXiv:2611.17681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complete game generation requires agents to coordinate rules, interactions, states, and presentation over a long development process. A single aggregate score obscures which capabilities are implemented and which requirements remain unmet. We present OCTAVE, a benchmark for complete HTML5 game generation organized around eight Capability Dimensions, with 180 tasks and 1,800 Evaluation Requirements drawn from real player requests, commercial-mechanics reconstruction, and human expert design. It covers PC Web, Mobile Web, 2D, and 3D. Requirements distinguish Completeness, assessing publicly specified core implementation, from Richness, assessing hidden, deeper system relationships. Static source-code judgments provide requirement-level diagnosi
s1dd73289bc.summary: OCTAVE is a benchmark of 180 tasks for end-to-end HTML5 game generation, scoring eight capability dimensions across PC Web, Mobile Web, 2D, and 3D.
s1dd73289bc.why: Capability-level scoring shows which parts of game generation agents implement and which requirements they miss, beyond one aggregate score.

sa52e770c3b.title: Co-Sight Harness: Externalized Control Assets and Deterministic Enforcement for Long-Horizon Business Agents
sa52e770c3b.description: arXiv:2611.17696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon business workflows fail in two ways: errors accumulate as a chain of activities lengthens, and the knowledge an activity needs is written in a different vocabulary from the user's request. We study whether such workflows can be made reliable without changing the language model. Our method keeps the backbone fixed and moves the workflow definition, state and domain knowledge into versioned control assets outside the model. A state machine and machine-checkable acceptance gates enforce these assets during execution; an independent auditor grades the resulting trace. The assets are updated only after a regression check and human approval .We evaluate the method on three deployed workflows exceeding 200 steps. On Domain A, a 120-case
sa52e770c3b.summary: Co-Sight Harness moves workflow definitions and domain knowledge into versioned control assets enforced by a state machine and acceptance gates, keeping the language model fixed.
sa52e770c3b.why: Externalizing workflow state and gates offers a way to make long business agent workflows more reliable without changing the model.

s941ec60473.title: An AI-enabled high-resolution chlorophyll-a forecasting model that outperforms the operational global biogeochemical system
s941ec60473.description: arXiv:2611.17704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface chlorophyll-a concentration is a key indicator of marine phytoplankton variability, and short-term forecasts of its distribution provide advance information for marine ecosystem monitoring and management. However, interactions between physical transport and biological processes complicate chlorophyll-a forecasting, and simulating these coupled processes with conventional numerical models imposes substantial computational demands. Here we introduce ChlCast, an AI model that generates daily forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a concentration over a 10-day horizon at approximately 4-km resolution between 60$^\circ$S and 60$^\circ$N. ChlCast combines factorized spatiotemporal convolutions with a multiscale architecture to learn from historic
s941ec60473.summary: ChlCast is an AI model that produces daily high-resolution forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a, reported to outperform the operational global biogeochemical system.

sa2f0c35054.title: Cross-Linguistic Acoustic Biomarkers of Cognitive Impairment Across Interactive and Single-Speaker Speech Tasks
sa2f0c35054.description: arXiv:2611.17710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multilingual dementia detection is essential for scalable and equitable screening. In recent years, automated speech analysis has emerged as a promising approach for supporting dementia detection by enabling non-invasive and scalable assessment of cognitive function. However, existing studies that use automated speech analysis often rely on one type of task, such as picture description, and use black-box models. These studies often neglect the role of task and language. To address these gaps, we performed a cross-linguistic and cross-task acoustic analysis that integrates a conversational dataset with structured speech tasks across four languages (Spanish, Mandarin, English, Japanese). We applied statistical, linguist-/clinician-guided, and m
sa2f0c35054.summary: A cross-linguistic study examines acoustic biomarkers for cognitive impairment across interactive and single-speaker speech tasks in multiple languages.

safaf656262.title: Federated Soft Poly-Level Learning Over a Distributed Network with Guaranteed Convergence
safaf656262.description: arXiv:2611.17722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-level learning/optimization, e.g., bilevel optimization, has been recognized for its versatile applicability across a broad array of domains, spanning from signal processing to machine learning. However, most existing works focus on bilevel and trilevel optimization. In contrast, multi-level optimization problems involving four or more hierarchical levels, which we term poly-level learning (PLL) problems, remain largely unexplored.In addition, in practical PLL, data may be distributed across multiple nodes over a distributed network. Nevertheless, extant studies on PLL predominantly focus on the non-federated setting, necessitating the collection of data to central servers and thereby posing potential privacy risks. To this end, we prop
safaf656262.summary: A paper proposes federated soft poly-level learning, extending multi-level optimization beyond bilevel and trilevel to four or more hierarchical levels over distributed networks, with convergence guarantees.
safaf656262.why: Offers theoretical convergence guarantees for hierarchical optimization across distributed nodes, though practical impact is still early.

s6978e7e6cc.title: A Spectral Framework for Universal Proxy Regularization in Model Merging
s6978e7e6cc.description: arXiv:2611.17728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model merging constructs multi-task models without expensive joint training but often suffers from parameter interference. Some solutions mitigate this by constraining finetuning using data from the other tasks to be merged, violating the core independence and privacy assumption of model merging. Recent work offers preliminary empirical evidence that a universal, task-agnostic proxy distribution can substitute for such data, but leaves open when and why it suffices. s6978e7e6cc.summary: A spectral framework is proposed for universal proxy regularization in model merging, aiming to replace task data with a task-agnostic proxy distribution to reduce parameter interference.
s6978e7e6cc.why: If a task-agnostic proxy suffices, model merging could avoid sharing other tasks' data, preserving the independence and privacy the method assumes.

scdb07f4f4a.title: Knowledge After Collapse: Context and Wording Shape Factual Accessibility in Language Models
scdb07f4f4a.description: arXiv:2611.17763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a language model accepts a false correction in a factual discussion, its next answer can depend on how the conversation continues. We introduce Knowledge Answer Divergence (KAD), an event-conditioned evaluation protocol that distinguishes initial false-answer adoption from subsequent persistence, recovery, and abstention. KAD freezes the conversation at the first explicit adoption of a designated false target and branches independent probes from that exact history. scdb07f4f4a.summary: Knowledge Answer Divergence, an evaluation protocol, tests how language models adopt, persist with, or recover from false corrections in factual conversations.
scdb07f4f4a.why: Shows that conversation history and wording can change whether models keep false answers, which affects reliability in multi-turn applications.

s5e6e51bb7c.title: Certified Improvements to Best-Known Thomson-Problem Configurations with a Search Pipeline Built with Large Language Model Agents
s5e6e51bb7c.description: arXiv:2611.17776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Thomson problem asks for N unit charges on a sphere with minimum Coulomb energy; for large N the best configurations known are curated in the Cambridge Cluster Database, whose largest-N entries were set in October 2026. We report configurations for N = 912, 1382 and 2502 with energies 0.0036186, 0.0109730 and 0.0614033 below the database values, certified by exact integer arithmetic. s5e6e51bb7c.summary: An LLM-agent search pipeline produced certified configurations for Thomson problem instances N=912, 1382 and 2502 with lower energies than Cambridge Cluster Database values.

s9b14e17bac.title: TReC: Evaluating Move-Induced State Changes in Instruction-Conditioned Go
s9b14e17bac.description: arXiv:2611.17781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a Go model predicts a move different from the expert's, coordinate distance measures how far the prediction lands from the reference. We introduce Transition Representation Consistency (TReC) to compare how the two moves change a board-state embedding. Both moves are executed from the same position under the game rules, and TReC is the cosine similarity between the two resulting representation changes. s9b14e17bac.summary: TReC, a metric, compares how a predicted Go move and the expert move change a board-state embedding in a frozen KataGo network, using cosine similarity over 680 positions.
s9b14e17bac.why: Offers a board-state-aware alternative to coordinate distance for evaluating game-playing model moves.

s71d70d1920.title: AutoRL: A Multi-Agent System towards Autonomous Reinforcement Learning
s71d70d1920.description: arXiv:2611.17790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is one of the most promising paths toward an AI singularity for superintelligence. Achieving this vision requires AI systems to undertake the full training pipeline for iterative improvement. Reinforcement learning (RL) plays an essential role in this cycle to improve model capabilities and generalization, yet automating RL remains difficult due to unstable training dynamics and the need for sustained supervision. We introduce AutoRL, a multi-agent system for automating RL training, as a cornerstone for future RSI. s71d70d1920.summary: Researchers introduce AutoRL, a multi-agent system designed to automate reinforcement learning training.
s71d70d1920.why: Automating RL training could reduce the manual supervision needed for stabilizing and iterating on model training pipelines.

s6ae5b51dd0.title: MASTARS: Multi-Agent Sequential Trajectory Augmentation with Return-Conditioned Subgoals
s6ae5b51dd0.description: arXiv:2611.17793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The performance of offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) is limited by the quality of the fixed offline dataset, motivating trajectory augmentation. However, augmenting multi-agent trajectories presents a fundamental challenge of the diversity-coordination trade-off: independent generation improves diversity but lacks coordination, while joint generation induces coordination but lacks diversity, reproducing the training distribution. s6ae5b51dd0.summary: Researchers present MASTARS, a diffusion-based method for augmenting offline multi-agent reinforcement learning trajectories while balancing diversity and coordination.
s6ae5b51dd0.why: It targets a known limit of offline multi-agent RL, where fixed datasets constrain performance, offering a data augmentation approach.

s6243dff041.title: Robustness Evaluation of GPU Cloud Pricing Benchmarks under Incomplete Observations: A Controlled Missingness Study
s6243dff041.description: arXiv:2611.17796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Daily GPU rental-price benchmarks can fail when marketplace quotes are missing. This article stress-tests a fixed equal-weight median rule under four imposed masking mechanisms and four benchmark-level recovery methods. Across 5,800 Monte Carlo realisations in 27 scenarios on 190 held-out days, whole-source outages reduce publication coverage to 0.77 while preserving zero conditional error on published dates; composition-changing loss retains 0.86 coverage but produces 7.74 log points of error. s6243dff041.summary: A study stress-tests a median-based GPU rental price benchmark under simulated missing marketplace quotes and evaluates recovery methods.
s6243dff041.why: Teams relying on GPU price indices should know how missing quotes affect coverage and error in published benchmarks.

s5051c90147.title: Vision-as-a-Tool: Visual Harness for Multimodal Agentic Coding
s5051c90147.description: arXiv:2611.17797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal agentic coding requires robust visual reasoning to analyze observations and evaluate generated artifacts. Current frameworks largely rely on a Thinking-with-Images paradigm, where agents depend on their intrinsic vision to execute visually grounded tasks. However, this architectural coupling introduces a fundamental bottleneck. Agent performance remains strictly bounded by internal perceptual limitations. Furthermore, text-only agents lack native perception. Without specialized tools, they cannot perform visual reasoning. To overcome these constraints, we introduce the Vision-as-a-Tool (VaaT) paradigm. Prior visual tool-use merely manipulates images for an agent's intrinsic vision to read. s5051c90147.summary: Researchers propose Vision-as-a-Tool, a framework that gives text-only coding agents visual perception through external tools rather than relying on the model's own vision.
s5051c90147.why: Decoupling perception into tools could help agentic coding systems evaluate generated UI artifacts beyond the base model's vision limits.

s8ea1455284.title: Can Agents Keep Up with Time? An Empirical Analysis of Temporal Adaptation After a Conversational Hiatus
s8ea1455284.description: arXiv:2611.17806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon agents increasingly serve as persistent personal assistants across modern web platforms, managing schedules, applications, and multi-step plans over weeks or months. Users often return to an ongoing conversation after a long conversational hiatus, while earlier bookings and preparation notes stay on record. During this hiatus, scheduled dates may pass even though the retained records remain unchanged and event outcomes go unrecorded. Existing evaluations of long-horizon agents focus on fact retention and explicit state updates. Whether agents perceive the passage of time and adapt their advice accordingly therefore remains unknown. We frame this ability as temporal state perception and use, which means perceiving the current time
s8ea1455284.summary: An empirical study examines whether long-horizon agents adapt to time passing during a conversational hiatus, when scheduled events lapse but records stay unchanged.
s8ea1455284.why: Persistent assistants that act on stale state after time gaps could make wrong scheduling decisions, so evaluations need time-awareness.

s4a5a2ec223.title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands
s4a5a2ec223.description: arXiv:2611.17814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), an increasing number of users are turning to LLM-powered agents for conversational shopping in e-commerce. However, the user needs continue to change as new product categories, procurement scenarios, and feature requests emerge. At the same time, the product's execution harness-including its tools, skills, and operating procedures-continues to evolve to support increasingly sophisticated interactions. s4a5a2ec223.summary: Researchers propose G-CAST, a governed continual self-training approach for LLM shopping agents facing shifting user demands and evolving tools.
s4a5a2ec223.why: Production agents whose tools and user needs change over time need governed retraining to avoid drift; the text gives limited detail on results.

sad8f20c1a1.title: Causally Constrained and Uncertainty-Aware Cardiopulmonary Risk Prediction
sad8f20c1a1.description: arXiv:2611.17819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Routine chest computed tomography (CT) captures pulmonary, cardiac, and vascular phenotypes that jointly stratify lung cancer and cardiovascular disease, the two leading causes of death in lung-screening populations. Yet clinical risk calculators evaluate each disease in isolation and omit CT findings, whereas unconstrained machine learning overfits small hospital cohorts, learns treatment- and illness-confounded risk directions, and conceals uncertainty when patient records are incomplete. sad8f20c1a1.summary: Researchers present CE-Agent, a causally constrained, uncertainty-aware model that predicts lung cancer and cardiovascular risk from routine chest CT.
sad8f20c1a1.why: Combining CT findings across diseases with uncertainty estimates targets clinical risk tools that currently evaluate each disease separately.

s6a1d2d99b3.title: Aligning AI Teams
s6a1d2d99b3.description: arXiv:2611.17820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. s6a1d2d99b3.summary: Researchers investigate why safety alignment on individual LLM agents fails to transfer to multi-agent teams and test interventions to preserve it.
s6a1d2d99b3.why: Single-agent safety testing may not carry over to multi-agent deployments, so teams should evaluate safety at the team level.

s46fc01c9e4.title: Is Abliteration Getting Harder? Not Uniformly: Refusal Removal by Direction-Based Ablation and ARA in Heretic on the Qwen3.8, Gemma 4, Olmo 3.1 and Mistral Small 3.2 LLMs Versus Their Predecessors
s46fc01c9e4.description: arXiv:2611.17846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Abliteration, a fine-tuning-free weight edit, removes refusal from open-weight large language models (LLMs). s46fc01c9e4.summary: A study tests whether direction-based abliteration and ARA can still remove refusal from newer open-weight LLMs compared with their predecessors.
s46fc01c9e4.why: Results show refusal removal is not uniformly getting harder, relevant for teams assessing safety robustness of open-weight model releases.

s227be0f675.title: DECODE: Diagnosing Interpretability Failures in Automated Interpretation Process
s227be0f675.description: arXiv:2611.17856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tools for interpreting the internal representations of Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly rely on LLMs themselves to both generate and evaluate explanations, creating a self-referential automated interpretation process with minimal human oversight. This automation raises significant reliability concerns, which are exacerbated by the absence of ground truth. In practice, it is difficult to validate explanations or to attribute interpretability failures to their source -- whether they originate from the tool's extracted representations or from the LLM used in the process. s227be0f675.summary: Researchers present DECODE, a method for diagnosing whether failures in LLM-based automated interpretability stem from extracted representations or from explanation generation.
s227be0f675.why: Self-referential LLM interpretation pipelines without ground truth raise reliability concerns that engineers evaluating such tools need to diagnose.

s66da9e3b2f.title: AI-aided Decision-Making in Education - Uncertainty, Explainability, and Human Responsibility
s66da9e3b2f.description: arXiv:2611.17858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based systems have become increasingly integrated into various aspects of everyday life, including education, understanding how these systems make decisions is of paramount importance. AI holds significant potential to enhance educational practices through the facilitation of personalized and adaptive learning, automation of assessment procedures, and assistance with administrative tasks. However, the opacity of AI-based decision-making in education (especially with deep learning and generative AI models) can hamper decision-making, especially when outcomes appear unjustified or incorrect. s66da9e3b2f.summary: A paper examines how AI-aided decision-making in education raises issues of uncertainty, explainability, and human responsibility.

s945d9dd613.title: FlexCast: Flexible Context Learning for Time Series Foundation Models
s945d9dd613.description: arXiv:2611.17862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) based on autoregressive (AR) next-token prediction entangle two factors: variable-context conditioning and prediction-unit factorization with autoregressive rollout. We propose FlexCast, a flexible context-target learning framework that disentangles these factors. FlexCast reformulates forecasting as variable-length masked prediction over time series patches: during pretraining, it dynamically samples visible context and masked target patches, exposing the model to diverse context-target configurations
s945d9dd613.summary: Researchers propose FlexCast, a time series foundation model framework that separates variable-context conditioning from autoregressive prediction to clarify sources of generalization.
s945d9dd613.why: Disentangling training and inference factors could guide design choices for time series forecasting models.

s1cf1844e5e.title: OmniScore-Bench: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Musical Score Reading
s1cf1844e5e.description: arXiv:2611.17870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer questions about musical scores, but their ability to recognise notation, recover its structure and interpret its musical meaning requires separate evaluation. Existing optical music recognition (OMR) resources establish detection and transcription measurements; a transcription score alone leaves the strengths and bottlenecks of a VLM score reader unresolved. We introduce OmniScore-Bench, an evaluation of OMR capabilities in VLMs through 3,000 questions spanning six aspects and 24 task subtypes. Each question specifies a visible scope, reference annotations and an answer schema, enabling automatic evaluation from symbol localisation to musical consistency and evidence-linked question answering. Our asse
s1cf1844e5e.summary: Researchers introduce OmniScore-Bench, a benchmark of 3,000 questions testing vision-language models on musical score reading across six aspects.
s1cf1844e5e.why: It separates recognition, structure, and meaning in VLM score reading, showing where models fail beyond transcription accuracy.

s2b05f37313.title: Soteria: Formally Verified Planning with Runtime Enforcement for Safe LLM Agents
s2b05f37313.description: arXiv:2611.17880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents that execute multi-step tool calls must satisfy two objectives simultaneously: completing the user's task (utility) and conforming to domain policies and correctness constraints (safety). These objectives are in tension -- blocking an unsafe action prevents a violation but can leave the agent stranded with no principled way to recover. Existing approaches sacrifice one objective for the other. We introduce Soteria, a framework that reconciles safety and utility through verified hierarchical planning and runtime enforcement of specifications. s2b05f37313.summary: Researchers introduce Soteria, a framework combining formally verified hierarchical planning with runtime enforcement to balance task completion and safety for LLM agents.
s2b05f37313.why: It addresses the tension where blocking unsafe tool calls can strand agents, offering a way to keep both utility and policy compliance.

s0f50ae43d6.title: Adversarially Attacking Symbolic Vocabulary Vulnerabilities In LLM Planners
s0f50ae43d6.description: arXiv:2611.17910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents, their abilities in navigating automated planning tasks have become essential. However, despite their strengths, LLMs' planning ability is not robust, particularly when they are not allowed to exploit commonsense cues in the symbolic vocabulary (e.g., names of actions, predicates, and objects) used to define planning tasks. This makes LLMs unreliable compared to symbolic planners. With recent reasoning models showing improved planning performance on tasks with obfuscated symbolic vocabularies, we utilize an adversarial attack framework to reveal to what extent the crucial weaknesses of LLM agents at joint symbolic interpretation and planning remain and whether they
s0f50ae43d6.summary: Researchers show adversarial changes to symbolic vocabulary can expose weaknesses in LLM planners that lack commonsense cues.
s0f50ae43d6.why: LLM planners that depend on naming cues may be unreliable under obfuscated task definitions, which matters for agent deployments.

s314482901f.title: SWIFT: Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning of Time-Series Foundation Models for Forecasting
s314482901f.description: arXiv:2611.17915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While current few-shot adaptation strategies for time series forecasting foundation models are predominantly dataset-centric, the necessity of obtaining an additional dataset for the finetuning process poses a significant hurdle for adoption. To address this constraint, we propose Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning (SWIFT), a novel forecasting adaptation framework that achieves fine-grained specialization by leveraging structural priors from the target instance's own history. This shift allows the fine-tuning process to be entirely transparent to the end-user, which significantly enhances the ease of adoption. s314482901f.summary: SWIFT proposes sample-wise instance fine-tuning that adapts time-series forecasting foundation models using each target instance's own history, without needing an extra dataset.
s314482901f.why: It removes the need for an additional fine-tuning dataset, a practical hurdle for adopting forecasting foundation models.

s0cd4573f42.title: When Cooperation Must Change: Semantic Strategy Unlearning in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
s0cd4573f42.description: arXiv:2611.17917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) supports coordinated decision-making in distributed Web services, multi-robot control, and collaborative games through learned coordination conventions. When deployment requirements change, a previously useful convention may become obsolete or unsafe. For example, revised cache-sharing permissions in Web content delivery may require caches to abandon a learned division of storage and serving roles while maintaining efficient delivery. Teams must therefore remove the specified convention while preserving useful cooperation. This is challenging because the same relational pattern can be reproduced by different agents across different histories. Runtime shielding leaves the underlying coordin
s0cd4573f42.summary: Researchers propose semantic strategy unlearning for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, so teams can drop a learned coordination convention when deployment requirements change.
s0cd4573f42.why: Learned multi-agent conventions can become obsolete or unsafe after requirement changes, and this offers a way to remove them.

sfff7d19619.title: RecMem: Recurrent Memory Compression for Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation
sfff7d19619.description: arXiv:2611.17921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative recommendation benefits from long interaction histories, but the cost of processing them directly grows with history length. We propose RecMem, a recurrent memory compression framework guided by three desiderata: space invariance, semantic fidelity, and lifelong evolvability. RecMem compresses historical segments into a fixed set of memory slots using a bifurcated encoder-decoder with shared lower layers and slot-wise forget-gated updates. sfff7d19619.summary: RecMem compresses long user interaction histories into fixed memory slots using recurrent memory, aiming to make generative recommendation over long sequences cheaper.
sfff7d19619.why: Processing cost in generative recommenders grows with history length, so fixed-size memory compression could cut serving costs.

sa0a9244e62.title: What Balanced Accuracy Cannot Identify in Neural-Signal Decoding under Test-Time Adaptation
sa0a9244e62.description: arXiv:2611.17925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptation for neural-signal classification is usually transductive: each batch is scored after updating on it, and the gain depends on the adapted model [4]. This paper asks what an aggregate change fails to characterise inside the cohort. Full test-time adaptation (full_ttt) was evaluated in 11 dataset-encoder cells (four each on Siena/EEG and PTB-XL/ECG, three on Sleep-EDF/EEG), with splits and source-model evaluation fixed; the subject was the unit, exact sign tests were Holm-corrected and conditional on the shared stream, and bootstrap intervals accompanied a dependence audit. Two results of different kinds follow. In the binary case balanced accuracy gives a one-class decoder the same value as one reporting both classes at 50%, so the a
sa0a9244e62.summary: A paper examines how balanced accuracy and aggregate metrics can miss subject-level effects when test-time adaptation is applied to neural-signal decoding across EEG and ECG datasets.
sa0a9244e62.why: Aggregate metrics can hide per-subject behavior changes, which matters when evaluating adaptive models on medical signal data.

sd9646e5b1b.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Scientific Paper Search: Retrieval Success and Inference Latency on Mac Studio and NVIDIA A100
sd9646e5b1b.description: arXiv:2611.17929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific literature search can benefit from locally deployed LLM assistants, which reduce reliance on hosted model providers while giving research teams greater control over their data and infrastructure. This work investigates whether open-weight models can support web-assisted paper retrieval under practical computing constraints. We first characterize inference latency as the input context grows from 512 to 128k tokens on a Mac Studio and a server equipped with two NVIDIA A100 GPUs. We then evaluate eight models on the retrieval of 70 papers from seven scientific repositories, using queries that represent three levels of domain knowledge. The results show that retrieval success depends strongly on the selected model and the specificity o
sd9646e5b1b.summary: The study measures latency and paper-retrieval success for eight open-weight LLMs on a Mac Studio and a two-A100 server, with context lengths up to 128k tokens.
sd9646e5b1b.why: It gives concrete latency and retrieval tradeoffs for running local LLM research assistants instead of hosted APIs.

scfd93a0534.title: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
scfd93a0534.description: arXiv:2611.17933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In many long-horizon settings, an agent's own choices create future constraints: committing finite capacity establishes future obligations and forecloses later opportunities. Sustaining performance therefore requires both keeping evolving plans feasible and comparing the value of resource allocations with the alternatives they displace. Recent benchmarks increasingly evaluate LLM agents in continuing operations, but give less attention to how agents keep their own commitments feasible while reassessing resource allocations as opportunities change. We introduce OutfitterBench, where agents manage an outdoor-equipment rental business for 200 days, purchasing from a 46-product catalog and handling roughly 1,100 reservation requests. Under a fixe
scfd93a0534.summary: OutfitterBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on long-horizon resource allocation and keeping their own commitments feasible as opportunities change.
scfd93a0534.why: It targets agent failures in sustained operations, such as overcommitting capacity, that short-horizon benchmarks miss.

s3907b6ae38.title: Tracing Actual Causes with Counterfactual Witness Maps
s3907b6ae38.description: arXiv:2611.17937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Halpernian actual causation, the formal study of which events in a specific situation caused a specific outcome in acyclic structural causal models, underpins legal responsibility, moral blame, and the assessment of causal harm. Despite the rich logical framework, no prior sound and complete enumeration procedure is known for finding all actual causes in a given setting, blocking downstream tasks such as responsibility attribution, blame assessment, and causal-harm grading that aggregate over the full cause set. We close this gap by introducing witness targets: sets of joint configurations containing every counterfactual witness. s3907b6ae38.summary: The paper introduces counterfactual witness maps, a sound and complete enumeration procedure for finding all Halpernian actual causes in acyclic structural causal models.
s3907b6ae38.why: Complete cause enumeration is a prerequisite for downstream responsibility and blame assessment, though the work is theoretical.

se05dbc4d35.title: Measured from the feed: the unsustainable growth of AI video generation
se05dbc4d35.description: arXiv:2611.17938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-video generation runs at commercial scale, but its broader environmental impacts remain, to our knowledge, understudied. Providers rarely disclose video volumes or energy needs; we measured the yearly video output of two commercial platforms and built a prospective model of such services' absolute footprint from training to storage. Our projections suggest that reducing emissions depends on both limiting growth in video generation and achieving substantial efficiency gains. Under continued growth, emissions rise nearly seventy-five-fold by 2030 despite technological improvements. se05dbc4d35.summary: The authors measured yearly video output of two commercial text-to-video platforms and project that emissions could rise nearly seventy-five-fold under continued growth.
se05dbc4d35.why: Engineering and leadership teams deploying generative video should weigh energy growth against efficiency gains.

s6cb799c6ee.title: Toward Interference-Agnostic RF Source Separation
s6cb799c6ee.description: arXiv:2611.17950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Separating a radio-frequency signal of interest from a co-channel interference is mostly addressed with specialized separators, each trained for one pair of signal and interference types and therefore relying on a label that a heavily jammed receiver cannot identify. We show that this reliance is not benign: applied to an interference it was not trained on, such a separator usually fails to recover the signal, and in most of the cases we measure it leaves the signal worse than no processing at all. We then train a single separator over every pair, giving it no indication at test time of which one it faces, on two architectures with no component in common: the convolutional WaveNet of the ICASSP 2024 RF Challenge, and a band-split transformer
s6cb799c6ee.summary: Researchers train a single RF source separator across many signal and interference pairs, rather than one specialized separator per pair, to handle unseen interference.
s6cb799c6ee.why: Specialized separators often fail on unseen interference, so a generalist separator addresses a real limitation for jammed receivers.

s08476d33ae.title: The Transformer Paradigm: Dynamic Processing and a New Principle of Inference
s08476d33ae.description: arXiv:2611.17953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We argue that the Transformer revolution is not adequately understood as a merely quantitative expansion of deep learning, but as the emergence of a new paradigm based on a different principle of inference. We interpret the Transformer as a system in which token representations are transformed by parameterized transformations, or transforming concepts. During inference, some of these transformations are dynamically constructed from the current input: previously acquired transformations are first adapted and then applied. At the mechanical-structural level, this dynamic processing is realized through output-weight interconnections, whereby outputs of some networks determine the weights of others. The resulting mode of processing, which we call
s08476d33ae.summary: A theoretical paper argues the Transformer represents a new inference paradigm in which some transformations are dynamically constructed from the current input.

s7e9a74ca3f.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
s7e9a74ca3f.description: arXiv:2611.17955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents powered by large language and vision-language models are increasingly applied to realistic browser work that spans heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows. However, existing reproducible web-agent benchmarks cover only a small number of web applications drawn from a few software categories, and restrict modality to text and vision. Live benchmarks broaden site coverage but sacrifice reproducibility, since pages and data drift between runs. Moreover, existing benchmarks do not meaningfully evaluate whether agents can understand and use audio and video content embedded within web tasks. To address these gaps, we introduce WebArena-Pro, a benchmark comprising 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applicati
s7e9a74ca3f.summary: WebArena-Pro is a reproducible benchmark for web agents spanning more heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows than prior benchmarks.
s7e9a74ca3f.why: Broader and reproducible web-agent evaluation helps teams compare agents on realistic multi-app browser work.

s2085e6546a.title: TotalSegmentator Aorta Report: Automated Aortic Diameter Measurement at 11 Standardized Landmarks on CT Images
s2085e6546a.description: arXiv:2611.17968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose: To develop and evaluate a fully automated, open-source tool that measures aortic diameters at 11 standardized landmarks from the aortic annulus to the bifurcation on any CT image, following current guideline recommendations. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 239 arterial phase CT angiography examinations of 230 patients (median age, 65 years [range, 18-99 years]; 163 men) performed between April 2025 and October 2026 (209 electrocardiographically [ECG] gated). The tool locates landmarks from TotalSegmentator segmentations of aortic branches and vertebrae and measures the maximum diameter at each. A senior radiologist reviewed and, where needed, corrected the automated measurements to create the re
s2085e6546a.summary: An open-source tool automatically measures aortic diameters at 11 standardized landmarks on CT angiography, evaluated on 239 examinations from a single center.
s2085e6546a.why: An open-source automated measurement tool could standardize aortic reporting in clinical imaging pipelines.

sc677cf2b3d.title: Interactive deep-learning based interface for brain tumour segmentation
sc677cf2b3d.description: arXiv:2611.17983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Brain tumour segmentation from MR images is an integral part of their treatment, either through surgical resection or radiotherapy. Both applications require a high degree of precision that can be difficult to ensure for all patients due to the high degree of variability in the size, shape, number, and location of these tumours. This leads to difficulties with their automatic segmentation via deep learning, which can display catastrophic segmentation errors when presented with images that differ, even subtly, in terms of the specific MR sequence used, which varies from vendor to vendor. This article presents a deep-learning-based interactive segmentation system that, while being fully automatic by default, has the capability of being easily c
sc677cf2b3d.summary: An interactive deep-learning interface for brain tumour segmentation from MR images is presented, aimed at reducing catastrophic errors on varied MR sequences.

s7e61a7e121.title: LACCO: Local Accumulation with Computation--Communication Overlap
s7e61a7e121.description: arXiv:2611.17991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training language models across low-bandwidth networks requires reducing synchronization overhead. Local optimization methods such as DiLoCo communicate only after several local steps, but outer gradient averaging and the outer update remain on the critical path. Existing computation-communication overlap methods avoid this stall through delayed or replica-local updates, which can degrade convergence or cause replicas to drift. s7e61a7e121.summary: LACCO is a two-stage algorithm that overlaps global gradient communication with computation for training language models over low-bandwidth networks.
s7e61a7e121.why: Reducing synchronization stalls in low-bandwidth distributed training could lower cost for teams training across slow networks.

s414ab39890.title: Understanding the limits of snapshot-based fault diagnosis in distribution networks
s414ab39890.description: arXiv:2611.17998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverter-based resources weaken fault currents in distribution networks, and snapshot-based diagnosis, which classifies a fault from voltage phasors at a few buses at one instant, offers a cheap first-stage screen. Its published accuracies, however, rest on different noise assumptions and do not show whether the error comes from the classifier, the features, the measurement error, or the fault resistance. s414ab39890.summary: The paper separates error sources in snapshot-based fault diagnosis on distribution networks, testing three IEEE feeders and a public dataset with distributed generation.
s414ab39890.why: Shows which factors limit fault classifier accuracy, informing when cheap snapshot-based screening can be trusted in grid operations.

s7b82a6cbf6.title: A$^3$: Adaptive Audio Agent Framework for Collaborative Edge Computing
s7b82a6cbf6.description: arXiv:2611.18064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embedded audio agents need a nearby edge server for speed, but a server-dependent agent returns nothing when the link fails. We present A$^3$, an adaptive audio agent framework that places whole pipeline stages on the server, keeps a complete fallback agent on devices that can host one, and hedges both paths with a link-aware deadline that decides when to give up on the server. On Jetson devices and an RTX A4500 server, A$^3$ matches the server-only agent on a healthy link, answers every request in a full outage on the AGX, and beats a percentile hedge in simulated outages.
s7b82a6cbf6.summary: Researchers propose A$^3$, an adaptive audio agent framework that splits pipeline stages between edge devices and a server, with a complete on-device fallback.
s7b82a6cbf6.why: It shows how to keep embedded voice agents responsive and working during network outages, relevant to edge AI system design.

sb44bf45e50.title: Two-Clustering Regime of Token Dynamics in Causal Attention
sb44bf45e50.description: arXiv:2611.18088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We partially resolve Conjecture 1 of [Karagodin et al., Clustering in Causal Attention Masking (NeurIPS 2024)] and extend it to time-dependent parameter regimes. The conjecture predicts that causal attention dynamics converge to two clusters aligned with the eigenvectors associated with the largest eigenvalue $\lambda_{\max}$ of the value transformation. We prove that this behavior holds when $\lambda_{\max}>0$ and is generally false when $\lambda_{\max}\le0$. sb44bf45e50.summary: A paper proves that causal attention token dynamics converge to two clusters when the largest eigenvalue of the value transformation is positive, and shows the conjecture fails otherwise.

s5bebf121cc.title: Do Machines Learn Deviance From Their Peers? A Randomized Test of Differential Association With AI Agents
s5bebf121cc.description: arXiv:2611.18098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differential association theory and its extension, social learning theory, hold that rule-breaking, and the definitions that make it acceptable, are learned through interaction with others. Because people choose their friends, this claim has been hard to test. We addressed this selection problem with AI agents, which learn only through communication and can be assigned to peers at random. In a preregistered experiment, 420 teams of three agents (1,260 agents; seven AI models) worked on coding tasks that could not be solved honestly. A scripted teammate said that it had cheated (deviant peer), that it had reported the problem honestly (honest peer), or said nothing (silent peer). s5bebf121cc.summary: A preregistered experiment with 420 teams of three AI agents tested whether agents learn rule-breaking behavior from peers via randomized assignment.

s17441cda69.title: Optimizing Drilling Trajectories in Multi-Material Structures Using Quantum Annealers
s17441cda69.description: arXiv:2611.18121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we present a quantum-hybrid optimization approach for planning drilling trajectories on multi-material structures, with the objective of minimizing total energy consumption. The proposed formulation models the drilling process as a constrained routing problem in which each hole must be visited while accounting for heterogeneous material properties, material-dependent drilling costs and displacement energy, as well as tool-wear penalties. Our method incorporates realistic industrial constraints, including open-path routing and mandatory grouping of holes belonging to the same material to avoid frequent tool-bit changes. s17441cda69.summary: Researchers present a quantum-hybrid optimization approach for planning drilling trajectories on multi-material structures to minimize total energy consumption.

s87a0c17225.title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
s87a0c17225.description: arXiv:2611.18130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to finance, creating a need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities across financial systems with different regulations and practices. However, existing financial benchmarks provide limited coverage of country-specific financial systems, and they are difficult to keep up to date as released questions leak into training data. We introduce JFinBench, a Japanese financial benchmark comprising 321 examples from the 2026 editions of six regularly administered certification exams covering accounting, tax, financial planning, and banking. s87a0c17225.summary: JFinBench is introduced as a Japanese financial benchmark of 321 examples from 2026 certification exams, designed to be continuously refreshed.
s87a0c17225.why: Engineers evaluating LLMs for finance in Japan get a country-specific, regularly updatable test set that reduces training-data leakage risk.

sb29cabb887.title: Large Language Model-Empowered Intelligent Agent for Adaptive Fast-Charging Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries
sb29cabb887.description: arXiv:2611.18140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is a multi-objective control problem that requires reducing charging time and sustaining high energy throughput while suppressing accelerated degradation and safety-critical electrochemical reactions. Conventional protocols are easy to implement but have limited ability to adapt to variations in battery chemistry, operating conditions, and aging state. Model-based optimization and conventional data-driven control often require accurate models, costly iterative search, or task-specific policies. sb29cabb887.summary: Researchers develop a large language model-based intelligent agent for adaptive fast-charging control of lithium-ion batteries.

s6b1fb627dd.title: Probabilities of Causation in Nondeterministic Causal Models
s6b1fb627dd.description: arXiv:2611.18245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study probabilities of causation in nondeterministic causal models, where mechanisms may remain intrinsically stochastic even after all latent variables are fixed. Focusing on binary treatments and outcomes, we develop a generic identification program that represents observational and interventional data as moment constraints on latent stochastic mechanism types and computes minimal/maximal values of counterfactual quantities via constrained optimization. s6b1fb627dd.summary: The paper derives sharp analytic bounds on probabilities of causation in nondeterministic causal models with binary treatments and outcomes.

s3e38f9f5d4.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation
s3e38f9f5d4.description: arXiv:2611.18248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, yet how a particular generation relates to the geometry learned in pre-training remains unclear. The fundamental explainability of LLMs is elusive. Here, we build a similarity network from the input embeddings of six open LLMs and map generation onto it. s3e38f9f5d4.summary: Researchers map LLM token generation onto a similarity network built from input embeddings of six open LLMs, finding a scale-free but fragmented topology.

sc8e7bfccd8.title: When evaluation becomes intervention in clinical AI
sc8e7bfccd8.description: arXiv:2611.18297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI judges, models that grade another system's output against a rubric, extend clinical review to the scale at which clinical AI writes. When teams use judge assessments to select a prompt or train a model, the judge becomes part of the intervention. Selection can then favor errors the judge overlooks. We describe what a judge's report must contain and the independent clinical test each judge-driven change needs.
sc8e7bfccd8.summary: The article argues that using AI judges to select prompts or train clinical AI models turns evaluation into intervention, and calls for independent clinical testing.
sc8e7bfccd8.why: Teams using LLM-as-judge to tune clinical systems risk optimizing for errors the judge misses, so independent validation is needed.

s935711d9b1.title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
s935711d9b1.description: arXiv:2611.18315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web platforms record user and item activity in relational databases whose schemas differ from platform to platform, which makes it difficult to transfer predictive models between them. Relational foundation models address this through cross-database pretraining, yet recent improvements have relied on increasingly large pretraining corpora. We ask whether a better architecture, together with features specific to the target database, can deliver comparable gains from far less pretraining data. s935711d9b1.summary: The paper introduces MoREGT, a mixture-of-relational-experts model for cross-database generalization that aims to match gains from large pretraining with less data.

s896bd046e0.title: Causal AI-Driven Secure mmWave Beam Alignment with Defensive Variational Autoencoders
s896bd046e0.description: arXiv:2611.18321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient and secure beam alignment is essential for mmWave communication systems. However, existing deep learning (DL)-based beam alignment methods often neglect causal relationships between inputs and outputs, resulting in limited interpretability, poor generalization, and excessive beam sweeping. Moreover, these DL solutions are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, where small perturbations in received power measurements can mislead beam classifiers. s896bd046e0.summary: Researchers propose a causally-aware deep learning framework with defensive variational autoencoders for secure mmWave beam alignment resistant to adversarial perturbations.

sfeee23b9a7.title: VLAN: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation
sfeee23b9a7.description: arXiv:2611.18346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accessible mobility is user-conditioned rather than scene-intrinsic, as walkable paths for one embodiment are inaccessible to another. Yet, existing benchmarks evaluate traversability under a fixed and limited embodiment. We present Vision-Language Accessible Navigation (VLAN), containing 1,000 scenes, 20K navigation trajectories, and 160K keyframes across diverse lighting, environmental conditions, scene semantics, and path geometries. sfeee23b9a7.summary: VLAN is a vision-language navigation benchmark with 1,000 scenes and 20K trajectories, providing embodiment-specific accessibility labels for legged and wheeled robots.

sfa2ff8e70f.title: VelServe: Taming Decode Jitters in LLM Inference with Tail-Calibrated Scheduling
sfa2ff8e70f.description: arXiv:2611.18392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive LLM services must meet latency service-level objectives (SLOs) for the time to first token (TTFT) and the time between tokens (TBT), as streaming and soft real-time applications require predictable token delivery. In aggregated serving, SLO-aware schedulers set each step's prefill budget until its predicted latency just meets the TBT target, leaving no room for mispredictions or host stalls. sfa2ff8e70f.summary: VelServe proposes tail-calibrated scheduling to reduce decode jitter in LLM inference and meet time-between-tokens latency SLOs in serving systems.
sfa2ff8e70f.why: Decode jitter causes many SLO violations in long streaming responses, so tail-aware scheduling directly affects serving reliability.

saac4fe7a77.title: Smart Home Agents Make Capable but Unpredictable Grid Operators
saac4fe7a77.description: arXiv:2611.18395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-enabled smart homes are becoming more common across the grid edge. However, there has not been much work on failure response. This area is critical because smart homes operate on the grid edge where failures can cascade down. If a power outage happens within a smart home, a user has to manually troubleshoot their smart home to include tasks such as power load balance and device recovery. We conduct the first resilience analysis of smart home agents across a full power outage, providing a suite of outage simulations in a live environment that measures resilience before, during, and post power outage. We show that smart home agents can act as grid operators in power outages and identify several new failure categories highlighting the current
saac4fe7a77.summary: A resilience analysis of smart home agents across simulated full power outages finds they are capable but behave unpredictably as grid operators.

saec85571de.title: LECAT: Measuring LLM Category Learning from Pretraining Data
saec85571de.description: arXiv:2611.18419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humans know that airplanes are fast, that this extends to red airplanes, but that it does not hold for broken airplanes. How do LLMs acquire category knowledge that humans learn and apply effortlessly? We introduce LeCat, a two-part framework to analyze LLM's Learning of Category knowledge. First, we use LeCat to evaluate models on their ability to learn category knowledge, distinguishing between three cases: memorization of in-domain category knowledge, generalization to unseen instances, and ability to flexibly use knowledge in appropriate contexts. Then, we use LeCat to trace how this knowledge can be learned in pretraining from text that may encode category knowledge in various ways, such as verbatim repetition or exceptions, which we ref
saec85571de.summary: LeCat is a two-part framework that measures how LLMs learn category knowledge from pretraining data, covering memorization, generalization, and flexible use.

se1d605aef1.title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram
se1d605aef1.description: arXiv:2611.18434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated sleep staging has achieved strong bench- mark accuracy; however, clinical adoption remains limited due to a lack of interpretability. In this work, we fill the research gap by extending the SleepXAI sleep staging framework to systematically compare five different XAI methods. Further, attribution fidelity is evaluated using Spearman rank correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands, serving as clinically grounded reference signals. In this paper, we focus on single- channel Electroencephalogram (EEG), which is more amenable to practical clinical deployment compared to full polysomnography setups. Experiments are conducted on the Sleep-EDF benchmark dataset and the DREAMT dataset. In DREAMT, we stratified subjects based on OSA i
se1d605aef1.summary: Researchers extend the SleepXAI framework to compare five explainability methods for single-channel EEG sleep staging, checking attributions against AASM frequency bands.
se1d605aef1.why: Interpretable sleep staging could ease clinical adoption of automated models, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s0effe99313.title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support
s0effe99313.description: arXiv:2611.18458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals. We introduce Support-Gated World-Model decision support, a lightweight extension of a propose--simulate--refine agent. A recurrent dynamics ensemble predicts short-horizon physiological responses to documented norepinephrine dose categories, while a behavior model estimates observational action support. The interface withholds predictions with insufficient support or excessive ensemble disagreement and abstains when no candidate qualifies. s0effe99313.summary: Researchers propose Support-Gated World-Model decision support, which withholds simulated patient responses to vasopressor doses when the data gives insufficient support.
s0effe99313.why: It shows a way for LLM agents to flag unreliable simulations in high-stakes settings instead of acting on them unchecked.

s83c5ff0c11.title: Typing Matters: Muscle, Language and Typing Behaviour in Live Keystroke Decoding from sEMG
s83c5ff0c11.description: arXiv:2611.18464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) from the wrists can recover typed text without a keyboard. It is usually posed as a signal-inference problem: characters are read out of the muscle signal and character error rate is reported offline. We argue that this framing removes most of the problem. The decoder is constrained simultaneously by the muscles, by the language being typed, and by typing behaviour such as typos, corrections, backspaces and line breaks, and a usable system must predict keys live while the hand keeps moving. s83c5ff0c11.summary: Researchers frame wrist sEMG keystroke decoding as a live problem constrained by muscle signals, language, and typing behaviour, not only offline character error rate.
s83c5ff0c11.why: Treating typing behaviour and language as constraints may matter for building usable real-time neural input interfaces.

sa5b6601e31.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
sa5b6601e31.description: arXiv:2611.18494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small language models are attractive for local, low-cost, and privacy-sensitive deployment, but they remain unreliable on mathematical reasoning tasks that require decomposition, exact computation, tool use, and verification. We introduce \textbf{ARCHER}: \textbf{A}ction-trace \textbf{R}einforcement for \textbf{C}alculator-grounded \textbf{H}ierarchical \textbf{E}xecutable \textbf{R}easoning, a two-stage framework for training small language models (SLMs) to produce executable and auditable reasoning trajectories. In the first stage, ARCHER compiles free-form chain-of-thought rationales into typed action traces containing reasoning steps, calculator calls, deterministic runtime observations, verification actions, and final answers. This shift
sa5b6601e31.summary: ARCHER is a two-stage training framework that teaches small language models to produce executable, calculator-grounded reasoning traces for math tasks.
sa5b6601e31.why: Executable, auditable reasoning could make small local models more reliable for math-heavy tasks where privacy or cost rules out large hosted models.

s661c8f9be9.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
s661c8f9be9.description: arXiv:2611.18514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinati
s661c8f9be9.summary: A case study applies mechanistic interpretability to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to explain why web agents hallucinate actions unavailable on a live website.
s661c8f9be9.why: It tests whether interpretability tools can diagnose real agent failures, a gap engineers debugging web agents would care about.

s33873f048a.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
s33873f048a.description: arXiv:2611.18531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise
s33873f048a.summary: A theoretical study models how evolutionary selection shapes AI agents' tradeoffs between task completion and rules of conduct, and whether experience aligns choices with human judgments.
s33873f048a.why: The text is theoretical and gives little concrete guidance for engineers building agents today.

s1c7b50d396.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
s1c7b50d396.description: arXiv:2611.18533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly relies on a harness, the scaffold around the model that decides what it sees of its own interaction and what guidance it receives. Most existing approaches train under a hand-written harness that stays fixed throughout. However, an effective harness depends on the domain, the data and the model, and keeps changing as the model trains. We introduce ModHarness-RL, which recasts the harness as programs that are learned from data and evolve as the model trains with RL. s1c7b50d396.summary: ModHarness-RL treats the agent harness, the scaffold deciding what the model sees and receives, as learnable programs that evolve during agentic reinforcement learning.
s1c7b50d396.why: Learned, evolving harnesses could replace hand-written scaffolds that stay fixed during agent RL training.

s8e1f110b13.title: HARDTESTGEN: A High-Quality RL Verifier Generation Pipeline for LLM Algorithmic Coding
s8e1f110b13.description: arXiv:2505.24098v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Verifiers provide important reward signals for reinforcement learning of large language models (LLMs). However, it is challenging to develop or create reliable verifiers, especially for code generation tasks. A well-disguised wrong solution program may only be detected by carefully human-written edge cases that are difficult to synthesize automatically. To address this issue, we propose HARDTESTGEN, an approach to synthesize high-quality test cases for algorithmic coding problems. We curate a comprehensive algorithmic programming dataset HARDTESTS with 26.6k problems and high-quality synthetic tests. s8e1f110b13.summary: HARDTESTGEN is a pipeline that synthesizes high-quality test cases to build reliable reward verifiers for reinforcement learning on algorithmic coding problems.
s8e1f110b13.why: Stronger verifiers reduce reward hacking from wrong code that passes weak tests, which matters for training code-generation models.

s794963e7ea.title: PhysDox: Benchmarking LLMs on Physical Feasibility Auditing of Physiological Sensing Protocols
s794963e7ea.description: arXiv:2606.05003v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly assist in experimental design, yet fluent protocols often remain physically infeasible. We introduce PhysDox, a physical feasibility auditing benchmark for biomedical protocols comprising a 683-sample expert-curated Gold set and a 5,000-sample Silver set across six sensing domains. We formulate the task as a two-stage evaluation: severity detection classifying protocols as valid, minor, or fatal, followed by the constraint-level diagnosis of fatal violations. s794963e7ea.summary: PhysDox is a benchmark testing whether LLMs can audit physiological sensing protocols for physical feasibility, classifying severity and diagnosing fatal constraint violations.
s794963e7ea.why: It shows LLM-generated experimental protocols can be fluent yet physically infeasible, a risk for teams using LLMs in lab design.

sf838d531d9.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Sequence Models for Sample-Efficient Energy Regression in Simulated Calorimeter Showers
sf838d531d9.description: arXiv:2611.17354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Energy reconstruction from electromagnetic calorimeter data underpins particle identification, event reconstruction and precision measurements in high-energy physics. Machine learning already performs well on this task, yet two questions remain open: how much the choice of data representation matters, and whether hybrid quantum-classical models add value in practice. We compare classical and quantum-enhanced models for incident positron energy reconstruction on the CaloGAN dataset, a public benchmark of 100,000 simulated electromagnetic shower events spanning 1 to 100 GeV. Eight architectures, namely SVR, ANN, CNN and LSTM together with their quantum counterparts, are trained on three calorimeter representations: engineered physical feature
sf838d531d9.summary: Researchers compare classical and hybrid quantum-classical sequence models for positron energy regression on the public CaloGAN calorimeter shower dataset.
sf838d531d9.why: The text gives limited detail on outcomes, so its practical relevance to most engineering teams is unclear.

s9ea55d4ab9.title: ProdPilot: A Layered Model Context Protocol System for Automated Production Readiness and Deployment of Vibe-Coded Projects
s9ea55d4ab9.description: arXiv:2611.17381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-assisted development environments turn natural-language requests into working applications, yet the projects they produce often fail on their first deployment for operational reasons: credentials in source files, missing security middleware, no container definition, no health endpoint and no delivery pipeline. Automated repair of such defects usually relies on free-form model generation, which varies between runs and is seldom checked independently. This paper presents ProdPilot, a local Model Context Protocol server that audits Node.js and React projects against 50 production readiness rules, repairs violations through a bounded loop, gates the result and deploys it. Each rule is classified by what its fix requires: 28 fixes are fixed t
s9ea55d4ab9.summary: ProdPilot is a local Model Context Protocol server that audits Node.js and related vibe-coded projects for production readiness issues like hardcoded credentials and missing health endpoints.
s9ea55d4ab9.why: Automated checks for deployment defects in AI-generated apps address a common failure point when prototypes first reach production.

s6545e0a14a.title: Time-Consistent Evaluation of Hierarchical Code Graphs for SWE Agents
s6545e0a14a.description: arXiv:2611.17388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating repository-aware software engineering (SWE) agents requires strict separation between pre-existing repository knowledge and future code evolution, yet standard benchmarks frequently suffer from temporal contamination and prompt-level solution leakage. Building on the time-consistent benchmark protocol of Sun (2026), we enforce strict zero-leakage isolation across DragonFly in C++ and React in JavaScript/TypeScript, locking repository snapshots and knowledge graphs at historical cutoff commits $T_0$ and evaluating 100 post-$T_0$ pull requests across four prompt granularities: Minimal, Concise, Contextual, and Guided. s6545e0a14a.summary: The paper evaluates repository-aware software engineering agents on DragonFly and React using repository snapshots and knowledge graphs locked at historical commits to prevent leakage.
s6545e0a14a.why: Zero-leakage evaluation protocols give a more trustworthy measure of coding agent performance than standard contaminated benchmarks.

sb64241c89f.title: Enumerating Posterior-Supported Priors: First-Order Error of Finite-Integral Cross-Categorical Measurement Morphisms
sb64241c89f.description: arXiv:2611.17390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In generative modeling, standard measure theory adopts the a.e. convention, which legitimately ignores any error component carried by a null-support set: a single null element can hide out-of-domain error inside null support and never be explicitly accounted for. The contribution of this paper is not a new distributional distance, but rather a verifiable structure that writes down which underlying predicate supports a high-level object, when it is invertible, and at which layer the error resides, from which we propose the enumerating posterior-supported prior framework.
