sb64241c89f.summary: The paper proposes a verifiable structure for specifying which predicate supports a high-level object in generative modeling, and bounds error in null-support regions.
sb64241c89f.why: The text is highly theoretical and offers little direct relevance to most engineering or leadership decisions.

s51745506b2.title: Confident and Wrong: Structure Confidence Is a Poor Selection Filter for Protein Function
s51745506b2.description: arXiv:2611.17391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Structure-guided protein design can generate plausible candidates, but structural confidence does not predict function. We trained a function-guided model on measured metal-binding affinity with protein sequence, ligand identity, and assay conditions, and used it to design rare earth element (REE) binding variants of lanmodulin, a lanthanide-binding protein with four EF-hand domains. s51745506b2.summary: Researchers designed lanmodulin variants for rare earth element binding and found that structural confidence did not predict measured metal-binding function across 297 designs.
s51745506b2.why: Structural confidence scores alone are a poor selection filter, so function-guided screening is needed in protein design pipelines.

sb4d5556a3f.title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming
sb4d5556a3f.description: arXiv:2611.17395v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in weight-space programming (WSP) have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can directly inspect and modify neural network weights without conventional gradient-based training. While this capability opens new possibilities for model improvement, it also raises an important security question: Can LLMs exploit weight-space programming to inject backdoors into neural networks? To answer this question, we present an empirical security study of LLM-driven weight-space programming for backdoor injection. sb4d5556a3f.summary: An empirical study tests whether LLMs can use weight-space programming to inject backdoors into neural networks by directly modifying their weights.
sb4d5556a3f.why: LLMs that can edit model weights create a new supply-chain security risk that teams deploying third-party models should account for.

sa3c4846598.title: WETW: Learning Pair-Specific Weighted Euclidean Distances for Efficient DTW Search
sa3c4846598.description: arXiv:2611.17412v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is the standard distance for similarity search over time series that are misaligned in time, but its cost is quadratic in the series length and lower bounds often prune few candidates, so search over large collections of long series is slow. Learned approximations embed the series to make comparisons cheap, yet compare every pair with the same fixed rule, usually the Euclidean distance, although DTW aligns each pair differently. sa3c4846598.summary: Researchers propose WETW, a method that learns pair-specific weighted Euclidean distances to approximate Dynamic Time Warping for faster similarity search over long time series.
sa3c4846598.why: Offers a potentially cheaper alternative to quadratic-cost DTW for searching large collections of misaligned time series.

s01fe63811c.title: Interpreting Coding Agents Through Their Behavioral Trajectories
s01fe63811c.description: arXiv:2611.17440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard coding-agent benchmarks primarily evaluate binary task success, treating execution as a black box and obscuring the behaviors that produce those outcomes. We analyze a large corpus of 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 agent configurations spanning 117 unique models. To enable comparisons across heterogeneous agent interfaces, we develop a rule-based parser that maps raw execution traces to high-level actions such as repository search, file editing, and test execution, and audit its predictions against a six-model consensus reference on 500 events. s01fe63811c.summary: Researchers analyzed 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 coding-agent configurations, using a rule-based parser to map traces to high-level actions beyond binary task success.
s01fe63811c.why: Suggests benchmarks that score only pass/fail hide behaviors behind agent outcomes, which matters when evaluating coding agents.

s4cf91bc8ca.title: Racing the Clock: Teaching VLNs Budget-Conditioned Object Search
s4cf91bc8ca.description: arXiv:2611.17442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A rescue robot entering a building with thirty seconds on the clock should sprint toward the single most promising room; given ten minutes, it should instead explore a broader tour. Yet vision-language-navigation (VLN) models are typically evaluated under a fixed episode limit that the policy never observes, even though time-critical missions require behavior to adapt to the available budget. We study budget-conditioned object search: given a target category and an explicit action budget, an agent must find as many distinct target instances as possible before the budget expires. We investigate how to supervise VLNs for this task by comparing a privileged TSP expert, which plans near-optimal routes using the full map and true target location
s4cf91bc8ca.summary: Researchers study budget-conditioned object search for vision-language-navigation agents, where the agent is given an explicit action budget and must find as many target instances as possible.

s6883673636.title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models
s6883673636.description: arXiv:2611.17462v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion-based generative models have become strong priors over plausible crystal structures, but turning that prior into promising candidates requires steering toward several conflicting properties at once. Fine-tuning is expensive and produces a new model for every new objective, while differentiable guidance is not applicable to many real-world tasks. We instead adapt these generative models at inference time using Diffusion Tree Sampling (DTS), a Monte Carlo tree search procedure over the denoising trajectory. s6883673636.summary: Researchers introduce Diffusion Tree Sampling, a Monte Carlo tree search over the denoising trajectory, to steer crystal generative models toward multiple properties at inference time.
s6883673636.why: Offers a way to adapt pretrained generative models to new objectives without fine-tuning a new model for each one.

s2851b3aa8f.title: Use-case-driven ontology modeling with the NeOn methodology for ambient assisted living
s2851b3aa8f.description: arXiv:2611.17466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Research on smart homes and ambient assisted living (AAL) has grown steadily over the last decade, driven largely by the ageing of the population. A smart home has to coordinate heterogeneous smart objects in order to offer services tailored to its dwellers, and this requires a shared formal description of both the dwellers and the devices. We present the ontology developed as the semantic data layer of the Virtual Home Framework in the Italian Design For All project. Its requirements are derived from two use cases: a frail elderly woman who exercises at home on a cycle-ergometer, and a designer who configures a kitchen for users with different impairments. The requirements are collected in an Ontology Requirements Specification Document an
s2851b3aa8f.summary: Researchers present an ontology built with the NeOn methodology as the semantic data layer of the Virtual Home Framework for ambient assisted living in smart homes.

s5bd6a6e24b.title: Do Mixture-of-Experts Routers Benefit from Ensembling?
s5bd6a6e24b.description: arXiv:2611.17472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ensembles of neural networks have repeatedly been shown to outperform single networks. Ensemble theory attributes this gain to the accuracy of the individual members and the diversity among them. Mixture-of-experts models already combine many experts, but a single router decides how the experts are weighted for each input. Motivated by ensemble theory, we apply ensembling to the routing step: an ensemble of routers, trained jointly with the experts, proposes the expert weights. s5bd6a6e24b.summary: Researchers evaluate applying ensembling to the routing step of mixture-of-experts models, using an ensemble of routers trained jointly with the experts to propose expert weights.
s5bd6a6e24b.why: Explores whether ensemble gains transfer to MoE routing, a design choice relevant to building sparse models.

s17d0cbb725.title: Adversarial Tracking: Attacks on Image Sensors for Object Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles
s17d0cbb725.description: arXiv:2611.17505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Object tracking systems estimate the motion of surrounding vehicles by linking detected objects across video frames. In particular, Tracking-By-Detection (TBD) systems combine object detectors with motion prediction and data association to maintain object identities over time. However, neural network-based detectors are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that perturb input images, and their impact on downstream trajectory estimation is not fully characterized by detection accuracy alone. Therefore, this paper evaluates image-specific and image-agnostic attacks on YOLOv3 and YOLOv4 detectors paired with SORT, Deep SORT, Strong SORT, and OC-SORT tracking systems. s17d0cbb725.summary: Researchers evaluate image-specific and image-agnostic adversarial attacks on detectors in tracking-by-detection systems, measuring their effect on vehicle trajectory estimation in autonomous driving.
s17d0cbb725.why: Shows detection accuracy alone does not capture how adversarial image perturbations degrade downstream tracking in autonomous vehicles.

s30407b76c2.title: Only as Safe as the Weakest Agent: A Break That Appears Only When the System Is Multi-Agent
s30407b76c2.description: arXiv:2611.17520v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Major industry multi-agent systems like Codex and Claude Code can be broken by attacks that have long been unsuccessful against modern frontier models. AI Safety as a discipline has largely focused on finding the bounds and vulnerabilities of AI models used in isolation. Yet as humans increasingly deploy these models as agents and multi-agent systems, the same attacks that had been thought to be patched when using a model in isolation can break these same models under specific circumstances. s30407b76c2.why: Indicates per-model safety testing may miss vulnerabilities that only emerge when models operate as part of multi-agent systems.

s7793a77614.title: GraphScent: Calibrating Directional Relevance Signals for Bounded-Context Code Localization
s7793a77614.description: arXiv:2611.17527v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Running open-weight language models locally on a single consumer GPU requires replacing expanding multi-turn exploration histories with short, stateless code inspections. s7793a77614.summary: Researchers study directional relevance signals for code localization with Gemma 4 models on 211 Python issues, aiming to run stateless repository localization on a single consumer GPU.
s7793a77614.why: Points toward practical local coding assistants that avoid long multi-turn exploration histories on consumer hardware.

sa2074f6ada.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Target-Centric Causal Discovery in Industrial Processes
sa2074f6ada.description: arXiv:2611.17556v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Causal discovery promises to find which recorded variables drive a process target such as product quality, yield or energy use. Process data with known causes are rare, and in existing benchmarks the difficulty of identifying the causes of a target is either fixed by the recorded data or set for the whole graph. We present a synthetic benchmark for target-centric causal discovery in industrial processes. Its generator is a two-level structural causal model inspired by batch production, assembled from components that each model one phenomenon of process data, such as a control loop or a delayed effect. sa2074f6ada.summary: Researchers present a synthetic benchmark for target-centric causal discovery in industrial processes, built from a two-level structural causal model inspired by batch production.

s05d9464cb7.title: Benchmarks Don't Talk Back: Learning Through Self-Disagreement
s05d9464cb7.description: arXiv:2611.17563v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A benchmark usually measures a language model alone with a question, and deployment rarely looks like that: answers get contested, and models give up correct ones under counter-reasoning that is itself wrong. It stands on first-answer accuracy without following from it: a model can be made materially better at answering and no better at this, and training for accuracy alone can drift against it. s05d9464cb7.summary: Researchers define dialectical competence, the ability of a language model to hold a correct position under contested answers and yield only to better reasoning, and show it differs from accuracy.
s05d9464cb7.why: Highlights that first-answer accuracy does not measure whether models resist wrong pushback, a gap relevant to deployed assistants.

s1f8a603a7f.title: Rethinking Visual Reasoning in Text-to-Image Reward Modeling
s1f8a603a7f.description: arXiv:2611.17585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reward models are a core component of modern text-to-image systems, serving as the objective for inference-time selection and RL-based post-training. Even when starting from strong vision-language backbones, preference fine-tuning erodes these capabilities, and continual-learning baselines fail to mitigate a steep tradeoff between visual reasoning and preference accuracy. We propose a data-centric intervention that injects visual reasoning supervision into preference le
s1f8a603a7f.summary: Researchers find that widely used text-to-image reward models perform poorly on targeted visual reasoning tests, and that preference fine-tuning can erode these capabilities.
s1f8a603a7f.why: Suggests reward models used for selection and RL post-training may fail on attribute binding, relations and counting, affecting image pipelines.

sd9d1144a64.title: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot
sd9d1144a64.description: arXiv:2611.17598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon navigation from indoors to outdoors remains an open problem for humanoid robots: one instruction covers rooms, doors and roads, and the camera moves with the gait. Worken, AGIBOT's measure of productive robot work, depends on robots that reach their workplaces autonomously. We present X-Nav, to our knowledge the first system to take a bipedal humanoid through a language-instructed long-horizon mission from indoors to outdoors. X-Nav covers a pipeline from data to deployment. Its data engine collects navigation data in open-source scenes, in digital twins of deployment sites and on real robots. Its navigation model, MELIOR, takes only RGB images from the robot's built-in camera and comes in two versions: MELIOR-A predicts action
sd9d1144a64.summary: AGIBOT presents X-Nav, a system that takes a bipedal humanoid robot through a language-instructed long-horizon navigation mission from indoors to outdoors.
sd9d1144a64.why: Demonstrates end-to-end data-to-deployment navigation on a humanoid, a benchmark for embodied robotics engineering.

s4ed2f8dfd7.title: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View 3D Transformers via Regime-Aware Attention Approximation
s4ed2f8dfd7.description: arXiv:2611.17629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-view 3D transformers such as VGGT reconstruct a scene from a set of unposed images in a single forward pass, predicting camera poses, depth and 3D points, but the cost of their global attention grows quadratically with the num- ber of images. Accelerators borrowed from large language models assume that each token attends to only a few oth- ers; on these models they lose accuracy or gain little speed. We study the global attention of three multi-view transform- ers on seven datasets and find that every layer plays one of three roles: it averages over the whole scene, matches points across many images, or anchors on the first image, whose coordinates the outputs use. Building on this anal- ysis, we propose Regime-AWare ATTention Approxi
s4ed2f8dfd7.summary: Researchers propose a training-free acceleration for multi-view 3D transformers like VGGT by approximating global attention differently per layer role, based on analysis across seven datasets.
s4ed2f8dfd7.why: Offers a no-retraining speedup for quadratic attention cost in multi-image 3D reconstruction models.

sdbdfdcb294.title: CoTTAGE: An Explainable Judge for Text-to-Audio Generation
sdbdfdcb294.description: arXiv:2611.17644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rapid progress in text-to-audio (TTA) generation demands reliable and explainable automatic evaluation. However, existing metrics fail to simultaneously deliver high correlation with human judgments and meaningful, audio-grounded explanations, forcing reliance on labor-intensive human evaluation that bottlenecks model development iteration. To address this, we propose CoTTAGE, a reasoning-based evaluator for text relevance (REL) and audio quality (OVL). Following a reason-then-predict paradigm, CoTTAGE first generates an audio-grounded rationale to diagnose errors before predicting scores. Supported by over 10K newly collected human OVL annotations, CoTTAGE is first trained via supervised fine-tuning and then refined with reinforcement lear
sdbdfdcb294.summary: Researchers introduce CoTTAGE, a reasoning-based evaluator that generates audio-grounded rationales before scoring text relevance and audio quality for text-to-audio generation.
sdbdfdcb294.why: Provides an explainable automatic judge that could reduce reliance on slow human evaluation when iterating on audio models.

s95d5d308e5.title: Binarization as an Attack Surface in Weightless Neural Networks
s95d5d308e5.description: arXiv:2611.17646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weightless Neural Networks (WNNs) are lightweight classifiers that binarize their inputs and learn by storing binary patterns in lookup memories, which makes them attractive for resource-constrained tasks such as intrusion detection. Because a small perturbation that crosses no binarization threshold leaves the binary input unchanged, WNNs may appear naturally robust to adversarial examples; a perturbation that does cross a threshold, however, can still change the prediction. We study this tension in WiSARD, the canonical RAM-based WNN, and in two variants that replace its memories with Bloom filters, Bloom WiSARD and BTHOWeN. A continuous perturbation reaches these classifiers only by crossing an encoding threshold, changing at least one b
s95d5d308e5.summary: Researchers study whether Weightless Neural Networks, such as WiSARD, are robust to adversarial examples, finding that binarization thresholds can still let perturbations change predictions.
s95d5d308e5.why: Engineers deploying lightweight classifiers for intrusion detection should not assume binarization alone provides adversarial robustness.

sd01d525796.title: Imitation Policies Learn a Proprioceptive Anchor: A Predictive Law for Perception Noise and Its Closed Loop Cost
sd01d525796.description: arXiv:2611.17658v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Imitation policies for robot manipulation are often trained on noisy object positions, and they learn to discount the noisy reading. We show how much they discount it, and why. Because demonstrators steer toward the object, the robot's own state carries information about where the object is. A trained policy combines this proprioceptive anchor with the reading and weights the reading by $\alpha = V/(V + s^2)$, where $s^2$ is the reading noise and $V$ the anchor's error variance. $V$ belongs to the learner and is far smaller than a linear model of the demonstrations implies, which is why classical errors-in-variables (EIV) regression overestimates $\alpha$. sd01d525796.summary: Researchers show imitation policies for robot manipulation learn to discount noisy object-position readings by blending them with the robot's proprioceptive state, and give a predictive formula for this weighting.
sd01d525796.why: Teams training robot policies on noisy perception can use this law to predict how much policies rely on sensor readings versus proprioception.

sc66c370adb.title: Agent-written heuristics versus commercial solvers on unsolved job-shop benchmark instances
sc66c370adb.description: arXiv:2611.17682v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Commercial solvers are the standard tool for difficult scheduling problems. We study whether a frontier large language model, used as a coding agent with open-source tools only, can match them in quality and speed. We report every run, and independent checkers verify every schedule. On the 100,000-operation job shop tai_100_1000_1, an agent-written solver reached 525,515, below OptalCP, Hexaly, and CP Optimizer. Unchanged, it improved all ten instances of the family and closed two. With equal budgets on the same workstation, it ended 0.0-1.8% above the lower bound, against 2.6-5.8% for CP Optimizer and 2.4-4.4% for Hexaly. On the Behnke-Geiger flexible job shops, an agent-written tabu search improved 11 of 32 open instances. With two transp
sc66c370adb.summary: An LLM used as a coding agent with open-source tools wrote a job-shop scheduling solver that was compared against commercial solvers on large unsolved benchmark instances.
sc66c370adb.why: It shows agent-written heuristics can approach commercial optimization solvers on hard scheduling problems, though the reported solver still trailed the commercial ones on the headline instance.

s4213fdacbc.title: Logically Consistent Accurate Forecasts
s4213fdacbc.description: arXiv:2611.17735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic forecasting systems based on large language models (LLMs) are now competitive with expert human forecasters, but these systems still suffer from a critical limitation: the inability to produce forecasts that are logically consistent. For example, forecasts for related events often fail to satisfy the axioms of probability, which in turn implies that related forecasts cannot simultaneously be correct and undermines their utility for decision makers. Enforcing consistency is not trivial -- naive approaches (e.g., projection onto the set of consistent forecasts) can degrade accuracy. We argue that the key to overcoming the apparent tradeoff between consistency and accuracy lies in the reasoning which supports each forecast. We finetune
s4213fdacbc.summary: Researchers present a method for making LLM-based agentic forecasting systems produce logically consistent forecasts that satisfy probability axioms across related events.
s4213fdacbc.why: Forecasts for related events that contradict each other undermine decision-making, so consistency enforcement matters for anyone using LLM forecasts operationally.

sf21872f6d4.title: Superfluid: Local AI Server for Distributed LLM Inference
sf21872f6d4.description: arXiv:2611.17753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Running large language models (LLMs) on local devices keeps data private, removes per-token cost, cuts network latency, and keeps working without a connection. Two shifts now strain how such models are served. On one device, several agents share a locally served model with an interactive user. Across devices, a developer or small team often owns several capable machines from different vendors, which sit idle most of the day because every local server serves one runtime on one machine. We present Superfluid, an open-source LLM server built for local inference at both scales. On one device, Superfluid drives llama.cpp, MLX, or BaseRT in isolated worker processes through one scheduler that moves interactive requests ahead of agent work, comput
sf21872f6d4.summary: Superfluid, an open-source local LLM server, is presented for distributing inference across several machines from different vendors and serving multiple agents on one device.
sf21872f6d4.why: Developers with several idle local machines could pool them to serve models privately without per-token cost.

sa62157b736.title: Creative Product Design under Brand Image Constraints
sa62157b736.description: arXiv:2611.17762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Industrial design requires creative visual exploration while satisfying constraints that are often product-specific and implicit. Existing text-to-image (T2I) approaches can generate creative designs through concept blending or multi-agent self-enhancement, but they provide limited mechanisms for ensuring that generated designs remain consistent with such constraints. We focus on brand image as a representative design constraint and propose a framework for brand-aware redesign generation. Given a product name, the framework constructs a brand image survey report that summarizes product and market information, derives a creative direction from the report, and integrates this direction into a self-enhancement loop in which generated images ar
sa62157b736.summary: Researchers propose a framework for brand-aware product redesign generation that uses a constructed brand image to keep text-to-image designs consistent with brand constraints.

sab059b9991.title: GDP.xlsx: Benchmarking Frontier Models on Professional Workbooks
sab059b9991.description: arXiv:2611.17766v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce GDP_xlsx, a benchmark of 70 realistic workplace requests written by professionals in 13 domains, each paired with an expert rubric of binary criteria and with the complete workbook or CSV file it refers to. Together the files hold 2.18 million populated cells, and the rubrics 791 criteria. Agents work in a container with spreadsheet tools, and an agentic judge that can open the file applies the rubric. Completeness and exclusivity criteria require set-valued answers to be found in full and with nothing extra. We rank models by strict pass@1, the share of attempts that meet every criterion. Across 20 model configurations, including frontier models from Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI, the top-scoring one, Gemini 4 Argon, passes on
sab059b9991.summary: GDP_xlsx is a benchmark of 70 professional workplace spreadsheet requests across 13 domains, scored with expert rubrics and an agentic judge that opens the workbook.
sab059b9991.why: It gives teams a rubric-based way to compare frontier models and agents on realistic spreadsheet tasks.

s4417e466d7.title: Activation Steering the Nan-Shan in Typhoon
s4417e466d7.description: arXiv:2611.17768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Typhoon is an audiovisual installation based on Joseph Conrad's novella, in which Captain MacWhirr steers the steamer Nan-Shan directly into and through a catastrophic storm. The novella is a study of what happens when the scale of a phenomenon exceeds the practical and conceptual frameworks available to comprehend it and of the paralysis that sometimes follows a demand for action in such overwhelming circumstances. We chose the text of Typhoon to reflect on human culture's current AI moment. We prompt a large language model, seeded with Conrad's original language, to feed endlessly on its own output, and explore when and how the text becomes increasingly alien and unwieldy as time progresses, including deviations from the narrative, digres
s4417e466d7.summary: Typhoon is an audiovisual art installation that prompts an LLM seeded with Joseph Conrad's novella to reflect on the current AI moment, using activation steering.

sa02f43225e.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
sa02f43225e.description: arXiv:2611.17780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier LLM agents that query databases with tools are among the most accurate text-to-SQL systems, but per-query calls to a hosted model are slow, costly, and expose sensitive organizational queries to external APIs. For example, a Claude Opus 5.5 agent serving 10,000 queries a day costs over $70,000 a year at list price. To what extent can local hardware already owned by an organization offload this burden without compromising the agent's accuracy? We present LuthorSQL, a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model that serves as a rapid System 1 gate for a slower LLM agent (System 2), escalating queries only when uncertain. LuthorSQL makes a single forward pass to predict slot scores over a bounded grammar for query plans, compiles and runs
sa02f43225e.summary: LuthorSQL is a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model proposed as a fast first-pass system that could run on local hardware ahead of a slower LLM agent.
sa02f43225e.why: Offloading routine queries to local models could cut API costs and keep sensitive organizational queries off external APIs.

s4fe0fb5e4e.title: Towards Seconds-level Video Representation: Quadratically Gated Feature Grid with Adaptive, Prediction-free Sampling
s4fe0fb5e4e.description: arXiv:2611.17786v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Implicit neural video representations are notoriously slow to build, which does not cross the basic practical threshold for most industrial applications. Here, we present Q-GAS, a coordinate-queryable video representation that couples multi-resolution explicit 3D feature grids with a compact SwiGLU-style quadratic-gating (QG) decoder and an error-aware, prediction-free sampler. The explicit grids avoid hash-collision coefficient sharing at the cost of modestly higher storage yet greatly boost the expressive capacity; the QG decoder introduces low-rank local second-order interactions to improve the nonlinear feature response. During fitting, a global error map periodically refreshes a high-error pool, and each batch mixes pool samples with u
s4fe0fb5e4e.summary: Q-GAS is a coordinate-queryable implicit video representation using 3D feature grids, a quadratic-gating decoder, and a prediction-free sampler to speed up building video representations.
s4fe0fb5e4e.why: Faster construction of implicit video representations could make them practical for industrial video applications.

s4c301d9d24.title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection
s4c301d9d24.description: arXiv:2611.17789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Direct weight editing offers a gradient-free alternative to fine-tuning pretrained detectors, but its generalization and the value of large language model (LLM) guidance remain uncertain. We evaluate five experimental phases using YOLO26 models and MS COCO, comparing deterministic scaling, random perturbations, differential evolution, CMA-ES, structured interventions, real local-LLM proposals, failure-aware guidance, and hybrid LLM-CMA-ES against a matched random-policy control. Optimization uses native Ultralytics mAP50-95 on 1,000 COCO Val2017 images; selected candidates are assessed on a disjoint, previously examined 1,500-image subset, with COCO API AP50-95 reported separately where available. Increasing the CMA-ES budget from 8 to 250
s4c301d9d24.summary: A multi-phase study evaluates whether LLMs can optimize pretrained YOLO26 detector weights gradient-free, comparing them against evolutionary methods and a random-policy control on COCO.
s4c301d9d24.why: Results indicate whether LLM guidance adds value over standard search for weight editing of detectors, a question teams weighing that approach need answered.

s5b8d19f052.title: Multimodal Person Concept Model for Person Identification under Varying Observation Conditions
s5b8d19f052.description: arXiv:2611.17802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Service robots in domestic and office environments must identify users to provide personalized services based on their preferences and previous interactions. This is challenging because only a few observations may be available for learning, while observation conditions change owing to appearance, environmental noise, and utterance content. To address this challenge, this study proposes a multimodal person concept model that learns person concepts from a small number of observations, without person labels, and enables robust identification under changing conditions. s5b8d19f052.summary: A multimodal person concept model is proposed that learns person identities from few observations without person labels, for robust identification by service robots under varying conditions.

s3a41667f7d.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
s3a41667f7d.description: arXiv:2611.17808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents can coordinate tools and applications to complete complex, multi-step tasks. As their interaction histories grow, effective context management becomes essential for reliable and efficient execution. Existing methods reduce context through summarization, pruning, or history selection. However, shorter contexts do not necessarily support better decisions: summaries can omit exact details needed for later actions, while retaining entire interactions can carry substantial irrelevant information. We propose CarryOn, a lightweight context manager that pairs compact execution state with fine-grained, source-linked evidence. s3a41667f7d.summary: CarryOn is a lightweight method that learns which parts of an agent's interaction history to keep in context for long-horizon LLM agent tasks.
s3a41667f7d.why: Better context selection addresses the tradeoff between summaries that drop needed details and full histories that add noise in long agent runs.

s1841b522f4.title: SceneAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Portable Game Scene Generation
s1841b522f4.description: arXiv:2611.17821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Moving a scene generator to a new game engine requires more than exporting its final output: planning, construction tools, and stored experience may also depend on the original backend. We present SceneAgent, a multi-agent framework for reusing the construction process and its experience across backends. A canonical SceneContext maintains the evolving world, while backend adapters isolate coordinate conventions, asset bindings, and export. Structured handoffs let fresh Builder sessions query this persistent state without inheriting the full construction transcript. Across generations, human-approved traces are distilled into asset-ID-free Layout skills and semantic Content skills that can be retrieved and recombined. We introduce GameSceneB
s1841b522f4.summary: SceneAgent is a multi-agent framework that reuses scene-generation construction processes and experience across different game engine backends via a canonical scene context and backend adapters.
s1841b522f4.why: Separating world state from engine-specific adapters could reduce rework when moving generation pipelines between game engines.

sc2855811f1.title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
sc2855811f1.description: arXiv:2611.17831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance. sc2855811f1.summary: V-JEPA-LM is a video-language model approach aimed at letting language models use the dynamics captured by V-JEPA video encoders rather than only retrieving static, caption-aligned attributes.
sc2855811f1.why: It highlights that video-LM training can leave useful encoder dynamics unused, relevant to teams building video question-answering systems.

saa13de8acd.title: Tracing Uncertainties of Extreme El Ni\~{n}o Prediction to Mesoscale Ocean Currents
saa13de8acd.description: arXiv:2611.17854v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The predictability of the El Ni\~{n}o-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) has historically been linked to large-scale errors in models' initial conditions such as heat content and surface wind stress. Here we demonstrate that these slowly evolving errors may ultimately originate from mesoscale errors in initial oceanic states that are common in current models and ocean observation systems. This hidden source of ENSO forecast uncertainty, in terms of mesoscale ocean-current errors, is convincingly exposed by the conditional nonlinear optimal perturbation (CNOP) method applied to a differentiable ocean AI model. saa13de8acd.summary: Researchers argue that errors in El Niño forecasts may originate from mesoscale errors in initial ocean-current states common to current models and observation systems.
saa13de8acd.why: It shows that small-scale initial-condition errors in ocean data can propagate into large-scale climate forecast uncertainty, relevant to anyone building or validating forecasting pipelines.

sd1d95f8ffb.title: Active Learning of Temporal Specifications through Distinguishing Queries
sd1d95f8ffb.description: arXiv:2611.17866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Temporal specifications are essential for verification and monitoring, yet writing formulas that capture the intended behaviour is difficult. Active learning derives such specifications through interaction between a learner and a teacher, but remains underexplored for temporal logics. Existing approaches require the teacher to answer equivalence queries and to construct counterexamples, and they often rely on SAT-based learning procedures that restart the search after each new example. sd1d95f8ffb.summary: Researchers present an active-learning framework for LTLf that learns temporal logic specifications through learner-teacher interaction, aiming to avoid equivalence queries and restarted SAT searches.
sd1d95f8ffb.why: Automatically learning temporal specifications could reduce the effort of writing verification and monitoring formulas, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sd886d447d5.title: UltraBERT-JEV: Encoder models for System One Applications
sd886d447d5.description: arXiv:2611.17867v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study encoder models that pick one of several options in a single forward pass, without generating text. This technical report compares recipes for fine-tuning UltraBERT-380M with one mask per option. The four recipes differ in how an option is scored and how the scores become probabilities; one follows the expert gate of DeepSeek-V3. sd886d447d5.summary: A technical report compares fine-tuning recipes for UltraBERT-380M encoder models that select among options in one forward pass, reporting 69.7% to 72.1% test accuracy versus 67.6% for Qwen3-0.6B.
sd886d447d5.why: Smaller encoder models may match a much smaller LLM on option-selection tasks at lower inference cost, which matters for cost-sensitive deployments.

se93fe3acc0.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
se93fe3acc0.description: arXiv:2611.17878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world's energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. City energy is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN's Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing studies are largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future cities; fine-grained, aligned monthly dynamic energy data are scarce; and existing GenAI models struggle to generate dynamic urban functional monthly energy. We present DySENSE, a joint multimodal GenAI framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with spatially aligned, dynamic monthly building energy consum
se93fe3acc0.summary: DySENSE is a framework for generating dynamic, spatiotemporal urban energy data and emulating energy use using satellite imagery, aimed at future cities.

s9099976e05.title: From Local Prediction Error to Final Outputs: A Theory of Expert Sharing in Multi-Step Reasoning
s9099976e05.description: arXiv:2611.17879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models can share experts across layers or computational steps, pooling training information from different contexts. This can reduce local prediction error, but multi-step systems are ultimately evaluated by their final outputs. We study when these local gains survive composition. In specified linear regression models, we derive exact sharing and merging criteria by balancing variance savings against bias from sharing across roles with different target behavior. s9099976e05.summary: A theoretical paper derives criteria for when sharing mixture-of-experts experts across layers or steps reduces local error and still helps final multi-step outputs.
s9099976e05.why: It gives principled guidance on when expert sharing in MoE architectures improves end-to-end results rather than only local prediction error.

sce0677a0e4.title: Photogrammetric 3D Model-Based Animal Behavior Classification
sce0677a0e4.description: arXiv:2611.17881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video-based behavior estimation is often implemented end-to-end from image sequences. We advocate a two-stage alternative: reconstruct 3D body and object geometry before classifying behavior. This makes ambiguities of the ill-posed 2D-to-3D inverse problem explicit and potentially correctable. We demonstrate the strategy with simulated interacting mice and extend it to real video.
sce0677a0e4.summary: Researchers propose classifying animal behavior by first reconstructing 3D body and object geometry from video, then classifying, demonstrated on simulated and real mouse video.

s1668e120e9.title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems by Design
s1668e120e9.description: arXiv:2611.17883v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems solve complex tasks by decomposing them into subtasks, delegating the subtasks to agents, and aggregating the agents' responses using an aggregation rule. Malicious agents can manipulate the final solution by providing malicious responses to their assigned subtasks. In this paper, we first propose response manipulation attacks (ReMA), which iteratively optimize malicious responses to maximize attack effectiveness. Specifically, we formulate untargeted and targeted attacks as optimization problems and develop an approach to approximately solve these problems by iteratively refining malicious responses based on feedback from a surrogate multi-agent system. s1668e120e9.summary: Researchers propose response manipulation attacks (ReMA) on multi-agent systems, where malicious agents optimize responses to skew the aggregated final solution, and study securing such systems by design.
s1668e120e9.why: Multi-agent systems that aggregate subagent outputs can be manipulated by a few malicious agents, so aggregation rules and agent trust need security design.

sc059b673d1.title: More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology
sc059b673d1.description: arXiv:2611.17899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) prediction from histology aims to infer spatially resolved gene expression profiles directly from tissue images. This is a challenging problem that is currently often addressed with complicated model architectures, additional inputs, and complicated training procedures, while remaining limited to fixed, small gene panels. This raises a natural question: Is there an efficient method for large-panel ST prediction? Here, we present GeneFlow, a simpler yet effective framework for large-scale spatial gene expression prediction that unifies flow-matching generative modeling with structured multimodal fusion. Specifically, GeneFlow first encodes both histological morphology and cross-gene interactions in spatial spots
sc059b673d1.summary: GeneFlow is a framework for predicting expression of large gene panels from histology images, presented as a simpler and more efficient alternative to complex existing methods.

s72d5d955cd.title: Condensing Law of Security Information
s72d5d955cd.description: arXiv:2611.17918v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling laws indicate that the generalization error of a large language model (LLM) decreases monotonically with model size once data is sufficient, and the corollary that larger models outperform smaller ones is now widely accepted. We argue that this corollary fails in security: decisions there hinge on anomalous inputs, which are long-tailed (e.g., zero-day attacks) and therefore poorly served by likelihood fitting. Worse still, the capability brought about by scale (e.g., inferring the intended whole from a corrupted part) leads a LLM silently \emph{repair} the anomaly before any downstream security head ever sees it. s72d5d955cd.summary: The paper argues that the scaling-law assumption that larger LLMs always do better fails in security, because anomalous, long-tailed inputs such as zero-day attacks are poorly served by likelihood fitting.
s72d5d955cd.why: Engineers choosing models for security tasks should not assume bigger models will detect rare anomalies better.

s7e83a04a21.title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration
s7e83a04a21.description: arXiv:2611.17931v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In mineral exploration, verifying geological hypotheses relies on designing a variety of geochemical experiments. While large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate downstream geoscientific data analysis, a crucial upstream capability remains largely unexplored: automated geochemical experimental design, i.e., deciding which experiments to conduct before committing to costly laboratory work. Evaluating this capability of LLM agents is difficult for two reasons. First, geochemical experiments exhibit high methodological diversity and subjectivity: to test the same hypothesis, different geologists may choose different minerals and instruments, so no single protocol can serve as the reference answer. Second, open-ended experimental
s7e83a04a21.summary: MineralExp is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on automated geochemical experimental design for real-world mineral exploration.

s221c6afdeb.title: Can You Trust Your Finance Agent? Drift, Diagnosis and Auditable Intervention on One Shipped Financial Research Agent
s221c6afdeb.description: arXiv:2611.17939v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can you trust a finance agent you did not build? We take the reference agent shipped with the Vals Finance Agent Benchmark v2, leave it untuned, and ask four questions a leaderboard score does not answer. Is the score stable? Seven identical runs on 18 questions pass between 105 and 123 of 149 rubric criteria, and the bill varies by up to 17%. When the agent fails, who owns the fix? We classify 20 failed trajectories, from three runs of nine held-out questions, by the layer whose owner would remedy them, under a taxonomy frozen in advance: 13 belong to the agent's instructions, 3 to its tools, 4 to the model, none to its data. Can that diagnosis be trusted? Four blind readers from three model families, given only the traces, name the same f
s221c6afdeb.summary: The paper audits the reference agent shipped with the Vals Finance Agent Benchmark v2, finding run-to-run score variation and classifying failures by which layer's owner would fix them.
s221c6afdeb.why: Shows that leaderboard scores hide instability and cost variation in agents, and that failures need ownership-based diagnosis before deployment.

s4ef40d9b87.title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
s4ef40d9b87.description: arXiv:2611.17966v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (CGEC) is typically formulated as a text-to-text problem. While suitable for digital texts, this formulation falls short in real-world K-12 education, where AI-assisted corrections are expected directly on essay images, which are primarily handwritten and exhibit many irregularities. To bridge this gap, we introduce Grounded Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (G-CGEC), an image-to-grounded-edit task requiring systems to predict both corrections and their positions on essay images. We propose G-CGEC-Eval, a benchmark comprising real-world images of K-12 Chinese essays with fine-grained annotations. For evaluation, we adapt IoU-based metrics from object detection and propose a more tolerant alternative b
s4ef40d9b87.summary: Researchers introduce G-CGEC, a task and benchmark for correcting grammatical errors in handwritten Chinese essay images by predicting both corrections and their positions.
s4ef40d9b87.why: Image-grounded correction for handwritten K-12 essays extends grammar-correction systems beyond digital text, a gap for education products.

s07e4982b92.title: RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$: On-Device Reinforcement Learning Runtime
s07e4982b92.description: arXiv:2611.18035v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-device reinforcement learning runs a periodic actor and a learner on one embedded GPU shared with other workloads. Because the learner produces the actor's weights, existing designs stall the actor or let its policy drift. We present RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$, an on-device runtime that makes this coupling a tunable parameter: a refresh bound limits actor releases between refreshes, and a GPU permit with slack-aware admission prioritises the actor and fills spare time with training atop any base scheduler. Under the real refresh cost on two Jetson boards, RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$ keeps a 16.8 M-parameter policy's deadline misses below 1%, against 85 to 100% without it.
s07e4982b92.summary: RL^RT is an on-device reinforcement learning runtime that shares one embedded GPU between an actor and learner, using a tunable refresh bound and GPU permits, evaluated on Jetson boards.
s07e4982b92.why: Engineers running RL on edge hardware face a tradeoff between actor stalls and policy drift, and this runtime makes that coupling tunable.

sb89f42088b.title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
sb89f42088b.description: arXiv:2611.18078v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Direct image-to-video diffusion models entangle pixel synthesis with implicit latent motion, precluding persistent 3D mechanical equilibrium, mid-rollout intervention, and counterfactual force control. Conversely, single-pass programmatic 3D reconstruction from an uncalibrated photograph leaves monocular depth and support clearance underconstrained, causing reconstructed scenes to interpenetrate or collapse under gravity. We present TelePhysica, a closed-loop framework that reconstructs an executable, multi-regime physical world from a single photograph to drive stateful 3D interaction and trajectory-grounded video synthesis. A vision-language coding agent synthesizes separable visual meshes and declarative physical models within a two-stag
sb89f42088b.summary: TelePhysica is a closed-loop framework that reconstructs physically interactive 3D scenes from a single photograph, aiming for stable, simulatable scenes that support interventions.

s250a57ee0f.title: AG-JEPA: Anatomically Guided Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Neurodegenerative Representation Learning
s250a57ee0f.description: arXiv:2611.18097v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Brain MRI can reveal early signs of Alzheimers disease (AD) before measurable cognitive decline becomes apparent. However, during the transition from cognitively normal (CN) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI), the disease-related signals are often subtle and confined to only a few brain regions. Existing Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) models learn general structural representations but do not explicitly capture the anatomical regions affected in AD. We propose Anatomically Guided JEPA (AG-JEPA), which introduces anatomical tokens that interact with patch tokens during pretraining to learn region-specific representations from brain regions relevant to neurodegeneration. Building on this representation space, we further propos
s250a57ee0f.summary: AG-JEPA adds anatomical tokens to a joint embedding predictive architecture to learn brain MRI representations for detecting early Alzheimer's-related changes.

s244054ed4b.title: EcoVGGT: Pinned-Key Inference for Efficient and Streamable Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Long Videos
s244054ed4b.description: arXiv:2611.18099v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Feed-forward multi-view transformers such as VGGT recover the cameras and geometry of a video in one pass, but the cost of their cross-frame attention grows quadratically with the frame count, and their accuracy drops on long videos. Most remedies approximate attention over all frames within a budget or select a few keys by their content. We hypothesize that the keys of a long video can be chosen without looking at its content, and our experiments on VGGT and $\pi^3$ support it: a few dozen evenly spread frames can serve as the keys of every frame. s244054ed4b.summary: EcoVGGT proposes pinned-key inference, choosing a few dozen evenly spread frames as attention keys for feed-forward 3D reconstruction from long videos, tested on VGGT and π³.
s244054ed4b.why: It targets the quadratic cost of cross-frame attention in multi-view transformers, suggesting a cheaper, streamable path for long-video 3D reconstruction.

s27be8abe92.title: An In-Silico Audit of Topographic Organization in a Multimodal Brain-Response Model
s27be8abe92.description: arXiv:2611.18105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: TRIBE v2 (d'Ascoli et al., 2026) predicts fMRI responses across the cortical surface from video, audio and text. Its authors validated it with category-selective localizers (faces, places, bodies, words) and language contrasts, but not with the classic topographic organization of sensory cortex: retinotopy, tonotopy, and motion selectivity in area MT+. There is a clear architectural reason to expect retinotopy to fail: TRIBE's video features are averaged over space before the response head, which should discard visual-field position. I present mapping stimuli, a fitting pipeline adapted from standard fMRI mapping analyses, and a stand-in model with known ground truth that serves as a positive and negative control, and apply them to TRIBE v2
s27be8abe92.summary: An in-silico audit tests whether the TRIBE v2 brain-response model reproduces classic topographic organization such as retinotopy, tonotopy, and MT+ motion selectivity.

sa9784775ed.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
sa9784775ed.description: arXiv:2611.18114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks are powerful predictors, yet their opacity limits their usefulness in science, where the goal is explanation rather than mere prediction. In neuroscience, for example, deep encoding models accurately predict brain activity in response to natural stimuli, but struggle to reveal which stimulus features drive those predictions. Here we introduce interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), a method in which an LLM agent iteratively builds interpretable models by explicitly programming their weights and features in code, without gradient-based training (backpropagation). Without backpropagation to tune parameters, the agent must draw on its prior knowledge and reason over previous trials to hypothesize, hand-craft, and refine
sa9784775ed.summary: Researchers introduce interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), where an LLM agent builds transparent models by writing their weights and features in code, applied to transformers and brain encoding models.
sa9784775ed.why: It offers a route to interpretable models built by LLM agents, relevant to teams needing explainable predictive systems.

se5a4fe74ed.title: PUMA-Former: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Computation Offloading in MEO-LEO Satellite Networks With Incomplete Information
se5a4fe74ed.description: arXiv:2611.18139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Satellite edge computing distributes mobile workloads across moving processors whose service capacity must be coordinated over time. In medium Earth orbit (MEO)--low Earth orbit (LEO) networks, periodic reports leave CPU states stale or missing, making offloading sensitive to uncertain capacity and shared-destination congestion. We propose PUMA-Former, an uncertainty-aware agentic framework for cooperative offloading under incomplete information that balances completed work, service delay, and execution cost. A MEO coordinator maintains distinct-report memory and closes the loop between available evidence, capacity estimates, allocation commands, and execution feedback. se5a4fe74ed.summary: PUMA-Former is proposed as an uncertainty-aware agentic framework for cooperative computation offloading across MEO-LEO satellite networks with incomplete CPU state information.

s699bd0c4a4.title: Who Should Be on the Panel? Task-Conditioned Persona Selection for LLM Trading Agents
s699bd0c4a4.description: arXiv:2611.18150v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems are built by fixing a cast of roles and then designing how the cast coordinates. Which agents should make up the group for a given task is left to the designer, and the same cast is reused for every task. Financial trading makes the cost of that choice visible: stocks trade differently, and the trading styles suited to one need not suit another. We study task-conditioned persona selection, composing the group from the characteristics of the task it will face, and instantiate it with FinPanel, an LLM multi-agent trading system in which a recruiter selects a panel of named trader personas for each stock from a direction-blind statistical sketch of how the stock trades, each persona gives an independent daily call in it
s699bd0c4a4.summary: The paper studies task-conditioned persona selection, composing LLM trading agent panels based on task characteristics, and instantiates it as FinPanel.
s699bd0c4a4.why: It suggests multi-agent LLM systems should select roles per task rather than reuse a fixed cast, a design choice relevant to agent architects.

sc857b0102f.title: T2ST: Data-Efficient Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models via Temporal Data and Knowledge Transfer
sc857b0102f.description: arXiv:2611.18199v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatio-temporal foundation models (STFMs) require large-scale training corpora, yet synchronized observations and spatial metadata are costly to acquire and curate, limiting the availability of suitable data. By contrast, time-series data are abundant and easier to collect. Since observations at each location form a time series, this motivates a natural question: can abundant time-series data enhance STFMs when spatio-temporal observations are scarce? To bridge this gap, we propose T2ST, a data-efficient training framework that augments limited spatio-temporal observations with selected auxiliary time series and transfers knowledge from a frozen time-series foundation model. sc857b0102f.summary: T2ST is a data-efficient training framework that augments scarce spatio-temporal data with abundant time-series data to build spatio-temporal foundation models.
sc857b0102f.why: It offers a way to train spatio-temporal foundation models when synchronized observations and spatial metadata are scarce.

s7387c6ab30.title: From Pen-and-Paper to Machine-Checked Proofs: Lean for System Identification
s7387c6ab30.description: arXiv:2611.18220v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mathematical proofs in scientific papers are often long and intricate, relying on chains of references to earlier results. This makes it difficult for readers and reviewers to verify each and every step. Interactive theorem proving offers a complement: the theorem and its proof are written as code, and every inference is checked by a small, trusted piece of software called the kernel. This paper serves as an introduction to the Lean 4 proof assistant for a system identification and control audience, assuming no prior exposure to formal methods. s7387c6ab30.summary: An introductory paper presents the Lean 4 proof assistant for system identification and control audiences, showing how machine-checked proofs can verify scientific derivations.

sc69d43cf61.title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots
sc69d43cf61.description: arXiv:2611.18230v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Personal assistant robots powered by large language models (LLMs) are likely to enter everyday life within the next decade, but the values that should guide their behaviour remain largely unspecified. Current alignment practice steers a single model toward an aggregate of human values, ignoring that individual users may prefer a robot whose value profile differs from their own. We administer parallel self- and robot-targeted versions of three established psycho-metric instruments - the simplified Schwartz Values Survey (SVS), the Portrait Values Questionnaire (PVQ-21), and the Moral Foundations Questionnaire (MFQ) - to potential future users (N=22), capturing both their personal values and the values they would want an assistant robot to em
sc69d43cf61.summary: The paper examines how personal LLM-powered assistant robots could be personalized to individual users' basic and moral value profiles rather than an aggregate human value set.
sc69d43cf61.why: Shows that per-user value alignment for assistant robots may differ from single aggregate alignment targets, relevant to product design.

sf1bd70109d.title: RACE: Ranking-Uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation
sf1bd70109d.description: arXiv:2611.18244v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efficient sequential recommendation has emerged as a promising paradigm for providing real-time personalized service. To deploy models under resource-constrained environment, model compression becomes a necessity, yet existing methods typically apply uniform compression ratios, overlooking the heterogeneity in user intent complexity. This "one-size-fits-all" approach leads to a fundamental Capacity-Complexity Mismatch, where computational resources are either wasted on simple instances or insufficient for complex ones. To address this, we propose RACE (Ranking-uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation), a framework that dynamically adapts both model structures and input sequences with uncertai
sf1bd70109d.summary: RACE proposes ranking-uncertainty aware, capacity-adaptive model compression for sequential recommendation, varying compression by user intent complexity instead of uniform ratios.
sf1bd70109d.why: It offers a way to allocate compute in recommenders by request complexity rather than applying one compression ratio everywhere.

s003002ca39.title: ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization
s003002ca39.description: arXiv:2611.18252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning across multiple inherently conflicting objectives requires selecting desirable trade-offs from the Pareto set. In this work, we study preference-guided multi-objective optimization, where a predefined preference function is minimized over the weak Pareto set of multiple nonconvex objectives. Leveraging a merit function that vanishes on the weak Pareto set, we propose a penalty-based min-max-min formulation, termed the M$^3$ problem, which unifies preference optimization and the enforcement of weak Pareto optimality in a single objective. s003002ca39.summary: ParetoM³ proposes a penalty-based min-max-min formulation for preference-guided learning on the weak Pareto set of multiple nonconvex objectives.

sac957ae48f.title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States
sac957ae48f.description: arXiv:2611.18272v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing memory forensics for machine learning systems typically targets static artifacts, such as model weights or prompt logs, rather than the transient computational states of a live inference process. This gap limits an examiner's ability to analyze the specific behavior of a running large language model (LLM) service that cannot be restarted or modified. We present a method for acquiring per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU process using a non-modifying debugger, without requiring prior knowledge of the model's architecture parameters or weights. sac957ae48f.summary: The paper presents a method to acquire per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU LLM process using a non-modifying debugger, enabling request-level attribution.
sac957ae48f.why: It enables forensic analysis of running LLM services that cannot be restarted or modified, useful for incident investigation in production.

s8fc7306346.title: Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering
s8fc7306346.description: arXiv:2611.18274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Activation steering via sparse autoencoders (SAEs) enables behavioral control of large language models without task-specific fine-tuning. Yet, standard methods apply the steering signal at every generated token, displacing representations from the distribution the model was trained on and eroding generation quality. s8fc7306346.summary: The paper proposes trajectory-aware activation steering for LLMs, treating steering with sparse autoencoders as a per-token allocation problem under a fixed budget of steerable tokens.
s8fc7306346.why: It suggests when steering is applied during generation affects output quality, offering a way to control behavior with less degradation.

sad93a409d8.title: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review
sad93a409d8.description: arXiv:2611.18293v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents increasingly review code, yet whether they catch the privacy defects that laws such as the GDPR require software to avoid remains largely untested, partly because few datasets connect real privacy defects to their accepted fixes and review context. We present PrivacyPR, a dataset of 4,131 merged GitHub pull requests (PRs) from 1,469 repositories, created between June 2018 and January 2024. Each PR includes its commits, diffs, review discussion, and LLM-generated labels for privacy relevance, fix type, and GDPR principles. sad93a409d8.summary: PrivacyPR is a dataset of 4,131 merged GitHub pull requests linking real privacy defects and fixes, built to benchmark whether coding agents catch GDPR-relevant issues in code review.
sad93a409d8.why: It provides a benchmark for testing whether AI code review tools catch privacy defects, relevant to compliance-focused engineering teams.

s02363fb45b.title: AI for Parameter Selection in Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization
s02363fb45b.description: arXiv:2611.18307v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) methods provide a way to compute molecular ground-state energies, but their accuracy and runtime depend sensitively on configuration choices such as the subspace dimension, propagation timestep, and the allocation of a fixed sampling budget across circuits, for which no formal selection method exists. In this work, we explore whether oracle models can predict the quantum runtime and approximation error from the Hamiltonian and the candidate configuration. s02363fb45b.summary: The paper explores whether oracle models can predict quantum runtime and approximation error to select configuration parameters for sample-based quantum diagonalization.

se841119ab8.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
se841119ab8.description: arXiv:2611.18359v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. se841119ab8.summary: A position piece argues that agentic robotics, where a foundation model runs a closed loop of observing, reasoning, invoking skills, and verifying, is replacing task-specific robot policies.
se841119ab8.why: It frames a shift from dedicated robot policies to foundation-model agents, though the piece's claims about a specific release are unverified here.

sb3b36b2217.title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment
sb3b36b2217.description: arXiv:2611.18372v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models adapt web-pretrained vision-language models to output robot actions, so that web knowledge carries over to physical control. In under 4 years the field has moved from RT-2, the first VLA, to open models that fine-tune on a single consumer GPU and to proprietary generalists that clean unseen homes. This survey reviews 88 works from December 2022 to October 2026, mainly on manipulation and navigation, plus humanoid control, world-action models and evaluation. We follow a VLA through its life cycle, from model design to training and deployment, along seven axes. sb3b36b2217.summary: A survey reviews 88 vision-language-action (VLA) robot models from December 2022 to October 2026, covering design, training, and deployment across manipulation, navigation, and humanoid control.
sb3b36b2217.why: It offers a life-cycle reference for engineers building robot foundation models, from architecture choices through training and deployment.

s093afc9ec4.title: AI-Based Multi-View Echocardiographic Image Synthesis using Dynamic Shape Control
s093afc9ec4.description: arXiv:2611.18375v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Although automated methods have improved echocardiographic workflows, progress remains constrained by the need for large, well-annotated datasets. As the development of clinical databases is often limited by ethical and logistical challenges, synthetic data generation has emerged as a promising alternative. However, existing approaches commonly rely on left ventricle shape-based supervision or are tailored to specific cardiac views, limiting the generation of additional standard and unconventional imaging planes and the preservation of multi-view consistency across cardiac chambers. s093afc9ec4.summary: Researchers propose an AI method for synthesizing multi-view echocardiographic images using dynamic shape control, aiming to reduce reliance on scarce annotated clinical datasets.

s67ddb54c88.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
s67ddb54c88.description: arXiv:2611.18397v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. s67ddb54c88.summary: Gamer is a generalist vision-language-action agent framework for long-horizon tasks in 2D graphical interfaces and 3D simulated worlds, trained on keyboard and mouse interaction data.
s67ddb54c88.why: Unified agents that operate across game and embodied environments show how perception, memory, and multi-step reasoning can be combined in one pipeline.

s327bf5315b.title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
s327bf5315b.description: arXiv:2611.18417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal continual instruction tuning requires multimodal large language models to sequentially acquire new capabilities without catastrophic forgetting. Mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures offer a promising way to mitigate task interference through expert specialization and combination. However, while existing MoE-based methods avoid overwriting shared parameters by allocating separate experts for each task, this progressive expansion incurs severe cross-task redundancy and linear parameter growth. s327bf5315b.summary: CoPre-MoE proposes a mixture-of-experts method for multimodal continual instruction tuning that aims to reduce cross-task redundancy and parameter growth while avoiding catastrophic forgetting.
s327bf5315b.why: Addresses parameter growth in continually updated multimodal models, a practical cost concern for teams fine-tuning MLLMs over time.

sa229d1692d.title: Between Obligations and Evidence: A Participatory Study of Translating the EU AI Act into Technical Requirements
sa229d1692d.description: arXiv:2611.18439v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The EU AI Act imposes technical and organizational requirements for high-risk AI systems, but applying these requirements involves contextual choices about what to measure and what evidence supports a compliance claim. We investigate these challenges through a participatory workshop involving 32 researchers, policymakers, and practitioners from different disciplines, using realistic scenarios in healthcare, recruitment, and public transport to examine how regulatory obligations are interpreted, translated into technical requirements, and evaluated in practice. sa229d1692d.summary: A participatory workshop with 32 researchers, policymakers, and practitioners examined how EU AI Act obligations for high-risk systems translate into technical requirements and compliance evidence.
sa229d1692d.why: Shows where interpretation gaps arise when turning EU AI Act obligations into measurable technical compliance evidence.

s38cc2fa65d.title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
s38cc2fa65d.description: arXiv:2611.18453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable use of large language models (LLMs) requires uncertainty estimates that separate ambiguity intrinsic to a prompt from genuine knowledge gaps. Bayesian and deep-ensemble methods deliver this aleatoric/epistemic decomposition in principle, but are computationally prohibitive at LLM scale and require white-box access. s38cc2fa65d.summary: Researchers introduce a black-box two-level ensemble method for LLM uncertainty quantification that aims to separate aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty without white-box access.
s38cc2fa65d.why: Lets teams using closed LLM APIs distinguish prompt ambiguity from knowledge gaps, improving reliability signals without model internals.

sf2b25f29d1.title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
sf2b25f29d1.description: arXiv:2611.18471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM-based verifiers are increasingly used to evaluate agent executions, but their reliability is typically measured under a single representation of the trajectory. In deployed agent systems, the same execution may be exposed through composed tools, delegation boundaries, or compacted histories, changing what execution evidence is directly observable to the verifier. sf2b25f29d1.summary: The paper introduces Verification Transport, a test measuring whether LLM verifier judgments of agent executions remain correct when trajectories are abstracted, composed, or compacted.
sf2b25f29d1.why: Agent evaluators may give different verdicts once tool composition or history compaction hides evidence, affecting how teams trust automated agent checks.

sc2441f47a7.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
sc2441f47a7.description: arXiv:2611.18484v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings. This structured scoping review finds that mature agentic care has not yet emerged: Most systems remain human led, while stronger decision-action coupling and embodied AI remain largely confined to prototypes and pilots. sc2441f47a7.summary: A scoping review finds AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is moving toward agentic systems, but most remain human-led and embodied healthcare robotics stays mostly at prototype or pilot stage.
sc2441f47a7.why: Indicates that autonomous care agents with real decision-action coupling are still largely experimental, guiding realistic healthcare deployment planning.

s00b61ce05d.title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors
s00b61ce05d.description: arXiv:2611.18485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Program induction refers to the process in which a learner aims to recover a program from a few given input-output examples. This paradigm broadens programming access by letting users demonstrate the rule-based behavior they want to apply to unseen data, instead of having to implement it themselves.
