s00b61ce05d.summary: The paper studies interactive program induction, using language model priors to resolve ambiguity when recovering a program from a few input-output examples.

s3f6c8be79b.title: TradeGauntlet: Evaluating Compliance Controls for Autonomous Trading Agents
s3f6c8be79b.description: arXiv:2611.18493v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous trading agents need controls that prevent problematic orders without making legitimate tasks impractical. We study this aspect of agentic compliance with TradeGauntlet, a replayable limit-order-book simulator that separates detection, prevention, and execution cost. In 1,680 simulated sessions with Claude Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, all conduct alerts were self-matches. Gates eliminated those alerts by rejecting self-crossing orders, while the aggregate-gate condition reduced Sonnet's two-sided fills by about 15%. A conduct reminder reduced Sonnet's alert rate but reduced Haiku's fills without a detectable alert benefit. These results show why zero alerts alone do not establish an agent's compliance. Scripted probes and two search
s3f6c8be79b.summary: TradeGauntlet is a replayable limit-order-book simulator that evaluates compliance controls for autonomous trading agents, testing 1,680 sessions with Claude Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5.
s3f6c8be79b.why: Demonstrates how pre-trade gates and reminders trade off detection, prevention, and execution cost for agents operating under compliance constraints.

sd0cac9360e.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
sd0cac9360e.description: arXiv:2611.18504v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes. The full stack of quantum computing encompasses several tasks: preparation of logical code states, implementation of logical gates, logical routines on encoded qubits, etc. Yet, these circuits are largely designed by hand for individual cases, with some recent works incorporating machine learning for certain aspects. We formulate this problem as agentic evolutionary program synthesis, wherein a large language model, leveraging its pretraining knowledge and tool-use proficiency, and guided by a circuit verifier, evolves a program that defines a Clifford circuit
sd0cac9360e.summary: Researchers formulate fault-tolerant quantum circuit design as agentic evolutionary search, aiming to automate circuits for logical state preparation and gates that are now mostly hand-designed.

s8eb3cc0e91.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
s8eb3cc0e91.description: arXiv:2611.18513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and generation to the reader's distinct position in the text. The system integrates a hybrid retrieval architecture, combining vector similarity, BM25, and summary embeddings, to ensure high fidelity to the reader's current context. We evaluate the system across classical English books using both quantitative comprehension metrics and qualitative LLM-based ind
s8eb3cc0e91.summary: MeReader is a privacy-preserving, offline AI assistant for eBook reading that limits retrieval and generation to the reader's current position to avoid narrative spoilers.
s8eb3cc0e91.why: Illustrates a local-first RAG design that restricts context by reading progress, relevant to privacy-sensitive consumer deployments.

s93ed487bea.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
s93ed487bea.description: arXiv:2611.18542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative modeling based on stochastic interpolants requires specifying two key choices: an interpolant schedule bridging the initial and target distributions, and an efficient discretization of the resulting probability-flow ODE. In this work, we introduce a new framework for joint schedule/discretization design based on the analyticity properties of the (complexified) ODE trajectories, which in turn ensure good numerical behavior. Our formulation can be solved exactly via conformal mapping, yielding a natural family of variance-preserving elliptic schedules, parametrized by Jacobi elliptic functions. Pairing an elliptic schedule with a tailored discretization, we obtain Zoloflow, a new sampling algorithm closely connected to Zolotarev's
s93ed487bea.summary: The paper introduces a framework for jointly designing interpolant schedules and ODE discretization for generative models based on analyticity, with a conformal-mapping solution for Gaussians.

sce30139330.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
sce30139330.description: arXiv:2611.18553v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. Experi
sce30139330.summary: WeightBench is a benchmark evaluating LLMs on 42 weight-space programming tasks across reading, fixing, and writing neural network weights without gradient descent.
sce30139330.why: Provides a standard way to measure whether LLMs can directly read and edit other networks' parameters, an emerging capability.

s66d8e40987.title: From Chats to Markets: AgenticPay for LLM-Powered Negotiation in Multi-Agent Commerce
s66d8e40987.description: arXiv:2602.06008v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly expected to negotiate and transact autonomously, yet existing benchmarks rarely combine multimodal product grounding, multi-issue bargaining, and competitive multi-agent markets. We introduce AgenticPay, a unified benchmark for evaluating multimodal agents' ability to reach high-welfare, multidimensional agreements in realistic markets. AgenticPay includes 160 multimodal tasks across four business scenarios (E-commerce, Food Delivery, Ride-hailing, and Apartment Rental) and eight market topologies, from bilateral bargaining to many-to-many competition. Agents interpret product images, infer opponents' hidden preferences, and negotiate binding contract terms such as price, lease duration, return
s66d8e40987.summary: AgenticPay is a benchmark with 160 multimodal tasks across four commerce scenarios and eight market topologies for evaluating LLM agents negotiating multi-issue agreements in competitive markets.
s66d8e40987.why: Gives teams a testbed for assessing how autonomous agents negotiate and transact in multi-agent markets before deploying them commercially.

sef5720ac7b.title: Evaluating Chain-of-Thought Reasoning through Reusability and Verifiability
sef5720ac7b.description: arXiv:2602.17544v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: AI applications increasingly compose multiple models, where one model acts on the output produced by another model. The transferred text can also carry the reasoning of the sender model. Chain-of-thought is our experimental instance of such text. We ask three questions about such inter-model reasoning transfer. Is the reasoning transmitted reliably? Is it useful to the receiver? Is it safe? We study these three questions with a Sender-Receiver setup. A Sender LLM produces a reasoning trace. A separate Receiver LLM must act on it. Neither model knows the identity of the other. The Sender therefore cannot tailor its reasoning to a particular Receiver. Reliability asks whether the Receiver recovers the Sender's intended conclusion. We measur
sef5720ac7b.summary: Researchers study whether chain-of-thought reasoning passed between a Sender LLM and a Receiver LLM is reliable, useful, and safe.
sef5720ac7b.why: Multi-model pipelines pass reasoning traces downstream, so engineers need to know whether that transferred reasoning can be trusted and acted on.

s8b8395d01a.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Multimodal Large Language Models with Incoherence-adjusted Semantic Volume
s8b8395d01a.description: arXiv:2602.24195v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite their capabilities, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) may produce plausible but erroneous outputs, hindering reliable deployment. Accurate uncertainty metrics could enable escalation of unreliable queries to human experts or larger models for improved performance. However, existing uncertainty metrics have practical constraints, such as being designed only for specific modalities, reliant on external tools, or computationally expensive. We introduce UMPIRE, a training-free uncertainty quantification framework for MLLMs that works efficiently across various input and output modalities without external tools, relying only on the models' own internal modality features. Inspired by Determinantal Point Processes (DPPs), UMPIRE c
s8b8395d01a.summary: Researchers introduce UMPIRE, a training-free uncertainty quantification framework for multimodal LLMs intended to flag unreliable outputs.
s8b8395d01a.why: Reliable uncertainty signals could let teams route risky multimodal queries to human experts or larger models without extra training.

s3df28f2237.title: Multi-Environment POMDPs with Finite-Horizon Objectives
s3df28f2237.description: arXiv:2605.07537v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) are systems in which one agent interacts with a stochastic environment, and receives only partial information about the current state. In a multi-environment POMDP (MEPOMDP), the initial state is unknown, and assumed to be adversarially chosen. In this work we focus on computing the optimal value and policy in MEPOMDPs with finite-horizon objectives. That problem is known to be PSPACE-complete in POMDPs. The extension is nontrivial: MEPOMDPs require reasoning about beliefs and payoffs across environments, and deterministic policies are no longer enough for optimal payoff. While the lower bound transfers immediately, the upper bound requires new techniques: we prove that mixtures of a
s3df28f2237.summary: Researchers study computing optimal values and policies for multi-environment POMDPs with finite-horizon objectives, where the initial state is adversarially chosen.

s12437685a4.title: Do LLMs Experience an Internal Polylogue? Investigating Reasoning through the Lens of Personas
s12437685a4.description: arXiv:2605.09159v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) encode behavioural traits ("personas") as linear directions in activation space, often called "persona vectors". Prior work has used such directions as static handles for behavioural steering. We instead treat them as dynamic signals: probes we can monitor and intervene on as reasoning unfolds. We use the term polylogue to denote the time series of alignments between persona vectors and hidden activations over the course of generation. Experiments across four open-weight models show that polylogue features predict correctness on MMLU-Pro on par with low-dimensional activation baselines, while remaining interpretable through their associated persona directions. They also suggest concrete
s12437685a4.summary: Researchers treat LLM persona vectors as dynamic probes, tracking their alignment with hidden activations during reasoning across four open-weight models.
s12437685a4.why: Monitoring persona signals during generation could offer a way to observe and steer model behavior mid-reasoning rather than only statically.

s393672b72f.title: D-VLA: A High-Concurrency Distributed Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models
s393672b72f.description: arXiv:2605.13276v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rapid evolution of Embodied AI has enabled Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to excel in multimodal perception and task execution. However, applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to these massive models in large-scale distributed environments faces severe systemic bottlenecks, primarily due to the resource conflict between high-fidelity physical simulation and the intensive VRAM/bandwidth demands of deep learning. This conflict often leaves overall throughput constrained by execution-phase inefficiencies. To address these challenges, we propose D-VLA, a high-concurrency, low-latency distributed RL framework for large-scale embodied foundation models. D-VLA introduces "Plane Decoupling," physically isolating high-frequency training dat
s393672b72f.summary: Researchers present D-VLA, a distributed asynchronous reinforcement learning framework for training Vision-Language-Action models at high concurrency.
s393672b72f.why: Addresses throughput bottlenecks from balancing physical simulation against VRAM and bandwidth demands when running RL on large VLA models.

se4c1f62db1.title: ShopGym: An Integrated Framework for Realistic Simulation and Scalable Benchmarking of E-Commerce Web Agents
se4c1f62db1.description: arXiv:2605.16116v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Developing and evaluating e-commerce web agents requires environments that preserve meaningful task structure while enabling controllable, reproducible, and scalable scientific comparison. Existing methods force a tradeoff: live storefronts provide realism but are non-stationary, difficult to inspect, and irreproducible, while hand-built sandbox benchmarks provide control but cover only a narrow range of layouts, catalogs, policies, and interaction patterns. We argue that the core bottleneck is methodological: the field lacks a scalable way to construct evaluation settings that are simultaneously realistic, diverse, controllable, inspectable, and reproducible. We introduce ShopGym, an integrated framework for realistic simulation and scal
se4c1f62db1.summary: Researchers present ShopGym, a framework for simulating and benchmarking e-commerce web agents in reproducible, scalable environments.
se4c1f62db1.why: Offers a controllable alternative to live storefronts for evaluating shopping agents, which teams building web agents need for repeatable comparisons.

scb76b353e5.title: Certified Policy Optimisation for Nested Causal Bandits via PAC-Bayes Risk
scb76b353e5.description: arXiv:2605.29788v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Critical sequential decisions are rarely single-timescale: a strategic decision causally shapes the context in which every subsequent tactical choice is made; standard bandit and reinforcement-learning theory does not capture this causal coupling between timescales. We formalise the problem class as Nested Contextual Causal Bandits (NCCBs), a hierarchical SCM where each level's action sets the next level's context distribution, and propose Nested Causal Thompson Sampling (NCTS), which draws one mechanism-factorised belief per episode and acts recursively under it. Our main theoretical result is a causal PAC-Bayesian excess-risk bound that certifies any candidate deployment policy from historic data alone, off-policy and anytime, answering
scb76b353e5.summary: Researchers propose Nested Causal Thompson Sampling for nested contextual causal bandits, where a strategic decision shapes the context for later tactical choices.

s864361318b.title: CoffeeBench: Benchmarking Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Economies
s864361318b.description: arXiv:2606.16613v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly capable of handling complex, long-horizon tasks and may eventually take on business management, a role traditionally performed by humans. Deploying them safely requires monitoring their capabilities and behavior in environments that reflect real economies. We introduce CoffeeBench, a benchmark built on a compact simulation of a coffee supply chain with realistic business mechanics. Six autonomous LLM coding agents run its farmers, roasters, and retailers, and negotiate and trade with one another to maximize their own net income over 90 simulated days. We evaluate eight recent proprietary and open-weight models by letting each run one roaster while a fixed background model runs the other five firms, and scoring
s864361318b.summary: Researchers introduce CoffeeBench, a benchmark where six LLM coding agents run farmers, roasters, and retailers in a simulated coffee supply chain.
s864361318b.why: Shows a way to test long-horizon multi-agent business behavior in simulated economies, relevant to assessing agents before deploying them in business roles.

s01beded6f8.title: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
s01beded6f8.description: arXiv:2608.09654v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: GUI agents are shifting from metadata-dependent large language models to purely visual multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that operate directly on screenshots. The core task, GUI grounding, requires translating abstract user instructions into precise element coordinates. This task faces a persistent dual obstacle: conventional grounding models lack the semantic richness to interpret abstract instructions, while end-to-end MLLMs suffer from coordinate hallucinations caused by deficient fine-grained perception. We propose a regression-free framework where a frozen MLLM performs instruction parsing and a dedicated grounding model handles precise localization without learning any coordinate regression. A frozen MLLM first elaborates the
s01beded6f8.summary: Researchers propose a regression-free, layout-aware matching method to reduce coordinate hallucinations in visual MLLM-based GUI grounding.
s01beded6f8.why: Coordinate hallucinations are a practical reliability problem for screenshot-based GUI agents that must click precise elements.

s84b2202933.title: ReForge: Keeping ABR Algorithms Never Finished with Verified Large Language Model Revisions
s84b2202933.description: arXiv:2608.15138v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Designing an ABR algorithm for a network scenario takes an engineer months, and large language models (LLMs) now do this work in hours. But either way, the algorithm is fixed once it is deployed. It fits the networks seen during its design and falls behind on the networks that arrive afterwards. We ask whether an ABR algorithm can keep being designed after deployment, revised as each new network arrives, without becoming worse on any network it already serves. We propose ReForge, which keeps a pool of existing ABR policies unchanged and lets an LLM revise only the rules that decide which policy chooses the next bitrate. When a new network arrives, the LLM reads how the current rules and every policy perform on the networks served so far a
s84b2202933.summary: Researchers propose ReForge, which revises ABR video streaming algorithms with verified LLM edits after deployment without degrading performance on networks already served.
s84b2202933.why: Shows a path to continuously improving deployed networking policies with LLMs while guarding against regressions on existing conditions.

sc8f6a8badb.title: Programmable Distributions of Semantics-Preserving Variants for Evaluating Code Agents
sc8f6a8badb.description: arXiv:2608.18389v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Code agents are increasingly deployed to resolve real software issues, yet their reliability under superficial code variations remains poorly understood. We evaluate whether coding agents that repair repository-level issues remain reliable when the surrounding codebase is rewritten into a semantically equivalent form. We sample semantically equivalent variants of a repository from an explicitly defined distribution and compare the agent's resolve rate on them with that on the original. Different distributions reveal different aspects of an agent, such as its sensitivity to routine refactoring or to misleading code near the location of a fix. We develop VDL, a probabilistic programming language for expressing such distributions, whose prog
sc8f6a8badb.summary: Researchers evaluate coding agents on semantically equivalent rewrites of repositories, finding resolve rates can shift under superficial code variations.
sc8f6a8badb.why: Suggests coding agent benchmarks may overstate reliability, since behavior can change when code is rewritten without altering its meaning.

s7853a4d467.title: From Regulation to Implementation: A Critical Evaluation of LLM-Assisted Regulatory Compliance in Industry
s7853a4d467.description: arXiv:2608.21317v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The European Union (EU) has emerged as a leading regulatory body in the development of sustainability and privacy regulations. While new regulation requirements vary, many include a documentation artifact to ensure compliance. Notably, the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) introduces Digital Product Passports (DPPs) for life cycle transparency, while the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) mandates Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) to mitigate privacy risks. Creating these compliance artifacts, however, is challenging. Industrial data, which often exists in heterogeneous formats and is scattered across company and supplier systems, is required for DPPs and can be difficult to extract into compliant DPP fo
s7853a4d467.summary: A critical evaluation examines using LLMs to help create EU regulatory compliance artifacts such as Digital Product Passports and GDPR impact assessments in industry.
s7853a4d467.why: Gives compliance and engineering leaders evidence on how far LLM-assisted documentation can meet EU requirements in practice.

sd1c9c2119b.title: AI Agents Push Humans Out of the Loop
sd1c9c2119b.description: arXiv:2608.23642v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: AI agents pose significant risks as they are granted increasing autonomy. A commonly proposed solution is human oversight and keeping a ''human in the loop'', but this is not a simple solution: Not only do current approaches to AI agent design impede effective human oversight, but the cognitive capacities required for it are also themselves degraded by extended use of AI systems. This position paper argues that current approaches to the development and deployment of AI agent systems do not support effective human oversight -- they contribute to its degradation. To address this, a top priority in the advancement of AI agents should be supporting the situated goals and cognitive requirements of effective human oversight, treating the human
sd1c9c2119b.summary: A position paper argues current AI agent designs undermine effective human oversight and degrade the cognitive capacities oversight requires.
sd1c9c2119b.why: Challenges the assumption that keeping a human in the loop is sufficient, which affects how teams design agent oversight.

s74408eb6e8.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Human-Agent Interaction
s74408eb6e8.description: arXiv:2609.04141v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: AI agents are trained on population-scale data to encode broad capabilities spanning those of many practitioners. Yet the artifacts they produce rarely meet the personal bar professionals need to stake their reputation on. On realistic, open-ended tasks where success criteria are heterogeneous and insufficiently documented, individual expertise lives precisely in the elevation and departure from the average. In practice, iterative human-agent interaction surfaces criteria that users cannot fully specify up front, yet apply repeatedly across tasks. We argue this cross-session interaction data is a rich, underused signal for closing the gap to individual expertise. In this work, we propose test-time adaptation through human-agent interactio
s74408eb6e8.summary: Researchers propose efficient test-time adaptation via iterative human-agent interaction to capture criteria users cannot fully specify upfront.
s74408eb6e8.why: Suggests a way to tailor agent outputs to individual expert standards through repeated interaction rather than upfront specification.

s837e46ac6a.title: MeanFlowAdvantage: Stable Reward Fine-Tuning for Few-Step Average-Velocity Generators
s837e46ac6a.description: arXiv:2609.37670v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: MeanFlow enables efficient few-step generation by predicting interval-average velocities, but this representation creates a mismatch for reward fine-tuning: existing advantage-based objectives are typically defined on instantaneous velocities or equivalent $x_0$-space predictions, whereas inference directly uses the learned average-velocity map. We introduce MeanFlowAdvantage, a signed advantage-weighted least-squares objective for average-velocity generators. Our key construction uses a shared, detached MeanFlow derivative correction to express the reward objective in prediction space while making rollout and reference regularization exact penalties on the average-velocity network deployed at inference. The resulting formulation preserve
s837e46ac6a.summary: Researchers introduce MeanFlowAdvantage, a reward fine-tuning objective for few-step average-velocity generators that matches the inference-time average-velocity map.

saa539defd4.title: Proof-Grounded Patient-Specific Clinical Explanations from Knowledge-Graph Reasoning
saa539defd4.description: arXiv:2610.06549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Clinical decision support can lack auditable links from observations and encoded knowledge to conclusions and recommendations. Downstream of a frozen, training-free clinical knowledge-graph reasoner, the CKG Clinical Explanation Engine converts patient inference states and disease knowledge into typed facts, explicit rule traces, provenance-linked conclusions, and policy-licensed recommendations. Separate availability, representation completeness, and disease-specific activation distinguish observed zero-activation and partial evidence from unobserved evidence. Language-generation evaluation remains future work. Across six usable workbooks (11,289 patients, 33,867 patient-disease traces, 1,715,928 feature-evidence rows), IG-range validity
saa539defd4.summary: Researchers describe the CKG Clinical Explanation Engine, which turns knowledge-graph reasoning outputs into typed facts, rule traces, and provenance-linked clinical recommendations.
saa539defd4.why: It targets auditable clinical decision support, where engineers building healthcare systems need traceable links from observations to recommendations.

s3b7e77ad09.title: When to Rethink: Learning Multi-Perspective Self-Verification for Vision-Language Models
s3b7e77ad09.description: arXiv:2610.07018v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance in multimodal reasoning, yet they remain prone to generating plausible but incorrect answers. Self-verification offers a practical way to improve answer reliability without relying on external judges, but existing methods typically depend on a single verification criterion or fixed prompt, resulting in incomplete and unstable reliability estimates. We first systematically analyze how verifier capability and prompt design affect verification performance. Our findings show that stronger verifiers provide more reliable judgments, while verification performance is highly sensitive to prompt choice, with no single prompt consistently dominating across tasks. Guided by these finding
s3b7e77ad09.summary: Researchers propose a multi-perspective self-verification method for vision-language models to better detect plausible but incorrect answers without external judges.
s3b7e77ad09.why: More reliable self-verification could reduce wrong answers from multimodal systems without adding external judge models.

sd4ba5cb869.title: Self-Building Labs
sd4ba5cb869.description: arXiv:2610.23826v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for. Adapting them to a new experiment still requires extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery. We introduce the self-building laboratory (SBL), which designs, configures, and operates its own laboratory setup given a high-level scientific goal. SBL starts from whatever already exists, from an empty room to a working SDL, and builds the missing capabilities: the lab layout, its digital twin, robot skills, and experimental workflows. We demonstrate t
sd4ba5cb869.summary: Researchers introduce a self-building laboratory that designs, configures, and operates its own lab setup from a high-level scientific goal.

s58e0591131.title: TorchTPU - A Hybrid Eager/Compiled Architecture for Native PyTorch Execution on TPU
s58e0591131.description: arXiv:2610.24161v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: TorchTPU is an open-source collaboration between Google and Meta that introduces a native and principled PyTorch backend for Google TPUs. It enables seamless out-of-the-box model execution and TPU migration while delivering industry-competitive inference and training performance through eager execution optimizations, torch.compile integration, and native hardware acceleration.
s58e0591131.summary: Google and Meta describe TorchTPU, an open-source native PyTorch backend for Google TPUs supporting eager execution and torch.compile integration.
s58e0591131.why: Engineers running PyTorch can migrate models to TPUs with less rework, using a native backend rather than a separate port.

seff63018ab.title: FlashRT-PAI: Fast Kernels Are Not Fast Pipelines for Physical AI
seff63018ab.description: arXiv:2610.24349v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA), video-action (VA), and world action models (WAMs) form the backbone of modern physical AI systems, yet their real-time single-batch inference remains a defining bottleneck. Latency is dominated not by individual kernel computation, but by system-level overhead: thousands of short kernel launches, intermediate data movement across operator boundaries, and redundant recomputation across consecutive decisions. General-purpose graph compilers cannot address these costs, as they optimize individual calls in isolation and lack visibility into cross-call state semantics and global pipeline structure. seff63018ab.summary: FlashRT-PAI targets real-time inference latency in physical AI models, arguing system-level overhead, not kernel speed, dominates vision-language-action pipelines.
seff63018ab.why: Robotics teams optimizing real-time inference may find kernel-level speedups insufficient without addressing pipeline overhead.

s6eeb144cbd.title: Pluralistic Alignment in Large Language Models: Objectives, Human References, and Preference Representations
s6eeb144cbd.description: arXiv:2610.24471v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pluralistic alignment aims to represent meaningful variation in human preferences rather than collapse heterogeneous judgments into a single target. Yet existing work often mixes three distinct questions: what pluralistic behavior a model should exhibit, whose preferences define the reference, and what evidence is sufficient to demonstrate success. We organize the literature around a two-layer taxonomy. Layer 1 distinguishes representing a range of human-supported viewpoints (Overton Pluralism), adapting faithfully to a specified perspective or preference condition (Steerable Pluralism), and matching the response distribution observed in a target population (Distributional Pluralism). Layer 2 distinguishes aggregate populations, countries
s6eeb144cbd.summary: A survey proposes a two-layer taxonomy for pluralistic alignment in LLMs, separating target behavior, whose preferences define the reference, and evidence of success.

s6095c295c9.title: TimesJev: Thinking Fast on Time Series with System 1 Sufficiency
s6095c295c9.description: arXiv:2610.26002v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently shown strong potential for time series reasoning, while models that reason over time series are usually with long chains of thought. However, this process often consumes thousands of tokens, directly leading to substantial latency during inference. In contrast, System 1 models such as Jev make decisions instantly and can naturally be an alternative, but raw time series are not compatible with the embedding space of these models, thus hindering the reasoning performance, especially when input series contain thousands of numeric points. s6095c295c9.summary: TimesJev proposes using fast System 1 models for time series reasoning, aiming to avoid the thousands of tokens long chain-of-thought reasoning requires.
s6095c295c9.why: Reducing reasoning tokens could cut inference latency for time series applications that currently depend on long chain-of-thought outputs.

sb8584c45b5.title: Can LLMs Improve Their Own Harness? A Controlled Study on ARC-AGI-3
sb8584c45b5.description: arXiv:2610.30499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A generally intelligent system acquires new skills efficiently without requiring humans to redesign its software scaffold for every new task. Yet language models rarely act alone. A harness is a symbolic program that orchestrates calls to the model, handling perception, memory, tool use, recovery, and inference allocation on the model's behalf. ARC-AGI-3 is an interactive benchmark in which agents must explore unfamiliar environments, figure out their goals on the fly, and keep learning as they go. On it, human-steered systems already report ceiling scores across the public games, so we know effective designs exist. sb8584c45b5.summary: A controlled study examines whether LLMs can improve their own harness, the scaffold orchestrating model calls, on the ARC-AGI-3 interactive benchmark.
sb8584c45b5.why: Self-improving agent scaffolds bear on how much human engineering agent harnesses will require in future.

sa6848ef258.title: One Offset, Two Directions: Baseline Adjustment via Subgroup Offsets
sa6848ef258.description: arXiv:2611.00782v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) estimates advantages against the within-prompt mean reward, a baseline shared across the group. In practice, rollouts within a prompt are not always homogeneous, differing in their solution strategies and reasoning trajectories, along which they may group into subgroups. We further find that these heterogeneous subgroups may exhibit distinct reward distributions. The global baseline, however, collapses them onto a single credit axis, where the credit reflects neither a rollout's standing within its subgroup nor the subgroup's standing relative to the rest. sa6848ef258.summary: Researchers propose subgroup-based baseline adjustment for GRPO, arguing the global within-prompt mean baseline collapses heterogeneous rollout subgroups with distinct rewards.
sa6848ef258.why: Better advantage baselines could improve reinforcement learning fine-tuning of reasoning models that use GRPO.

s0e1357720a.title: Function-Preserving Audits of Visual Weight Readers
s0e1357720a.description: arXiv:2611.05798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A neural field can encode the same image with different weights. A reader that recognizes one such representation may therefore rely on parameter coordinates rather than the visual function. We study this distinction through function-preserving transformations, measuring recognition, prediction disagreement, and numerical fidelity together. Across shape, digit, and natural-image fields, high accuracy on the original weights coexists with substantial sensitivity to equivalent representations. On 10,000 official CIFAR10 test origins, one-period hidden-bias shifts change 7.3% of a released HiddenProbe configuration's predictions while barely changing accuracy; three-period shifts change 22.0% and reduce accuracy from 57.8% to 54.4%. s0e1357720a.summary: Researchers show visual readers of neural field weights can be highly accurate on original weights yet sensitive to function-preserving equivalent representations.

sd328870dff.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
sd328870dff.description: arXiv:2611.08752v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet they remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety mechanisms and elicit harmful or unintended outputs. Although safety can be improved through model fine-tuning, such approaches can be computationally expensive and may degrade previously acquired capabilities through catastrophic forgetting. Recent jailbreak defenses have therefore explored targeted interventions on specific model components associated with unsafe behavior. However, existing approaches typically decouple two inherently related decisions: where to intervene and how to modify the selected components. Such sequential optimization may be suboptimal because the optima
sd328870dff.summary: AttentionSwitch proposes a jailbreak defense for LLMs that jointly learns sparse attention-head selection and scaling, avoiding costly fine-tuning.
sd328870dff.why: Targeted component interventions offer a potentially cheaper alternative to fine-tuning for hardening LLMs against jailbreaks.

sb3a6e4e943.title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
sb3a6e4e943.description: arXiv:2611.09326v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Foundation models are increasingly deployed as agentic systems that perceive context and act autonomously, raising the need to evaluate their moral behavior as active decision-makers. Existing benchmarks, however, largely ask models to judge human actions from third-person textual vignettes, leaving untested how models behave when they themselves become the acting agent. We introduce ABHBench, a multimodal benchmark built from Detroit: Become Human, an interactive narrative game, to evaluate how foundation models make moral decisions in first-person human-android dilemmas. ABHBench places foundation models in branching narrative scenarios with visual observations, dialogue, memory, and action choices. Inspired by Asimov's Three Laws of Ro
sb3a6e4e943.summary: ABHBench is a multimodal benchmark built from the game Detroit: Become Human that tests how foundation models make moral decisions as acting agents.
sb3a6e4e943.why: Evaluating models as first-person agents exposes moral behavior that third-person vignette benchmarks miss, relevant to autonomous deployments.

s13f9d9491c.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
s13f9d9491c.description: arXiv:2611.12762v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce Sage-Taiyi, a metacognition-inspired architecture that uses accumulated scientific understanding to guide what to investigate next and how to investigate it. Through explicit monitoring and control, the system revises its understanding of evidence, assumptions, and unresolved questions, then uses these assessments to adapt research targets and select reusable reasoning methods. On Taiyi-Bench, an AI co-scientist ideation benchmark comprising 265 tasks from 50 papers across ten disciplines, Sage-Taiyi ranks first on all eight metrics of historical rediscovery and open-ended ideation, achieving an Overall score of 54.0 compared with 47.9 for the strongest baseline, AI Scientist-v2. It also performs well on two external scientif
s13f9d9491c.summary: Sage-Taiyi is a metacognition-inspired architecture that guides scientific investigation, reporting first place on all eight metrics of the Taiyi-Bench ideation benchmark.

s6f21f818dd.title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
s6f21f818dd.description: arXiv:2611.13710v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Manifold embedding for data visualisation is dominated by a small set of hand-designed state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithms. Their design targets are fixed at development time, resulting in inflexible algorithmic behaviour that cannot be readily steered towards user-specified structural priorities. Hand-designing new embedding algorithms to address user priority requires highly specialised expertise and is time consuming. To address autonomous algorithm design tailored to user preference, we introduce an agentic algorithm generation pipeline AutoManifold. It composes new manifold embedding algorithms from a constrained vocabulary of affinity, cost, and optimisation primitives, supported by multi-agent large-language-model (LLM) orchestratio
s6f21f818dd.summary: AutoManifold is an agentic pipeline that generates data visualisation embedding algorithms tailored to user-specified structural priorities.
s6f21f818dd.why: Shows agents automating algorithm design for user-specified objectives, a pattern applicable to other engineering tooling.

se0544ad648.title: MIGRO: A Decoupled and Portable Long-Term Memory System for Language Models
se0544ad648.description: arXiv:2611.15315v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Language models evolve, but the observations, revisions, and context accumulated through user interactions should remain usable. Each new model must be able to retrieve past evidence, track revisions, and add new observations. We present MIGRO, a decoupled long-term memory system that treats experience as a persistent state shared across successive language models. MIGRO follows a simple principle: preserve historical evidence exactly, organize it approximately, and decide what to retrieve only when the question is known. We call this asymmetric fidelity with deferred selectivity. A shared semantic index supports retrieval, while exact records retain observations and their historical relationships. se0544ad648.summary: MIGRO is a decoupled long-term memory system that keeps interaction history as persistent state shared across successive language models.
se0544ad648.why: A model-independent memory layer could let teams swap underlying LLMs without losing accumulated user context.

s192b15e64d.title: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models
s192b15e64d.description: arXiv:2611.15592v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In September 2026, TypeSafe announced Jev as the first model in its System One category: unstructured state goes in, and typed, calibrated decisions that software can use directly come out. Jev's architecture and training data are unpublished, but many open typed-decision models have followed, including Nimble, the Decision 1.0-3.0 family and Clef. They answer structured questions about a piece of text, such as a yes/no check, a choice among labelled options or a graded score, by reading the text with a language model and scoring the options with a small readout. Each pairs a different readout with a different backbone, training mix and recipe, so it is unclear which design choices matter. We re-implement five readouts and train all of th
s192b15e64d.summary: A controlled study compares typed-decision models, which read text with a language model and output calibrated yes/no, choice, or graded-score decisions.
s192b15e64d.why: Typed decision heads could cut inference cost for routing and classification, but the text gives few concrete results to judge them by.

s2bb32454b2.title: Benchmarking AI risk behaviors
s2bb32454b2.description: arXiv:2611.16318v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We evaluate LLM risk propensities across a range of contexts and task demands. We evaluate models for how risk averse or risk tolerant they are in various conditions, as well as how stable and consistent their behavior is across conditions. We present a toolkit for developing model risk profiles that can be used to predict model behavior and which can be adapted to include new evaluations of risk propensities. We also examine how these properties have changed across model generations and families. We observe that 2026 state-of-the-art models tend to be more stable, more consistent, and more risk neutral than older models. These trends appear to be related; newer models are more stable and consistent because they are more likely to use exp
s2bb32454b2.summary: Researchers present a toolkit that profiles LLM risk propensities, measuring how risk-averse or consistent models are across contexts and generations.
s2bb32454b2.why: Standardized risk profiles could help teams predict model behavior and compare model generations before deploying them in sensitive settings.

s894b840845.title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
s894b840845.description: arXiv:2611.16937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Typed System-1 (S1) decision models are increasingly deployed in LLM agents for routing, moderation, and authorization to cut inference cost, yet untrusted context can still manipulate typed outputs and alter execution branches. Unlike autoregressive System-2 (S2) models, S1 interfaces score dynamic rules and options without token-by-token decoding, mismatching attacks targeting text continuation or explicit override commands. We propose S1-Evo, a self-evolving framework tailored to S1's contract-based option competition and margin feedback. S1-Evo perturbs untrusted fields via contract-aware evidence channels to induce \emph{evidence competition} with original task evidence while preserving fact invariance. Offline on seed tasks, it opti
s894b840845.summary: S1-Evo proposes a self-evolving attack framework that manipulates typed System-1 decision models used for routing, moderation, and authorization in LLM agents.
s894b840845.why: Agents relying on typed decision models for authorization may be vulnerable to context-based manipulation, so these attacks matter for defense design.

s9411c87e03.title: Ballad: Bandit-Based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery
s9411c87e03.description: arXiv:2611.17241v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern automated heuristic discovery (AHD) systems increasingly rival hand-crafted heuristics by leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to iteratively mutate and refine solutions. A natural assumption is that more powerful and more expensive models consistently yield better heuristics. We challenge this empirically: across multiple NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems, we find no consistent advantage for larger, costlier models. This raises a deeper question: given a pool of LLMs spanning frontier and freely hosted or open-weight models, how should one adaptively select which model to invoke at each step of the search? The challenge is non-trivial. The optimal LLM may shift over the course of a run, and because one LLM's output se
s9411c87e03.summary: Ballad uses bandit-based routing across LLMs for automated heuristic discovery, finding no consistent advantage for larger, costlier models on NP-hard problems.
s9411c87e03.why: Engineers may be able to cut costs in automated optimization pipelines by routing among cheaper models rather than always using the most expensive one.

sd198ae4b3b.title: Fake News Detectors are Biased against Texts Generated by Large Language Models
sd198ae4b3b.description: arXiv:2309.08674v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The spread of fake news has emerged as a critical challenge, undermining trust and posing threats to society. In the era of Large Language Models (LLMs), the capability to generate believable fake content has intensified these concerns. In this study, we present a novel paradigm to evaluate fake news detectors in scenarios involving both human-written and LLM-generated misinformation. Intriguingly, our findings reveal a significant bias in many existing detectors: they are more prone to flagging LLM-generated content as fake news while often misclassifying human-written fake news as genuine. This unexpected bias appears to arise from distinct linguistic patterns inherent to LLM outputs. To address this, we introduce a mitigation str
sd198ae4b3b.summary: A study finds many fake news detectors are biased, more often flagging LLM-generated texts as fake than human-written ones.
sd198ae4b3b.why: Teams using automated detectors to filter content should check for bias against machine-generated text, since it can skew moderation outcomes.

s0cb4621f8f.title: Astraios: Parameter-Efficient Instruction Tuning Code Large Language Models
s0cb4621f8f.description: arXiv:2401.00788v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The high cost of full-parameter fine-tuning (FFT) of Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to a series of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods. However, it remains unclear which methods provide the best cost-performance trade-off at different model scales. We introduce Astraios, a suite of 28 instruction-tuned OctoCoder models using 7 tuning methods and 4 model sizes up to 16 billion parameters. Through investigations across 5 tasks and 8 different datasets encompassing both code comprehension and code generation tasks, we find that FFT generally leads to the best downstream performance across all scales, and PEFT methods differ significantly in their efficacy based on the model scale. LoRA usually offers the most favorable
s0cb4621f8f.summary: Astraios is a suite of 28 instruction-tuned code models comparing seven parameter-efficient tuning methods across four model sizes up to 16 billion parameters.
s0cb4621f8f.why: The comparison of tuning methods across scales helps engineers pick cost-effective fine-tuning approaches for code models.

sbc27a3af6e.title: BigCodeBench: Benchmarking Code Generation with Diverse Function Calls and Complex Instructions
sbc27a3af6e.description: arXiv:2406.15877v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Task automation has been greatly empowered by the recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) via Python code, where the tasks ranging from software engineering development to general-purpose reasoning. While current benchmarks have shown that LLMs can solve tasks using programs like human developers, the majority of their evaluations are limited to short and self-contained algorithmic tasks or standalone function calls. Solving challenging and practical tasks requires the capability of utilizing diverse function calls as tools to efficiently implement functionalities like data analysis and web development. In addition, using multiple tools to solve a task needs compositional reasoning by accurately understanding complex instruc
sbc27a3af6e.summary: BigCodeBench is a benchmark testing code generation that uses diverse function calls and complex instructions, beyond short algorithmic tasks.
sbc27a3af6e.why: It offers a more realistic test of whether code models can use multiple tools for practical tasks, informing model selection.

s1fb0088e98.title: Benign Overfitting for Regression with Trained Two-Layer ReLU Networks
s1fb0088e98.description: arXiv:2410.06191v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the least-square regression problem with a two-layer fully-connected neural network, with ReLU activation function, trained by gradient flow. Our first result is a generalization result, that requires no assumptions on the underlying regression function or the noise other than that they are bounded. We operate in the neural tangent kernel regime, and our generalization result is developed via a decomposition of the excess risk into estimation and approximation errors, viewing gradient flow as an implicit regularizer. This decomposition in the context of neural networks is a novel perspective of gradient descent, and helps us avoid uniform convergence traps. s1fb0088e98.summary: A theoretical paper proves generalization results for two-layer ReLU networks trained by gradient flow in the neural tangent kernel regime.

s20f7693f48.title: LEGAL-UQA: Testing Constitutional Question-Answering Systems for Urdu Speakers with a Parallel English-Urdu Benchmark
s20f7693f48.description: arXiv:2410.13013v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Legal information assistants could help Urdu speakers understand their constitutional rights, but building reliable systems requires test data and evaluation methods suited to the language. We present LEGAL-UQA, a parallel English-Urdu benchmark of 619 question-answer pairs linked to passages from Pakistan's Constitution. Each example includes the question, reference answer, and source passage in both languages. We evaluate two components separately: answering Urdu questions when the source passage is supplied, and retrieving the passage from which each question was generated. We also compare JEV, a decision model used as an automated judge, with human grades. The findings show that model rankings depend on how answer similarity is
s20f7693f48.summary: LEGAL-UQA is a parallel English-Urdu benchmark of 619 question-answer pairs based on Pakistan's Constitution, for testing constitutional question answering.
s20f7693f48.why: It shows how multilingual legal assistants need language-specific evaluation data, which teams building non-English RAG systems should account for.

s46ae32a332.title: AbFlowNet: Optimizing Antibody-Antigen Binding Energy via Diffusion-GFlowNet Fusion
s46ae32a332.description: arXiv:2505.12358v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Complementarity Determining Regions (CDRs) are critical segments of an antibody that facilitate binding to specific antigens. Current computational methods for CDR design utilize reconstruction losses and do not jointly optimize binding energy, a crucial metric for antibody efficacy. Rather, binding energy optimization is done through computationally expensive Online Reinforcement Learning (RL) pipelines rely heavily on unreliable binding energy estimators. In this paper, we propose AbFlowNet, a novel generative framework that integrates GFlowNet with Diffusion models. s46ae32a332.summary: AbFlowNet combines diffusion and GFlowNet methods to jointly optimize antibody CDR design for antigen binding energy.

s25142c3821.title: Chi-Square Wavelet Graph Neural Networks for Heterogeneous Graph Anomaly Detection
s25142c3821.description: arXiv:2505.18934v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Graph Anomaly Detection (GAD) in heterogeneous networks presents unique challenges due to node and edge heterogeneity. Existing Graph Neural Network (GNN) methods primarily focus on homogeneous GAD and thus fail to address three key issues: (C1) Capturing abnormal signal and rich semantics across diverse meta-paths; (C2) Retaining high-frequency content in HIN dimension alignment; and (C3) Learning effectively from difficult anomaly samples with class imbalance. To overcome these, we propose ChiGAD, a spectral GNN framework based on a novel Chi-Square filter, inspired by the wavelet effectiveness in diverse domains. Specifically, ChiGAD consists of: (1) Multi-Graph Chi-Square Filter, which captures anomalous information via applying
s25142c3821.summary: ChiGAD is a spectral graph neural network framework for anomaly detection in heterogeneous graphs, addressing meta-path semantics and class imbalance.

s7f4346d078.title: Graph Your Own Prompt
s7f4346d078.description: arXiv:2509.23373v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose Graph Consistency Regularization (GCR), a novel framework that injects relational graph structures, derived from model predictions, into the learning process to promote class-aware, semantically meaningful feature representations. Functioning as a form of self-prompting, GCR enables the model to refine its internal structure using its own outputs. While deep networks learn rich representations, these often capture noisy inter-class similarities that contradict the model's predicted semantics. GCR addresses this issue by introducing parameter-free Graph Consistency Layers (GCLs) at arbitrary depths. s7f4346d078.summary: Graph Consistency Regularization (GCR) injects relational graph structure derived from model predictions into training to produce more class-aware representations.

sffdcd27fa7.title: BigCodeArena: Unveiling More Reliable Human Preferences in Code Generation via Execution
sffdcd27fa7.description: arXiv:2510.08697v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Crowdsourced model evaluation platforms, such as Chatbot Arena, enable real-time evaluation from human perspectives to assess the quality of model responses. In the coding domain, manually examining the quality of LLM-generated content is extremely challenging, as it requires understanding long chunks of raw code and deliberately simulating code execution. To this end, we introduce BigCodeArena, an open human evaluation platform for code generation backed by a comprehensive and on-the-fly execution environment. Built on top of Chatbot Arena, BigCodeArena enables the execution of LLM-generated code and allows humans to interact with the execution process and outcomes. We collected over 14,000 raw code-centric conversation sessions ac
sffdcd27fa7.summary: BigCodeArena is an open human evaluation platform for code generation that runs generated code on the fly so raters can judge execution results.
sffdcd27fa7.why: Execution-based human preference evaluation may give more reliable model comparisons for coding tasks than reading raw code.

se38ea0614b.title: Manifold Approximation leads to Robust Kernel Alignment
se38ea0614b.description: arXiv:2510.22953v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Centered kernel alignment (CKA) is a popular metric for comparing representations, determining equivalence of networks, and conducting neuroscience research. However, CKA does not account for the underlying manifold and relies on numerous heuristics that cause it to behave differently at different scales of data. In this work, we propose Manifold-approximated Kernel Alignment (MKA), which incorporates manifold geometry (i.e., local neighborhood) into the alignment task. We derive a theoretical framework for MKA. Our construction removes representation-dependent degree weighting, yields a closed-form alignment score, and gives each row a probabilistic interpretation as a local Markov transition distribution. We further establish kern
se38ea0614b.summary: Manifold-approximated Kernel Alignment (MKA) modifies centered kernel alignment to account for data manifold geometry, aiming for more robust representation comparisons.

s05531200a1.title: E0: Expressive Fine-Grained Discrete Action Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models via Tweedie Discrete Diffusion
s05531200a1.description: arXiv:2511.21542v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer a unified framework for robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and control generation. However, existing VLA systems still struggle to generalize across diverse tasks, scenes, and camera viewpoints, and often produce coarse or unstable actions. We argue that these limitations are closely tied to the structural properties of actions in VLA settings, including the inherent multi-peaked nature of action distributions, the token-based symbolic reasoning of pretrained VLM/VLA backbones, and the effective finite resolution imposed by real-world robotic control. Motivated by these properties, we introduce E0, a tweedie discrete diffusion framework that formul
s05531200a1.summary: E0 proposes discrete diffusion for fine-grained action prediction in vision-language-action robotics models to produce more stable, expressive actions.
s05531200a1.why: Robotics teams building VLA systems may find more stable action outputs useful, though the text gives no benchmark results.

s4fe0a8211b.title: Model-Free Assessment of Simulator Fidelity via Quantile Curves
s4fe0a8211b.description: arXiv:2512.05024v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As generative AI models are increasingly used to simulate real-world systems, quantifying the ``sim-to-real'' gap is critical. For each input setting of interest -- which we call a \emph{scenario}, such as a survey question or operating condition -- the real and simulated systems are associated with unobserved latent population parameters, and their discrepancy varies across scenarios. A fundamental challenge is that, for any given scenario, this discrepancy cannot be observed directly, since both systems are accessible only through finite samples, often of heterogeneous sizes across scenarios. s4fe0a8211b.summary: Researchers propose a model-free method using quantile curves to assess how well simulators match real systems across scenarios, quantifying the sim-to-real gap.
s4fe0a8211b.why: Gives teams a way to measure simulator fidelity without needing direct observations of the real system's latent parameters.

s2201a7ff34.title: NEAT: Neighborhood-Guided, Efficient, Autoregressive Set Transformer for 3D Molecular Generation
s2201a7ff34.description: arXiv:2512.05844v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Transformer-based autoregressive models offer an efficient alternative to diffusion- and flow-based approaches for generating 3D molecules. One challenge remains: standard transformer architectures require a sequential ordering of tokens, which is not inherently defined for the atoms in a molecule. Prior works have addressed this by using canonical atom orderings. However, these approaches are not permutation invariant w.r.t. atoms and bias next-token prediction towards ordering conventions. We overcome this limitation by introducing a novel neighborhood-guided training strategy. s2201a7ff34.summary: Researchers introduce NEAT, a neighborhood-guided autoregressive set transformer that generates 3D molecules without relying on canonical atom orderings.
s2201a7ff34.why: Offers an efficient transformer alternative to diffusion models for 3D molecule generation that is permutation invariant over atoms.

sf7f0c55c64.title: Vision-language models lag human performance on physical dynamics and intent reasoning
sf7f0c55c64.description: arXiv:2601.01547v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spatial intelligence is central to embodied cognition, yet contemporary AI systems still struggle to reason about physical interactions in open-world human environments. Despite strong performance on controlled benchmarks, vision-language models often fail to jointly model physical dynamics, reference frames, and the latent human intentions that drive spatial change. We introduce Teleo-Spatial Intelligence (TSI), which captures an important aspect of spatial reasoning: integrating physical dynamics and action goals to reason about actions and their spatial consequences. sf7f0c55c64.summary: Researchers introduce Teleo-Spatial Intelligence, a benchmark finding vision-language models lag humans at reasoning about physical dynamics and human intent.
sf7f0c55c64.why: Highlights a gap in VLM spatial and intent reasoning that matters for embodied and real-world human-environment applications.

s139fdfdfa1.title: ISLA: Ensemble learning and domain adaptation for generalizable acute ischemic stroke lesion segmentation in diffusion MRI with clinical validation
s139fdfdfa1.description: arXiv:2601.08732v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate segmentation of acute ischemic stroke (AIS) lesions on MRI is essential for clinical decision-making. Deep learning methods offer a promising approach to automating this task. However, they often generalize poorly to unseen clinical sites, and few AIS lesion segmentation methods have been externally validated. In this study, we propose $\mathit{ISLA}$ (Ischemic Stroke Lesion Analyzer), a framework for AIS lesion segmentation built on the design principles of $\mathit{nnU\text{-}Net}$. $\mathit{ISLA}$ combines attention modules, deep supervision, and ensemble learning across different input resolutions, convolutional block types, and loss functions. We also introduce $\mathit{ISLA\text{-}MT}$, a variant that leverages unlabe
s139fdfdfa1.summary: Researchers present ISLA, an ensemble nnU-Net-based framework for acute ischemic stroke lesion segmentation in diffusion MRI, aimed at generalizing to unseen clinical sites.
s139fdfdfa1.why: Addresses poor generalization of medical segmentation models across clinical sites, with external clinical validation.

s4d86dbf728.title: Tracing 3D Anatomy in 2D Strokes: Can Projection-Derived Masks Replace 3D Segmentation for Cervical Spine Fracture Recognition?
s4d86dbf728.description: arXiv:2601.15235v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cervical spine fractures require rapid and accurate diagnosis, yet automatic CT interpretation remains challenging as subtle injuries must be assessed across large 3D volumes. We ask whether full 3D vertebra segmentation is necessary for fracture recognition, or whether vertebra masks approximated from 2D projections preserve sufficient diagnostic context. In the proposed multi-stage pipeline, a YOLOv8 detector localizes the cervical spine from multi-view variance projections (3D mean Intersection over Union 94.45%). s4d86dbf728.summary: Researchers test whether masks approximated from 2D projections can replace full 3D vertebra segmentation for detecting cervical spine fractures in CT.
s4d86dbf728.why: Suggests a potentially cheaper pipeline for CT fracture recognition that avoids full 3D segmentation.

sfb2e5fb86a.title: The Alignment Curse: Modality Alignment Supercharges Audio Attacks via Text Transfer
sfb2e5fb86a.description: arXiv:2602.02557v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advances in end-to-end trained omni-models have substantially improved audio capabilities by strengthening text-audio modality alignment. However, whether such alignment inadvertently facilitates the transfer of safety vulnerabilities across modalities remains underexplored. This question is critical as text-based jailbreak attacks are considerably more mature than audio-based ones; if they transfer systematically, current audio safety evaluations may underestimate risks originating from the text modality. sfb2e5fb86a.summary: Researchers show that modality alignment in end-to-end omni-models can let text-based jailbreak attacks transfer to audio, potentially underestimating audio-related risks.
sfb2e5fb86a.why: Suggests current audio safety evaluations may miss risks inherited from text, so teams deploying omni-models should test cross-modal attacks.

s9968513c74.title: ROCKET: Rapid Optimization via Calibration-guided Knapsack Enhanced Truncation for Efficient Model Compression
s9968513c74.description: arXiv:2602.11008v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present ROCKET, a training-free model compression method that achieves state-of-the-art performance in comparison with factorization, structured-sparsification and dynamic compression baselines. s9968513c74.summary: ROCKET is a training-free model compression method that allocates layer-wise compression via a multi-choice knapsack formulation under a global size budget.
s9968513c74.why: Offers a training-free way to compress models to a target size while minimizing reconstruction error, reducing retraining costs.

s5b41758b44.title: ScrapeGraphAI-100k: Dataset for Schema-Constrained LLM Generation
s5b41758b44.description: arXiv:2602.15189v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Producing output that conforms to a specified JSON schema underlies tool use, structured extraction, and knowledge base construction in modern large language models. Despite this centrality, public datasets for the task remain small, synthetic, or text-only, and rarely pair real page content with the prompts and schemas used in practice. We introduce ScrapeGraphAI-100k, 93,695 schema-constrained extraction events collected via opt-out ScrapeGraphAI telemetry in Q2--Q3 2025, deduplicated and balanced by schema from 9M raw events. The corpus spans 25,453 unique schemas, across 15 named languages, with English covering 89% of detected content. s5b41758b44.summary: Researchers release ScrapeGraphAI-100k, a dataset of 93,695 schema-constrained extraction events pairing real web page content with JSON schemas and prompts.
s5b41758b44.why: Provides realistic, real-world data for training and evaluating structured JSON output from LLMs.

s1e2b9e70fe.title: ESENSC: A Polynomial-Time Axiomatic Alternative to SHAP
s1e2b9e70fe.description: arXiv:2603.00496v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose ESENSC, a computationally efficient and theoretically grounded alternative to SHAP. ESENSC is a deterministic, closed-form attribution rule that requires only linearly many coalition-value evaluations, satisfies the null-player property, and admits an axiomatic characterization based on efficiency, a restricted form of differential marginality, and explicit computational constraints.Empirically, on tabular prediction tasks using neural network and XGBoost models, ESENSC shows close agreement with exact SHAP in both attribution magnitude and feature rankings while requiring substantially less computation. Under the evaluated settings, it compares favorably with widely used sampling-based SHAP approximations. While exact SH
s1e2b9e70fe.summary: Researchers propose ESENSC, a deterministic closed-form feature attribution rule that approximates SHAP values using linearly many coalition evaluations.
s1e2b9e70fe.why: Offers a faster, deterministic alternative to SHAP for explaining tabular model predictions, with close agreement to exact SHAP.

sc40978f2ae.title: ViroGym: Realistic Large-Scale Benchmarks for Evaluating Viral Proteins
sc40978f2ae.description: arXiv:2603.06740v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) have shown strong potential for zero-shot prediction of missense variant effects, yet systematic benchmarking on viral proteins remains limited, a critical gap given the need for proactive tools that can anticipate emerging mutations ahead of experimental validation. Here we introduce ViroGym, a comprehensive benchmark evaluating pLMs across three tasks: 79 deep mutational scanning (DMS) assays covering eukaryotic viruses with 552,065 mutated sequences across 7 phenotypic readouts, 21 influenza neutralisation tasks, and a real-world pandemic prediction task for SARS-CoV-2. We benchmark well-established pLMs on fitness landscapes, antigenic diversity, and pandemic forecasting, and find that the ProGen2
sc40978f2ae.summary: Researchers introduce ViroGym, a large benchmark evaluating protein language models on viral protein variant effect prediction across multiple tasks.
sc40978f2ae.why: Provides a systematic benchmark for judging whether protein models are reliable for anticipating viral mutations.

se97dca5666.title: Efficiently Aligning Draft Models via Parameter- and Data-Efficient Adaptation
se97dca5666.description: arXiv:2603.09527v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference but suffers from performance degradation when target models are fine-tuned for specific domains. A naive solution is to retrain draft models for every target model, which is costly and inefficient. To address this, we introduce a practical parameter- and data-efficient framework named Efficient Draft Adaptation, abbreviated as EDA, for efficiently adapting draft models. se97dca5666.summary: Researchers propose Efficient Draft Adaptation (EDA), a parameter- and data-efficient framework for adapting speculative decoding draft models to fine-tuned target models.
se97dca5666.why: Lets teams keep speculative decoding speedups after domain fine-tuning without costly full draft model retraining.

sd927b02da7.title: A Variational Latent Equilibrium for Learning in Neuronal Circuits
sd927b02da7.description: arXiv:2603.09600v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Brains remain unrivaled in their ability to recognize and generate complex spatiotemporal patterns. While AI is able to reproduce some of these capabilities, deep learning algorithms remain largely at odds with our current understanding of brain circuitry and dynamics. This is prominently the case for backpropagation through time (BPTT), the go-to algorithm for learning complex temporal dependencies. In this work we propose a general formalism to approximate BPTT in a controlled, biologically plausible manner. Our approach builds on, unifies and extends several previous approaches to local, time-continuous, phase-free spatiotemporal credit assignment based on principles of energy conservation and extremal action. Our starting point
sd927b02da7.summary: Researchers propose a biologically plausible formalism that approximates backpropagation through time in neuronal circuits using a variational latent equilibrium approach.
sd927b02da7.why: Foundational neuroscience-inspired learning research with limited direct near-term applicability for engineering teams.

s671caa5958.title: Comparative Analysis of 3D Convolutional and 2.5D Slice-Conditioned U-Net Architectures for MRI Super-Resolution via Elucidated Diffusion Models
s671caa5958.description: arXiv:2603.14667v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) super-resolution (SR) methods that computationally enhance low-resolution acquisitions offer a software alternative to higher-field scanners. We study an elucidated diffusion model (EDM) framework for 2x in-plane brain MRI SR and compare two U-Net backbones: (i) a 3D convolutional U-Net that processes volumetric patches and (ii) a 2.5D slice-conditioned U-Net that super-resolves each slice while conditioning on its two neighbouring slices. s671caa5958.summary: Researchers compare 3D convolutional and 2.5D slice-conditioned U-Net backbones for 2x brain MRI super-resolution using elucidated diffusion models.
s671caa5958.why: Compares architecture tradeoffs for diffusion-based MRI enhancement, a software alternative to higher-field scanners.

s8d5d1fa36c.title: FlashSampling: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Sampling
s8d5d1fa36c.description: arXiv:2603.15854v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sampling from a categorical distribution is mathematically simple, but in large-vocabulary decoding, it often triggers extra memory traffic and extra kernels after the LM head. We present FlashSampling, an exact sampling primitive that fuses sampling into the LM-head matmul and never materializes the logits tensor in HBM. The method is simple: compute logits tile-by-tile on chip, add Gumbel noise, keep only one maximizer per row and per vocabulary tile, and finish with a small reduction over tiles. s8d5d1fa36c.summary: Researchers present FlashSampling, an exact sampling primitive that fuses categorical sampling into the LM-head matmul without materializing the logits tensor in HBM.
s8d5d1fa36c.why: Reduces memory traffic and kernel launches in large-vocabulary LLM decoding, directly relevant to inference performance work.

s5b100727fd.title: Generative machine learning for protein design
s5b100727fd.description: arXiv:2603.26378v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Designing proteins with specific biological functions is of considerable interest for both the development of new therapeutics and the engineering of enzymes, yet achieving the intended activity remains challenging. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool to explore the vast space of possible designs by learning from protein sequence and structural data. Here, we review 59 generative approaches across six protein design tasks, including sequence generation, backbone generation, structure-conditioned sequence design, joint sequence-structure design, motif scaffolding, and binder and antibody design. We outline common generative approaches and protein representations and discuss how structural constraint
s5b100727fd.summary: A review of 59 generative AI approaches across six protein design tasks, covering sequence, backbone, and structure-conditioned generation.
s5b100727fd.why: Gives a consolidated map of generative protein design methods for teams evaluating tools for therapeutics or enzyme engineering.

s2e83590f28.title: Pruning Extensions and Efficiency Trade-Offs for Sustainable Time Series Classification
s2e83590f28.description: arXiv:2604.07953v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Time series classification (TSC) at scale requires balancing predictive performance against resource consumption, which is subject to the given data, model, and hardware. This paper introduces a multi-dimensional evaluation framework that allows for explicitly benchmarking and exploring the resource-versus-quality trade-offs in TSC. To improve efficiency, we present a pruning strategy with bounded error for leading hybrid classifiers - Hydra and Quant - and moreover propose Hydrant, a novel extension that integrates interval representations with random convolutions and dictionary learning.
