s2e83590f28.summary: Researchers propose a multi-dimensional framework for benchmarking resource-versus-quality trade-offs in time series classification, plus a bounded-error pruning strategy for Hydra and Quant.
s2e83590f28.why: Offers practical methods to cut compute for time series classifiers at scale, which matters when serving costs and energy budgets are constraints.

sf88e7ab244.title: Minimizing classical resources in variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling
sf88e7ab244.description: arXiv:2604.11578v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) is a framework for quantum information processing in which a computational task is carried out through one-qubit measurements on a highly entangled resource state. Due to the indeterminacy of the outcomes of a quantum measurement, the random outcomes of these operations, if not corrected, yield a variational quantum channel family. Traditionally, this randomness is corrected through classical processing in order to ensure deterministic unitary computations. Recently, variational measurement-based quantum computation (VMBQC) has been introduced to exploit this measurement-induced randomness to gain an advantage in generative modeling. A limitation of this approach is that the corresponding
sf88e7ab244.summary: Researchers study minimizing classical processing in variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling.

scab7db3616.title: Generating Concept Lexicalizations via Dictionary-Based Cross-Lingual Sense Projection
scab7db3616.description: arXiv:2604.14397v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the task of automatically expanding WordNet-style lexical resources to new languages through sense generation. We generate senses by associating target-language lemmas with existing lexical concepts via semantic projection. Given a sense-tagged English corpus and its translation, our method projects the annotated synsets onto aligned target-language tokens and assigns the corresponding lemmas to those synsets. To generate alignments and ensure their quality, we augment a pretrained base aligner with a bilingual dictionary, which is also used to filter incorrect sense projections. scab7db3616.summary: Researchers present a method that expands WordNet-style lexical resources to new languages by projecting senses across aligned corpora using a bilingual dictionary.
scab7db3616.why: Relevant mainly to teams building multilingual NLP resources, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s08d6bc2d2c.title: CPGRec+: A Balance-oriented Framework for Personalized Video Game Recommendations
s08d6bc2d2c.description: arXiv:2604.14586v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The rapid expansion of gaming industry requires advanced recommender systems tailored to its dynamic landscape. Existing Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based methods primarily prioritize accuracy over diversity, overlooking their inherent trade-off. To address this, we previously proposed CPGRec, a balance-oriented gaming recommender system. However, CPGRec fails to account for critical disparities in player-game interactions, which carry varying significance in reflecting players' personal preferences and may exacerbate over-smoothness issues inherent in GNN-based models. Moreover, existing approaches underutilize the reasoning capabilities and extensive knowledge of large language models (LLMs) in addressing these limitations. To brid
s08d6bc2d2c.summary: Researchers extend CPGRec into CPGRec+, a graph-based video game recommender that balances accuracy and diversity while weighting player-game interactions differently.

sacda27fe23.title: Screen Before You Interpret: A Portable Validity Screen for Benchmark-Based LLM Confidence Signals
sacda27fe23.description: arXiv:2604.17714v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: LLM confidence signals drive abstention, routing and escalation, yet evaluations rarely check whether a signal varies with correctness before computing metrics on it. Clinical personality assessment handles the analogous problem by screening response validity before interpreting substantive scales. We specify a portable screen in that tradition. From the correctness-by-confidence table it computes the rate of high confidence on errors (L), the rate of low confidence on correct answers (Fp), and their contrast (RBS, equal to minus Youden's J). It adds no new statistics: it separates blanket confidence, blanket withdrawal and inversion, attaches interval guards, and calls a signal Valid only when it measurably tracks correctness. On 2
sacda27fe23.summary: Researchers propose a portable validity screen that checks whether LLM confidence signals actually vary with correctness before metrics are computed on them.
sacda27fe23.why: Teams using LLM confidence for abstention or escalation can use this check to avoid acting on signals that don't track correctness.

s4cd40da2f8.title: BoostLoRA: Growing Effective Rank by Boosting Adapters
s4cd40da2f8.description: arXiv:2604.27308v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods face a tradeoff between adapter size and expressivity: ultra-low-parameter adapters are confined to fixed low-rank subspaces, capping performance even with extended training. We propose BoostLoRA, a gradient-boosting framework that overcomes this limit by iteratively training and merging minimal adapters on the examples the current model gets wrong. A ROTATE SVD basis strategy assigns each round to an orthogonal subspace, so cumulative effective rank grows linearly with the number of rounds while each adapter remains ultra-low-rank. s4cd40da2f8.summary: Researchers introduce BoostLoRA, a gradient-boosting approach that iteratively trains and merges minimal adapters on mispredicted examples to grow effective rank in parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
s4cd40da2f8.why: Suggests a way to raise expressivity of ultra-low-parameter fine-tuning adapters without increasing adapter size per round.

s28d8252584.title: Time series causal discovery with variable lags
s28d8252584.description: arXiv:2605.04081v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) are a powerful tool for reasoning under uncertainty about complex real-world problems. Such problems evolve over time, responding to external shocks as they occur. To support decision-making, CBNs require a cause-and-effect map of the variables under consideration, known as the network's structure. Learning the graphical structure of a causal model from data remains challenging; learning it from time-series data is even harder because dependencies may arise at different time lags. We construct a method that jointly learns a temporal ordering and a dominant lag for each selected ordered variable pair. Our contribution is a decomposable BIC-style objective score for mixed data that combines node-specifi
s28d8252584.summary: Researchers present a method for learning causal structure from time-series data where dependencies occur at variable time lags.

sfe1d34f9b4.title: Exposing and Mitigating Temporal Attack in Deepfake Video Detection
sfe1d34f9b4.description: arXiv:2605.07398v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While spatiotemporal deepfake detectors achieve high AUC, our experiments reveal their susceptibility to evasion attacks. These models tend to overfit on fragile temporal spectrum cues, rather than learning robust semantic causality. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose SpInShield, a temporal spectral-invariant defense framework explicitly designed to decouple semantic motion from manipulatable spectral artifacts. We propose a learnable spectral adversary that dynamically synthesizes severe spectral deformations, simulating extreme attack scenarios. sfe1d34f9b4.summary: Researchers show spatiotemporal deepfake detectors overfit to fragile temporal spectrum cues and propose SpInShield, a spectral-invariant defense against evasion attacks.
sfe1d34f9b4.why: Highlights that high-AUC deepfake detectors can be easily evaded, relevant to teams deploying detection in adversarial settings.

sa1970c439d.title: Hybrid Mechanical and Agentic Specification Inference
sa1970c439d.description: arXiv:2605.10005v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Adoption of formal verification has long been hindered by the cost of manual specification. To prove high-level properties, one must also write contracts for supporting functions, many of which are mechanical and low-level. Specification inference automatically derives such contracts from the program. We present a hybrid of mechanical and agentic inference for Move, a smart contract language, integrated into its verifier, the Move Prover. A large language model (LLM) agent drives inference and verification through a tool that calls the Move Prover and derives specifications from code by weakest-precondition (WP) analysis. sa1970c439d.summary: Researchers describe a hybrid of mechanical and LLM-agent specification inference for Move smart contracts, integrated into the Move Prover verifier.
sa1970c439d.why: Shows an agentic LLM loop driving formal verification tooling, which may reduce the manual cost of writing contracts for smart contract teams.

s49f09a08f2.title: Wavelet Flow Matching for Multi-Scale Physics Emulation
s49f09a08f2.description: arXiv:2605.16573v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate emulation of multi-scale physical systems governed by PDEs demands models that remain stable over long autoregressive rollouts while preserving fine-scale structures. Deterministic emulators produce overly smoothed predictions, while generative approaches better capture details but are costly. Latent-space generative models have emerged as a compromise but with the additional cost of separately pre-trained autoencoders. We propose Wavelet Flow Matching (WFM), a generative emulator that overcomes current trade-offs between cost and skill by performing optimal-transport flow matching directly in the multi-scale wavelet space. s49f09a08f2.summary: Researchers propose Wavelet Flow Matching, a generative emulator for multi-scale PDE physics that aims to avoid the cost of separately pre-trained autoencoders.

sf39a6534a2.title: TransitLM: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Map-Free Transit Route Generation
sf39a6534a2.description: arXiv:2605.22355v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Public transit route planning traditionally depends on structured map infrastructure and complex routing engines, and no existing dataset supports training models to bypass this dependency. We present TransitLM, a large-scale dataset of nearly 13 million transit route planning records from four Chinese cities covering 120,845 stations and 13,666 lines, released as a continual pre-training corpus and benchmark data for three evaluation tasks with complementary metrics. Experiments show that an LLM trained on TransitLM produces structurally valid routes at high accuracy and implicitly grounds arbitrary GPS coordinates to appropriate stations without any explicit mapping. sf39a6534a2.summary: Researchers release TransitLM, a dataset of about 13 million transit route records from four Chinese cities for training LLMs to generate routes without map infrastructure.
sf39a6534a2.why: Provides a large benchmark and continual pre-training corpus for LLM-based route generation, though the text gives limited evaluation detail.

s805c6fa92a.title: DeltaBox: Millisecond-Scale Sandbox Checkpoint and Rollback for Stateful AI Agents
s805c6fa92a.description: arXiv:2605.22781v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Emerging LLM-powered AI agent workloads, such as test-time tree search and reinforcement learning (RL), require high-frequency state exploration, relying on rapid checkpoint/restore (C/R) of the complete sandbox state, including files and process state. Existing mechanisms duplicate the entire state, causing hundreds of milliseconds to seconds of latency per C/R, which severely bottlenecks deep search and large-scale fan-outs. We observe that consecutive sandbox states between checkpoints differ only marginally. s805c6fa92a.summary: Researchers introduce DeltaBox, a sandbox checkpoint and rollback system that stores only state differences to reach millisecond-scale restores for stateful AI agents.
s805c6fa92a.why: Faster sandbox checkpoint and restore could remove a bottleneck for agent tree search and RL workloads that need many state branches.

s52e8f65e2b.title: Larch: Learned Query Optimization for Semantic Predicates
s52e8f65e2b.description: arXiv:2606.07923v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the advent of Large Language Models (LLMs), many database systems introduced semantic operators that enabled analytical queries over unstructured data (e.g. text, images, videos). Semantic operators typically incur high inference costs and latencies making semantic (AI) SQL queries challenging to apply on large scale datasets. At the same time, their semantic nature leads database engines to treat them as black boxes, making AISQL queries difficult to optimize. In this paper, we introduce Larch, a framework for optimizing the execution of semantic filters in AI SQL queries. Larch was inspired by two key observations: i) the high latency of semantic operators leaves significant room for computationally-heavy runtime optimization
s52e8f65e2b.summary: Researchers present Larch, a learned query optimizer for semantic predicates in AI SQL queries that call costly LLM-based semantic operators.
s52e8f65e2b.why: Addresses high inference cost of semantic operators in database queries, which matters to teams running LLM-powered analytics at scale.

se012f8559c.title: QVal: Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
se012f8559c.description: arXiv:2606.32034v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly act over long horizons, where outcome-only rewards say little about which intermediate actions were good. Dense supervision methods address this by scoring intermediate steps, but they are usually evaluated through the downstream performance of a full training pipeline. This is expensive, confounds signal quality with other training choices, and means that methods are rarely compared on common ground. We introduce QVal, a training-free testbed that measures the $Q$-alignment of a dense signal: whether it orders the candidate actions in each state the same way as their returns under a reference policy do. se012f8559c.summary: Researchers introduce QVal, a training-free testbed that measures how well dense supervision signals order intermediate steps for long-horizon LLM agents.
se012f8559c.why: Offers a cheaper way to compare dense reward signals for agent training without running full training pipelines.

s793f1ad820.title: When Simpler Is Better: Evaluating Translation Pipelines for Medieval Latin Manuscripts
s793f1ad820.description: arXiv:2607.03836v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Despite remarkable progress in machine translation, Vision Language Models (VLMs) struggle on historical manuscripts, a domain that stresses core Natural Language Processing (NLP) capabilities: low-resource transliteration, archaic vocabulary, and noisy input signals. We present a systematic framework for evaluating the full image-to-translation pipeline on medieval Latin manuscripts, a setting in which scribal shorthand, ligatures, and parchment degradation expose failure modes that are invisible in clean-text benchmarks. s793f1ad820.summary: Researchers evaluate image-to-translation pipelines for medieval Latin manuscripts, finding that simpler approaches can outperform more complex ones on vision-language tasks.
s793f1ad820.why: Shows vision-language models struggle on noisy historical documents, a caution for OCR and translation pipelines in low-resource domains.

se8cc1f2209.title: URSA: Chemistry-Aware Benchmark for Utilitarian Retrosynthesis Assessment
se8cc1f2209.description: arXiv:2607.04688v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Synthesis planning aiming to find pathways of reactions for a target molecule is one of the most important and challenging tasks in drug discovery. Recent progress has produced both specialized deep-learning retrosynthesis systems and general-purpose large language models, but objective comparison remains difficult due to the lack of flexible, chemically interpretable benchmarking protocols. se8cc1f2209.summary: Researchers introduced URSA, a chemistry-aware benchmark framework for evaluating retrosynthesis planning systems, including deep-learning tools and general-purpose LLMs.
se8cc1f2209.why: It offers a chemically interpretable way to compare retrosynthesis systems, which helps teams choose tools for drug discovery workflows.

s059c443f23.title: Input Pathways Shape Few-Shot, Not Zero-Shot, Binding in Tiny Transformers: A Fully-Enumerable Study
s059c443f23.description: arXiv:2607.04926v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How does the way information reaches a transformer -- as symbolic tokens, a clean per-factor "oracle" code, or an entangled perceptual vector -- shape whether it binds that information compositionally? We study ~6-10K-parameter transformers on finite factored worlds enumerated exhaustively, so every measurement covers the whole input space and the informative routes are information-matched (exact Bayes ceiling 1.0). s059c443f23.summary: A study of ~6-10K-parameter transformers on exhaustively enumerated factored worlds finds input encoding affects few-shot but not zero-shot compositional binding.

s067e89c697.title: REFORGE: A Method for Benchmarking LLMs' Reverse Engineering Capabilities in Decompiled Binary Function Naming
s067e89c697.description: arXiv:2607.07738v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to reverse-engineering tasks, and recent threat-intelligence reporting shows them operating inside live offensive-security workflows. Claims about their capability, however, outpace our ability to measure it. Existing benchmarks for LLM-assisted binary analysis treat the construction of function-level ground truth as a solved pre-processing step and report accuracy without disclosing how many functions were reliably evaluable. s067e89c697.summary: Researchers propose REFORGE, a method for benchmarking LLMs on naming decompiled binary functions, arguing existing benchmarks skip reliable ground-truth construction.
s067e89c697.why: Current LLM reverse-engineering accuracy claims may overstate capability because evaluable function counts are rarely disclosed, affecting security tool assessments.

s8c0b3ea0b2.title: CPM-MultiAgent: A CPM-Grounded Appraisal Framework for Simulating Dynamic Patient Emotional Evolution in Healthcare Dialogue
s8c0b3ea0b2.description: arXiv:2607.07824v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) enable patient simulation for healthcare communication training, where learners practice responding to clinical information, concerns, and emotional reactions. However, existing patient simulation and affective dialogue systems often represent patient emotions as static attributes or focus on recognizing emotions and generating empathetic responses. They provide limited support for modeling how a simulated patient's emotional state evolves in response to a healthcare professional's communication. Changes in patient emotion constitute interactional feedback that learners must recognize and respond to across dialogue turns. We draw on the Component Process Model (CPM), a psychological theory that explains
s8c0b3ea0b2.summary: CPM-MultiAgent is a framework for simulating how a virtual patient's emotions evolve across healthcare dialogue, aimed at communication training.

s4db670c3f0.title: Courteous Anticipation: Improving Long-Lived Task Planning in Persistent Shared Environments
s4db670c3f0.description: arXiv:2607.20289v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a task planning scenario in which robots sharing a persistent environment are assigned tasks one at a time from a held-out sequence. Standard task planners, lacking foresight of future tasks and inconsiderate of others' constraints, solve each task in isolation, leaving terminal states that increase future cost for all; side effects that compound over lengthy task sequences. To reduce cost over the sequence, a robot must anticipate how its actions now may impact performance on future tasks for all robots sharing the environment. s4db670c3f0.summary: Researchers propose a planning approach where robots sharing a persistent environment anticipate how their actions affect future tasks for all robots.
s4db670c3f0.why: Multi-robot planners that ignore downstream effects can accumulate costs over long task sequences, relevant to fleet and warehouse automation.

sa2bb803cab.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
sa2bb803cab.description: arXiv:2607.29617v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Imitation learning (IL)---training an agent to replicate expert behavior from demonstrations---underpins applications from robotics to language model training. Standard approaches such as Behavior Cloning (BC) are known to suffer from compounding errors and performance plateaus, particularly when the learner cannot perfectly represent the expert's policy (as is typical, e.g., in distillation). sa2bb803cab.summary: A paper examines when on-policy expert querying helps value-based imitation learning, analyzing representational tradeoffs versus behavior cloning.

s17f82ce264.title: Cloud-Edge LLM Collaborative Learning via Accelerating Personalized Bilevel Optimization
s17f82ce264.description: arXiv:2609.15664v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Amid the rapid advancement of physical-world intelligence, cloud-edge collaborative large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising roadmap for practical LLM deployment. However, existing cloud-edge paradigms struggle to balance global consensus with local personalization, which fails to satisfy the need for a unified knowledge foundation on the cloud and domain-specific adaptation at the edge. To address this, we propose a personalized bilevel optimization framework that formalizes cloud-edge LLM collaboration as a dual structure: the upper level optimizes edge-side personalization, while the lower level governs cloud-side knowledge transfer, reaching cloud-edge evolving in coordination. s17f82ce264.summary: Researchers propose a personalized bilevel optimization framework for cloud-edge LLM collaboration, balancing global consensus with local edge personalization.
s17f82ce264.why: Cloud-edge LLM deployments must balance shared knowledge with per-device adaptation, a practical architecture question for teams deploying models at the edge.

sf376523054.title: Hidden not Deleted: How Networks Suppress Entangled Features
sf376523054.description: arXiv:2609.27593v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When a neural network stops reporting a feature, has it forgotten the feature or merely hidden it? With the representation fixed, restoring a single bias partially recovers target detection by exposing a signal hidden behind the output's activation threshold. sf376523054.summary: A small autoencoder study shows that suppressed neural network features are often hidden behind activation thresholds rather than deleted.

sb85696c75a.title: From Data to Program: Fast & Direct Generative Program Inference from Empirical Data
sb85696c75a.description: arXiv:2609.35348v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Estimating probability densities from a finite set of samples typically requires dataset-specific model fitting. We introduce PRODiGI, a pretrained data-to-program model that infers an explicit, executable generative program in a single forward pass. Pretrained on synthetic datasets paired with their ground-truth programs, PRODiGI accommodates diverse generative families and data dimensionalities through template prediction and non-autoregressive program parameter decoding. Its inferred programs support direct sampling, density and score evaluation, and inspection independently of the pretrained model. We further introduce program-space fine-tuning, which refines differentiable program parameters by maximizing the likelihood of empi
sb85696c75a.summary: PRODiGI is a pretrained model that infers an executable generative program from data samples in a single forward pass.
sb85696c75a.why: Direct data-to-program inference could replace dataset-specific density model fitting, though the text gives limited detail on practical performance.

s04b7be52c5.title: Parameterization method of reservoir properties for ensemble-based data assimilation using intermediate latent space of StyleGAN
s04b7be52c5.description: arXiv:2609.39626v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ensemble smoothers are the most successful and efficient techniques currently available for history matching. However, because these methods rely on Gaussian assumptions, their performance is severely degraded when the prior geology is described in terms of complex facies distributions (non-Gaussian). In this way, for these methods, we need to apply efficient parameterization techniques. Currently, the most efficient methods for performing parameterization are deep learning models. However, given the variety of existing deep learning models, studies have not identified which is most suitable for use with ensemble-based methods, although some important models had already been evaluated. Based on a recent literature review, the most p
s04b7be52c5.summary: Researchers propose parameterizing reservoir properties using StyleGAN's intermediate latent space for ensemble-based history matching of non-Gaussian geology.

s8f856e07dc.title: Cross-Benchmark Transfer from RL on Agentic Coding Tasks
s8f856e07dc.description: arXiv:2610.00890v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coding agents often fail in the last mile: they build most of a feature but drop a requirement, test only the cases their implementation already handles, break behavior that was supposed to stay intact, or validate against an unchecked assumption. We ask whether reinforcement learning (RL) on expert-built agentic coding tasks closes this gap, and whether what the agent learns transfers beyond the training distribution. We post-train Kimi K2.7 Code, a 1T-parameter (32B active) open-weight mixture-of-experts model, with RL alone on 1,700 tasks: 1,000 repository tasks graded by hidden fail-to-pass tests and by pass-to-pass tests of existing behavior, and 700 terminal tasks graded by expert-written hidden verifiers. The reward is the fr
s8f856e07dc.summary: Researchers post-trained Kimi K2.7 Code, a 1T-parameter open-weight MoE model, using RL on 1,700 expert-built agentic coding tasks to study transfer across benchmarks.
s8f856e07dc.why: RL on agentic coding tasks may close the 'last mile' gaps in coding agents, relevant to teams building or evaluating coding assistants.

se6c92d4d3d.title: Nearly Optimal Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with 1-Bit Feedback
se6c92d4d3d.description: arXiv:2610.02771v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study fixed-confidence best-arm identification under strict 1-bit feedback constraints. At each round, the learner selects an arm and a query set, and receives only a single bit indicating whether the sampled reward belongs to that set. We consider a distribution-free finite-variance setting with arm-wise localization, where direct empirical mean estimation is no longer available and clipping becomes unavoidable. We first formulate a time-uniform 1-bit mean-estimation primitive based on randomized threshold queries and a clipped tail-integral identity. We then embed this primitive into candidate-challenger best-arm identification algorithms. A fixed-clipping algorithm gives a simple anytime $(\epsilon,\delta)$-PAC guarantee, whil
se6c92d4d3d.summary: A paper studies fixed-confidence best-arm identification under strict 1-bit feedback, developing a time-uniform 1-bit mean-estimation primitive.

s517e2c79a9.title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
s517e2c79a9.description: arXiv:2610.03713v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continual learning treats any drop in performance on previously seen data as forgetting, a convention inherited from settings where the prediction target is stationary. World models violate this assumption: their target is the environment, which changes, so knowledge that was accurate when learned can later become false, and revising it is correct behavior rather than a defect. Non-stationary ground truth is well studied in the concept drift literature and in the temporal factuality of language models, but it has not been formulated for world models, which are distinctive in that they also encode structural knowledge, such as physical laws and object permanence, that must never be degraded. We argue that continual world models need
s517e2c79a9.summary: Researchers argue that world models should selectively retain knowledge, treating accurate-then-outdated information as correct revision rather than forgetting.
s517e2c79a9.why: Continual-learning evaluation that counts necessary revisions as forgetting may misjudge world model quality in changing environments.

s9d6f71dabb.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
s9d6f71dabb.description: arXiv:2610.13672v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models struggle to reliably identify and correct errors in their own reasoning. Unlike prior training-based approaches that fine-tune an LLM to generate revisions or feedback, we learn where to intervene in failed rollouts and determine how to redirect them. To choose where to intervene, we train a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder using only final-answer correctness. For redirection, we find that under a fixed generation budget, the tested inline injections fail to reliably redirect reasoning, whereas presenting the same instruction in a new user turn changes the model's course. The resulting correction framework, UPTURN (User-Prompt TURN injection at a learned position), requires no LLM fine-tuning: it ret
s9d6f71dabb.summary: Researchers train a small MLP head to locate where to intervene in failed LLM reasoning rollouts, finding inline injections often fail to redirect reasoning.
s9d6f71dabb.why: Shows that naive inline correction prompts may not reliably fix LLM reasoning errors under fixed generation budgets.

s5e7debe60c.title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
s5e7debe60c.description: arXiv:2610.21025v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When does a language model acquire a capability? Developmental studies usually answer this by tracking when models start producing the correct token. But that prediction passes through the unembedding matrix, or readout, which is itself still being learned during pretraining. We show that a model's hidden states can encode task information before its own readout expresses it, so timelines read from outputs conflate what the model encodes with what its readout expresses. To track the readout directly, we introduce parameter-trajectory crosscoding, which fits one sparse dictionary to every token's readout row at every checkpoint. s5e7debe60c.summary: A paper introduces parameter-trajectory tracking to measure when a language model's unembedding readout expresses capabilities its hidden states already encode.
s5e7debe60c.why: Output-based capability timelines may misdate when models acquire skills, which matters for evaluating training progress and checkpoints.

sc8d74ff070.title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
sc8d74ff070.description: arXiv:2610.28411v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep learning models have become essential tools in medical imaging, yet training them end-to-end for diverse tasks remains challenging due to limited labeled data and computational constraints. To address this, we introduce Brain2Vec, a foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans pooled from multiple studies. Brain2Vec can serve both as a weight initialization backbone for fine-tuning downstream tasks and as a standalone feature extractor. We evaluated Brain2Vec in three tasks: downstream predictive performance, convergence speed, and embedding quality. Using Brain2Vec's pretrained weights as initialization and fine-tuning on labeled data for a brain age prediction task, results demonst
sc8d74ff070.summary: Researchers introduced Brain2Vec, a self-supervised 3D foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted brain MRI scans, usable for fine-tuning or as a feature extractor.
sc8d74ff070.why: Shows pretraining a large medical imaging foundation model on pooled data can serve as a reusable backbone when labeled data is scarce.

scd0f08d5fb.title: Operationalizing Governed Agentic Workflows in Regulated Finance: A Customer Zero Case Study using Zafin AIOS
scd0f08d5fb.description: arXiv:2610.33253v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Regulated industries such as finance and healthcare face critical governance challenges that hamper the adoption of AI-assisted software development and hinder the transition from experimental pilots to production work. This paper presents Zafin AIOS, an end-to-end orchestration platform and control plane designed to deploy AI within regulated industries such as finance. We provide the architectural principles and an empirical comparison between AI-assisted and human-led workloads. To validate this framework empirically, we conduct a case study analysis of Zafin's internal enterprise workflows, which we refer to as Customer Zero. This paper contributes a production case study of AI-assisted software engineering in regulated industri
scd0f08d5fb.summary: Researchers presented Zafin AIOS, an orchestration platform and control plane for deploying governed AI-assisted development in regulated finance, with a case study comparing AI-assisted and human-led work.
scd0f08d5fb.why: Offers architectural patterns for governance controls that teams in regulated industries need to move AI development from pilots to production.

s272aff2fb8.title: EmbodiExp: Compositional Experience Transfer for Embodied Agents
s272aff2fb8.description: arXiv:2610.39180v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Experience from past tasks can help embodied agents perform new tasks, but it may not remain applicable or effective when conditions change. Tasks with different overall goals often share subgoals, providing a basis for cross-task experience transfer. We present EmbodiExp, a framework for constructing outcome-grounded subgoal experiences and composing them in new tasks. Each experience describes how to pursue a subgoal, when the guidance applies, and what outcome must be verified for completion. Verified outcomes from applying one experience can satisfy the conditions for applying another, allowing experiences from different past tasks to be composed online. By examining the actions and observed outcomes at the subgoal level, Embodi
s272aff2fb8.summary: Researchers propose EmbodiExp, a framework that builds outcome-verified subgoal experiences for embodied agents and composes them to transfer experience across tasks with shared subgoals.
s272aff2fb8.why: Suggests reusable, verified subgoal experiences may help robotic agents generalize across tasks, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s0da9bcce49.title: NaijaFacts: A Framework for Disentangling Language from Knowledge in Facts about Nigeria
s0da9bcce49.description: arXiv:2611.06504v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multilingual benchmarks for African languages mostly translate generic questions into local languages, measuring linguistic competence but not whether models know facts about Africa. We introduce NaijaFacts, a benchmark of factual and statistical questions about Nigeria, authored by native speakers and grounded in authoritative official statistics, with every question available in English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yor\`ub\'a, Igbo, and Hausa. Answering similar questions for the UK and US yields a country by language matrix that disentangles a language effect (the model knows the fact but degrades in a low-resource language) from a knowledge effect (the fact is absent in every language). Across eight frontier and Nigeria-adapted models, the
s0da9bcce49.summary: Researchers released NaijaFacts, a benchmark of native-speaker-authored factual questions about Nigeria in English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa, compared against UK and US questions.
s0da9bcce49.why: Separates factual knowledge from language competence in multilingual evaluation, which matters for teams assessing models on African-language content.

sd5979cc0db.title: Accepted but Wrong: Silent Failures of LLM Code Repairs after API Migrations
sd5979cc0db.description: arXiv:2611.08269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: After an API migration, an LLM-repaired procedure can run cleanly yet return wrong results, and a typical-input release check ships it. We report a preregistered study of 73 tasks on 60 documented changes in CPython, Node.js and SQLite. In the main stages, repairs are choices among documented code fragments, run on the real runtimes against withheld contracts. Over the complete repair space, the all-assertions gate on typical inputs released 0.410 of wrong repairs. One edge input written from the release note cut this to 0.065, and to 0.061 on 15 unseen clusters; three inputs from a blind low-cost commercial writer (GPT-5.6-luna) reached 0.070. Two more frozen stages enlarged the menu to 1491 fragments and added 233 hard distractors
sd5979cc0db.summary: A preregistered study of 73 tasks across 60 API changes in CPython, Node.js and SQLite found LLM code repairs can run cleanly yet return wrong results that typical-input checks miss.
sd5979cc0db.why: Shows typical-input release checks let many wrong LLM-generated repairs ship, so teams need edge-case tests derived from release notes.

s6d8cd8c87c.title: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
s6d8cd8c87c.description: arXiv:2611.10123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Can a language model report a pain state it represents? Recent work reported a linear pain direction in open-weight models that, when amplified, leads fine-tuned models to choose actions that delete a user's photographs or their own weights. We asked whether models can say when that direction is active, on three open-weight models from two families, with and without the original work's adapters, and under every protocol we tried they cannot. Using Open-Weight Masked Introspection (OWMI), we added the pain direction and its nearest emotional neighbours to the residual stream while models answered neutral tasks, then asked what had changed, against sham runs, random perturbations matched in output disruption, and a text-only condition
s6d8cd8c87c.summary: A study found that three open-weight language models cannot report when an injected pain direction is active, across every protocol tested using the OWMI method.
s6d8cd8c87c.why: Indicates that models' self-reports about internal states are unreliable, which matters for anyone relying on model introspection for safety monitoring.

s719682cd7e.title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
s719682cd7e.description: arXiv:2611.12799v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning is now the mainstream paradigm for training LLMs on agentic tasks, yet standard practice keeps only the best-validation checkpoint and discards the rest. We show that this is lossy: in GRPO training of LLM agents, the best-validation checkpoint fails on problems that earlier checkpoints from the same run had already solved, and the union of problems solved across checkpoints far exceeds any single one. The discarded checkpoints thus form a teacher pool obtained at no additional training cost, which on-policy distillation (OPD) can mine to recover the lost coverage. Mining this pool raises two challenges: i) which checkpoint to distill from, as no checkpoint dominates the others and complementarity to the stude
s719682cd7e.summary: Agentic-OPD proposes recovering capabilities from discarded RL checkpoints by using earlier checkpoints as a teacher pool for on-policy distillation in agentic LLM training.
s719682cd7e.why: Suggests checkpoints normally discarded during GRPO agent training can be reused at no extra training cost to recover solved problems.

s05a355378b.title: Before Words, Beyond Speech: Evaluating Nonverbal Social Reasoning in Early Childhood
s05a355378b.description: arXiv:2611.13213v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Children's earliest years are a period of intense social learning, during which meaning is built through gaze, gesture, and physical contact. Yet, this critical aspect of social interaction remains under-evaluated in multimodal video understanding, as existing benchmarks prioritize the conversation-driven interactions of adults. We address this gap with \bench ($\textbf{N}$aturalistic $\textbf{E}$arly-childhood $\textbf{S}$ocial in$\textbf{T}$eractions), the first child-centric benchmark for nonverbal social reasoning. \bench comprises \totalvids manually annotated clips ($\sim$12s) curated for diversity across naturalistic settings, cultural contexts, and developmental stages. Beyond a lack of data, targeted model improvement in th
s05a355378b.summary: Researchers introduced NESTI, a benchmark for evaluating nonverbal social reasoning in early-childhood videos, focusing on gaze, gesture and physical contact.
s05a355378b.why: Highlights a gap in multimodal video benchmarks, which mostly target adult conversational interaction.

s028ccf691b.title: Deletion Sensitivity Is a Property of the Model: A Three-Condition Measurement over 72 Valid Experimental Cells
s028ccf691b.description: arXiv:2611.13223v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reasoning models write a trace at every turn of a multi-turn tool session, and later turns read it. Upstream providers hold different retention constraints, so a request forwarded across issuers arrives with its history deleted, and its task cost remains unmeasured. This paper reports a direct, blind, multi-seed measurement of full history deletion in multi-turn tool calling, through three rendering conditions, a calibrated set of 72 valid experimental cells, a multi-seed protocol, and the official checker. The same deletion separates the models by direction and by magnitude, one class losing tens of points, another gaining, and a third unchanged, with the endpoint ordering reproduced across seeds and task subsets modulating the mag
s028ccf691b.summary: A multi-seed study across 72 valid experimental cells measured how deleting full reasoning history in multi-turn tool-calling sessions affects model task performance.
s028ccf691b.why: Shows deleting history when requests cross providers can change task outcomes, relevant for teams routing multi-turn agent traffic across issuers.

sae658b55be.title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA
sae658b55be.description: arXiv:2611.13331v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fine-tuning large-scale foundation models across resource-constrained, distributed clients presents significant computational and communication challenges. While merging Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with Federated Learning (FL) enables rank-based flexibility, the interdependence of the adaptation matrices ($\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$) often complicates optimization. In this work, we theoretically demonstrate that LoRA fine-tuning with Gaussian initialization and a frozen $\mathbf{A}$ matrix acts as a stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning, where batch gradients are subject to a random, rank-dependent perturbation. Motivated by this insight, we propose freezing and periodically resampling $\mathbf{A}$ matrices at the client lev
sae658b55be.summary: Researchers propose stochastic projections and rank-aware learning rates for federated LoRA fine-tuning, arguing frozen-A LoRA with Gaussian initialization approximates full fine-tuning.
sae658b55be.why: Offers theory and methods for communication-efficient fine-tuning of foundation models across resource-constrained distributed clients.

s6b61db8712.title: ForeSpark: Joint Draft and Verification Budget Scheduling for Parallel Speculative Decoding
s6b61db8712.description: arXiv:2611.13442v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parallel drafters accelerate LLM decoding by proposing a whole block of draft tokens in a single forward pass, making them attractive for LLM serving. Recent systems optimize goodput (i.e., accepted tokens per second) because rejected drafts steal compute from other requests. However, these systems control only how many tokens are verified, so every request still drafts a full block. At high serving load, we find that drafting consumes up to 40% of step time, of which a majority is discarded because it is never verified. s6b61db8712.summary: ForeSpark proposes jointly scheduling draft and verification budgets for parallel speculative decoding, noting drafting can consume up to 40% of step time at high serving load.
s6b61db8712.why: Targets wasted compute in LLM serving, where most drafted tokens are discarded, which directly affects inference throughput and cost.

scf5d1f715b.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
scf5d1f715b.description: arXiv:2611.13971v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Generative inpainting can remove the occluder but replaces the missing image content with synthesis, which is unsuitable when visual provenance matters. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regio
scf5d1f715b.summary: Researchers present TransGHOST, a causal, reference-guided method for real-time reconstruction of tissue occluded by instruments in ophthalmic microsurgery video, without synthesis.
scf5d1f715b.why: Relevant to robot-assisted surgical systems that need reliable scene perception, though the text offers little on deployment readiness.

sa19e53c482.title: CastWorld: Benchmarking Context-Aware Agentic Time Series Forecasting Beyond Predictive Accuracy
sa19e53c482.description: arXiv:2611.15262v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Agentic time series forecasting extends conventional approaches beyond one-shot numerical prediction toward autonomous, context-aware interaction. However, existing benchmarks offer limited integrated support for diverse contextual information, forecasting-specific adaptive interactions, and systematic evaluation of forecasting agents. In this paper, we introduce CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting. First, its context-rich dataset suite spans 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets, covering external variables, events, and historical cases under a unified context specification. Second, a lightweight, modular forecasting-native harness provides 49 core tools and a state-adaptive loop that tracks for
sa19e53c482.summary: Researchers introduced CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting spanning 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets.
sa19e53c482.why: Provides a way to evaluate forecasting agents beyond numerical accuracy, including their use of contextual information.

s5cdca25a2f.title: CARE-Drive: Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories
s5cdca25a2f.description: arXiv:2611.15360v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models bring multimodal understanding and world knowledge to end-to-end autonomous driving. To further improve the quality of predicted trajectories, existing studies introduce candidate refinement, residual denoising, and token correction. However, these methods typically focus on unified refinement of the entire trajectory, paying limited attention to the distinct physical quantities and their interactions. We further investigate physical specialization and coordination in trajectory refinement, centering on position and heading for simpler and more intuitive correction modeling. s5cdca25a2f.summary: CARE-Drive proposes coupled alternating refinement of ego-trajectories for vision-language-action models in end-to-end autonomous driving, specializing refinement across physical quantities.
s5cdca25a2f.why: Offers a trajectory refinement approach for VLA-based driving models, though the text gives little on measured gains.

sf1afdd74ed.title: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents
sf1afdd74ed.description: arXiv:2611.16174v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on expert trajectories is a standard paradigm for training LLM agents. However, it suffers from a well-known training-inference distribution mismatch, calling for target-aware data synthesis strategies that ground the training data in the target model's native state distribution. To bridge this gap, emerging approaches incorporate the expert either to guide mixed rollouts alongside the target model, or to provide dense step-wise supervision. sf1afdd74ed.summary: JudgeMix proposes judge-guided mixed-rollout data synthesis to train LLM agents, aiming to ground supervised fine-tuning data in the target model's own state distribution.
sf1afdd74ed.why: Addresses the training-inference distribution mismatch in agent SFT, a practical issue for teams fine-tuning agents on expert trajectories.

sd1d5743b5e.title: Indic-Task Gains and Regressions after Reinforcement Learning
sd1d5743b5e.description: arXiv:2611.16228v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We run reinforcement learning (RL) with GRPO across four environments, starting from a supervised fine-tuned 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model covering English and eight Indic languages. We compare the model before and after RL across 34 benchmarks in one evaluation campaign. MATH improves by 36.07 points, and most Indic benchmarks also improve. Yet XQuAD-Indic F1 falls 19.32 points as English answers rise from 8.7% to 91.7%; IndicQA falls 8.64, while English XQuAD gains 11.71 F1. A second RL run from the same supervised initialization adds an Indic environment together with language and repetition rewards. Compared with the released model, it improves both passage-answering and instruction-following benchmarks, along with preserving
sd1d5743b5e.summary: Researchers applied GRPO reinforcement learning to a 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model covering English and eight Indic languages, finding math gains alongside Indic QA regressions.
sd1d5743b5e.why: RL post-training can lift some benchmarks while silently degrading others, such as low-resource language QA, so multilingual evals need checking before and after tuning.

sb67d815d4a.title: Rectified Looped Transformer
sb67d815d4a.description: arXiv:2611.16265v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Looped Transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying a shared block, offering a parameter-efficient approach to language modeling. However, most existing works directly reuse each loop's output as the next's input, which can lead to hidden-state scale growth and perturbation amplification as recurrence deepens. We propose Rectified Looped Transformer (RLT), which redesigns feedback between loops using an interpolation schedule inspired by flow-based modeling. At each loop, RLT forms the next input by linearly interpolating between the current state and its prediction. sb67d815d4a.summary: Researchers propose Rectified Looped Transformer, which redesigns loop feedback with an interpolation schedule to avoid hidden-state scale growth in looped language models.
sb67d815d4a.why: Looped transformers offer parameter-efficient depth, and this addresses instability that grows as recurrence deepens, relevant to efficient model architecture choices.

s6b753130ca.title: HyBridge: Bridge-Guided Self-Supervised Hyperbolic Hypergraph Representation Learning
s6b753130ca.description: arXiv:2611.16351v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hypergraphs capture groupwise relationships among multiple nodes and often exhibit tree-like structures. Although hyperbolic space is well suited for modeling such structures, simply extending existing hypergraph representation learning (HRL) methods to hyperbolic space does not consistently improve performance. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between node structural properties and hyperbolic embedding radii and find that bridge nodes tend to lie closer to the center in graphs, whereas this relationship is not consistently observed in hypergraphs. We further find that conventional bridge score estimation may fail to capture the groupwise connectivity of hypergraphs. Motivated by these findings, we propose HyBridge, a
s6b753130ca.summary: Researchers present HyBridge, a self-supervised hyperbolic hypergraph representation learning method that uses bridge-node structure to guide embeddings.

s60e155c105.title: ZONOS3-Mini Technical Report
s60e155c105.description: arXiv:2611.16525v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: ZONOS3-Mini is an ultra-compact, ultra-fast, zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model. The model can run in real time on a laptop or smartphone. For its latency and size, it achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and cloning fidelity. To achieve this we propose a latent MoE backbone with only 886M parameters (100M active per token) and a new audio codec, Zyphra Audio Codec 1 (ZAC-1), which represents 44.1 kHz audio at a 15 Hz frame rate. On the new ZTTS2-Eval benchmark, ZONOS3-Mini reaches a 6.71% macro-average WER over 55 language sets (35 clean and 20 in the wild), which is competitive with larger and slower state-of-the-art models. We release the model weights, inference, and training code.
s60e155c105.summary: Zyphra released a technical report for ZONOS3-Mini, an 886M-parameter zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model with a new audio codec, claiming real-time performance on laptops and phones.
s60e155c105.why: A compact, on-device voice-cloning model with a new codec could enable low-latency speech features without cloud inference costs.

sc9b6c856d8.title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLM
sc9b6c856d8.description: arXiv:2611.17461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current evaluations of Large Language Models (LLMs) report performance at the dataset or task level, revealing what a model achieves but offering little insight into the internal processing associated with its performance. We propose a task-centric framework for characterising the model-internal processing elicited by a benchmark. It combines attention- and activation-based signals with representation-based measures to characterise benchmarks spanning a continuum from retrieval-dominant to reasoning-dominant and to surface failure modes that task-level scores conceal. We evaluate 16 LLMs across 24 diverse benchmarks and conduct targeted internal-state analyses on representative models and tasks, observing systematic differences in processing
sc9b6c856d8.summary: Researchers propose a task-centric framework that combines attention, activation, and representation signals to characterize model-internal processing elicited by LLM benchmarks.
sc9b6c856d8.why: Going beyond aggregate benchmark scores to inspect internal processing can reveal failure modes that task-level metrics hide when comparing models.

s9b41115bae.title: Poetry 'resurrection' from LLMs
s9b41115bae.description: arXiv:2611.17464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In an era where linguistic creativity is challenged by algorithmic authorship, we pose a provocative question: can artificial intelligence (AI) write an infinite poem? We set up two experiments to investigate the quantitative and qualitative output produced by AI utilizing couplets that evidence a poetic relationship between end words, the only variation in a strict anaphoric, litany structure. Our results show that while AI can generate interesting pairings, it still falls short of human-level creativity and understanding of poetic relationships. We offer commentary and a brief survey of the field of computational poetry experiments, tracing back authorial intention and distinctions of 'natural' and 'artificial' poetry, as well as justifying
s9b41115bae.summary: Researchers tested whether AI can write an infinite poem using couplets with poetic end-word relationships, finding AI produces interesting pairings but falls short of human creativity.

se6172fe56f.title: Creating Steering Vectors via Input Optimisation
se6172fe56f.description: arXiv:2611.17481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Activation steering influences a language model's behaviour by adding a steering vector to its residual stream during generation, but it requires white-box access to modify the hidden states at every generation step. We introduce ActGCG, a modification of Greedy Coordinate Gradient which optimises a suffix to match the target activations obtained by adding a steering vector to the residual stream. We further introduce universal suffixes trained across many prompts at once, a model-translation step that rewrites the suffix into human-readable text midway through optimisation, and a soft-suffix variant to remove the discrete token space constraint. We study two behaviours: steering a model to answer in German, and anti-refusal steering for jail
se6172fe56f.summary: Researchers introduce ActGCG, which optimizes a text suffix to mimic activation steering effects, plus universal suffixes and a step that rewrites suffixes into readable text.
se6172fe56f.why: It suggests steering-like behavior could be induced through prompts alone, without white-box access to hidden states, which matters for deployed model control.

s11b0698244.title: CamSpokenNLI: A Pilot Resource for Cross-Variety Transfer Evaluation in Cameroon Pidgin English and Camfranglais
s11b0698244.description: arXiv:2611.17573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cameroon Pidgin English (a West African Pidgin English variety) and Camfranglais are widely used in Cameroon, yet to our knowledge, neither has a dedicated spoken Natural Language Inference (NLI) resource. We introduce CamSpokenNLI, a pilot dataset of 114 scenario-matched spoken NLI items in each variety (228 in total), recorded by one native speaker from Buea. Each item pairs premise audio and text with a hypothesis, an NLI label, and English glosses. The author assigned labels, so the dataset is an exploratory resource rather than a mature benchmark. The NLI experiments use the reference text; the audio is evaluated separately. XLM-RoBERTa baselines with five-fold item-level cross-validation reach 44.7% on Pidgin and 46.2% on Camfranglais (
s11b0698244.summary: Researchers released CamSpokenNLI, a pilot spoken natural language inference dataset of 228 items in Cameroon Pidgin English and Camfranglais, labeled by a single author.

sf714bb12bc.title: Small Open-Weight Language Models for Crowd Decision-Making: Capabilities and Limits of Output-Level Fusion and Linguistic Aggregation
sf714bb12bc.description: arXiv:2611.17589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small open-weight language models can run crowd decision-making (CDM) on an institution's own infrastructure, which keeps the checkpoint, the inference settings and the opinions under its control. Their judgements vary across repeated queries; whether repeating and aggregating them, often through the 2-tuple linguistic representation, settles the decision rather than the labels is untested. Five open-weight models of 8-36B total parameters on one consumer GPU and a hosted reference classify 474 TripAdvisor reviews of four London restaurants ten times each; three open-weight models repeat the protocol on 600 reviews of twelve Madrid restaurants. Continuous evaluations preserve resolution: snapping each review leaves 5 distinct values against 2
sf714bb12bc.summary: A study tests whether repeated queries to small open-weight LLMs, aggregated via linguistic methods, settle crowd decisions on 474 TripAdvisor restaurant reviews, finding limits.
sf714bb12bc.why: Running small open-weight models on in-house infrastructure keeps data and checkpoints under institutional control, though repeated outputs may not yield stable decisions.

sb68014ea04.title: What Do Multilingual Self-Supervised Speech Encoders Know About Sentence Meaning?
sb68014ea04.description: arXiv:2611.17686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) have been scaled up to thousands of languages and millions of hours of audio, yet little is known about how these models structure semantic knowledge across languages. In this work, we probe sentence-level semantics in massively multilingual S3Ms across 76 languages, using linear maps from frozen speech representations into a frozen text embedding space, evaluated by cross-modal retrieval. Sentence meaning is linearly accessible but highly uneven across languages and resource tiers. Cross-lingual probes can match language-specific probes on languages never seen in probe training, but per-model monolingual decodability does not predict transfer. sb68014ea04.summary: Researchers probe sentence-level semantics in 76-language self-supervised speech encoders using linear maps to text embeddings, finding meaning is uneven across languages and resource tiers.

s3f2e148862.title: See Every Block Once: Variance-Reduced Post-Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models
s3f2e148862.description: arXiv:2611.17754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy gradient methods are widely used to align large language model outputs with human preferences, but the log-likelihoods they require cannot be directly computed in Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs). MDLM post-training therefore relies on a surrogate objective based on the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), and recent work estimates a blockwise variant of this objective via Monte Carlo methods to support blockwise generation. However, existing estimation schemes randomly sample the block index, so they may evaluate the same block more than once and leave some blocks unevaluated. s3f2e148862.summary: Researchers propose a variance-reduced blockwise ELBO estimation scheme for policy-gradient post-training of masked diffusion language models, sampling blocks to cover each once.
s3f2e148862.why: Better gradient estimates for diffusion LLM alignment could make preference post-training of non-autoregressive models more efficient.

s80e268322e.title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG
s80e268322e.description: arXiv:2611.17788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), query rewriting serves as a core interface that aligns user intent with external knowledge bases, and its effectiveness directly determines overall system performance. However, generative retrieval faces three critical challenges in real-world deployment: noisy retrieval feedback, the difficulty of jointly optimizing discrete prompt templates and continuous decoding-control parameters, and the limited generalization of static rewriting strategies under semantically complex scenarios. To address these issues, we propose RAG-FGO, a dynamic optimization framework for generative retrieval strategies. s80e268322e.summary: Researchers present RAG-FGO, a method that dynamically optimizes query-rewriting agents for generative RAG, jointly tuning prompt templates and decoding parameters.
s80e268322e.why: Query rewriting strongly affects RAG quality, and joint optimization of rewriting prompts and decoding settings could improve retrieval pipelines in production.

s31b2bbe291.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
s31b2bbe291.description: arXiv:2611.17811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. Prior work studies how LLM reviews align with human ones, yet we know little about which parts of a paper these models actually criticize. In this work, we investigate 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, and show that the latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of their review weaknesses from the appendix. This behavior holds across the API, coding-agent, and web access methods for using LLMs to review a paper. s31b2bbe291.summary: A study of 2,000 ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR papers finds latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of review weaknesses from appendices.
s31b2bbe291.why: Teams using LLM reviewers or evaluators should know these models may weigh appendix content heavily, which can skew assessments of submitted work.

s11fbf68749.title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
s11fbf68749.description: arXiv:2611.17834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI conference submissions grow rapidly, AI reviewers are being considered as an alternative. However, simply imitating human reviewing is problematic because reviewing serves multiple purposes, including evaluating papers' soundness, interestingness, and clarity, the last two of which are subjective. In this work, we focus solely on evaluating soundness, the most important and objective criterion, and define the learning objective as jointly maximizing (1) precision, based on the soundness and substantiveness of review points, and (2) recall, the coverage of high-quality reference review points. Under this problem formulation, we construct a quality-labeled review point dataset, PaperSound-23K, using 1K ICLR submissions and 23K human-writt
s11fbf68749.summary: Researchers present PaperCritic, a method for training AI reviewers to assess paper soundness, optimizing precision and recall of review points on the objective criterion.

s1728c1b2b5.title: BLiMP-RO: A Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs for Romanian
s1728c1b2b5.description: arXiv:2611.17836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating grammatical knowledge in language models requires benchmarks that cover diverse linguistic phenomena and are validated against human judgments. We introduce BLiMP-RO, a Romanian minimal-pair benchmark covering 50 grammatical phenomena across ten domains. It comprises 493 linguist-constructed sentence pairs, evaluated by native speakers in five experiments, and 5,942 additional semi-automatically generated, human-validated pairs. We further investigate grammatical generalization under limited linguistic input by training GPT-2 and GPT-BERT models from scratch on Romanian BabyBabelLM data and a newly collected corpus of 10 million words from child-targeted video captions. s1728c1b2b5.summary: Researchers released BLiMP-RO, a Romanian minimal-pair benchmark of 493 linguist-built pairs across 50 grammatical phenomena, plus 5,942 semi-automatically generated validated pairs.

s7f26d9728b.title: In the Eye of the Beholder: Human Label Variation in Textual and Visual Entailment
s7f26d9728b.description: arXiv:2611.17954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human Label Variation (HLV) is increasingly recognised as an informative signal that reflects meaningful differences in how people interpret the same input. While HLV has been studied extensively in Natural Language Inference (NLI), much less is known about HLV in Visual Entailment (VE; Xie et al., 2019), where the textual premise is replaced by an image, keeping the hypothesis and label space fixed. We introduce VariNLI-VE, a dataset for studying how HLV changes between paired NLI and VE instances. We re-annotate a subset of originally neutral SNLI (Bowman et al., 2015) instances and their visual counterparts, with the same annotators evaluating both the textual and visual versions. Each annotation includes a label, confidence score, and exp
s7f26d9728b.summary: Researchers introduce VariNLI-VE, a dataset studying how human label variation changes when textual premises are replaced by images in entailment tasks.
s7f26d9728b.why: It shows human disagreement in multimodal labeling differs from text-only NLI, relevant for building and evaluating vision-language training data.

s2d46717342.title: Toward Universal Translatability: On the Statistical Ontology of Generative AI
s2d46717342.description: arXiv:2611.17963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper argues that the problem of translation functions both as a point of origin and as a normative horizon for contemporary generative AI. In current discourse around ''world models,'' their attainment is framed as the achievement of internal consistency, cross-modal alignment, and physical grounding. Taken together, these demands converge on an ideal of the model as a universal translation machine capable of establishing lossless correspondences across linguistic, visual, and physical representation spaces. s2d46717342.summary: A paper argues that translation serves as both origin and normative goal for generative AI, critiquing the ideal of models as universal translators across representation spaces.
s2d46717342.why: It is a philosophical critique of 'world model' framing, offering limited concrete guidance for engineering teams.

s4b4ac34500.title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls
s4b4ac34500.description: arXiv:2611.18050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a conversational Voice AI agent places an outbound call, the far end may be a live person, a voicemail greeting, an interactive voice response (IVR) system, or increasingly another AI system answering on the callee's behalf. Standard Answering Machine Detection (AMD) reports only whether a human or a machine picked up, a design meant for human call centres, where one machine is as uninteresting as another. That single bit does not tell a Voice AI agent what to do, since leaving a voicemail message, navigating an IVR and holding a short exchange with another AI are three different actions and a two-valued label cannot distinguish them. s4b4ac34500.summary: FEND is a method for detecting the far end of outbound Voice AI calls, distinguishing live humans, voicemail, IVR systems, and other AI systems.
s4b4ac34500.why: Standard answering machine detection only yields human-or-machine, which is insufficient for voice agents deciding whether to leave messages or navigate menus.

s2b5446e03b.title: Agent-as-a-Judge
s2b5446e03b.description: arXiv:2611.18067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence has progressed from task-specific systems toward general models spanning perception, generation, reasoning, and autonomous interaction, making reliable evaluation essential for comparison, deployment, and post-training feedback. At scale, modern evaluation pipelines increasingly rely on LLM-as-a-Judge to produce scores, preferences, and critiques; in its fixed-context setting, the judge relies on the supplied evaluand and evaluation materials. Yet a reliable verdict may require evidence beyond the supplied evaluand and context---either because critical environmental states remain unrecorded in the static execution log, or because controversial factual claims require external verification. Passive judges cannot obtain t
s2b5446e03b.summary: Agent-as-a-Judge proposes evaluation where the judge gathers evidence beyond the supplied material, extending the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm.
s2b5446e03b.why: Evaluation pipelines for deployed models may need agentic judges that verify evidence rather than relying only on fixed context.

s0f6b5482d0.title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization
s0f6b5482d0.description: arXiv:2611.18096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve strong multimodal performance, yet they remain prone to object hallucination---generating answers that are linguistically fluent but visually ungrounded. This issue is especially severe in low-resource languages, where weaker cross-modal alignment causes models to rely more on language priors than on image evidence. Existing remedies either require costly multilingual annotations or external translation/reward models, or intervene at inference time in ways that can distort the output language. s0f6b5482d0.why: It targets hallucinations in low-resource languages without costly multilingual annotation or external reward models, which matters for multilingual deployments.

s1b08a65242.title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity
s1b08a65242.description: arXiv:2611.18104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fingerprint by which a classifier recognizes the LLM behind a text is usually treated as a fixed property of the model. We show that it is contagious: a model that continues a conversation begun by another model inherits that model's fingerprint. This undermines audits of API relays, which can serve the first turns of a conversation with the model a customer pays for and silently hand the rest to a cheaper one. After such a handoff, detection of the substitute by a text classifier drops from 0.97 to 0.72 (DeepSeek replacing Claude Sonnet) and from 0.87 to 0.54 for a same-vendor downgrade (Haiku), and retraining on handoff data repairs only substitutes seen in training. s1b08a65242.summary: The paper shows that a model continuing another model's conversation inherits its text fingerprint, so API relays can silently substitute cheaper models after handoff.
s1b08a65242.why: This undermines audits of API providers, since customers paying for one model may receive a cheaper substitute mid-conversation.

s31fc06bc5d.title: Folding Language Models into Themselves
s31fc06bc5d.description: arXiv:2611.18113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge distillation usually trains a compact student from scratch, which needs a large amount of data even though the teacher's weights already encode most of what the student has to learn. In this work, we explore building the student directly from the teacher's weights. We propose Concertina, which folds every group of N adjacent teacher layers into one shared block that is executed N times. Each loop step carries a low-rank correction initialized from the layer it replaces, and a per-token gate mixes these corrections, to let every token recover the behavior of the original layers from a single shared block. s31fc06bc5d.why: It could reduce the data needed for distillation by reusing teacher weights, relevant for teams compressing models.

saefd0a36e0.title: A Multi-Layered AI Pipeline for BPMN Generation from Natural Language
saefd0a36e0.description: arXiv:2611.18157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The automated transformation of unstructured natural language process descriptions into Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) diagrams remains a challenging task, due to linguistic ambiguity and the difficulty to detect non-adjacent control-flow relationships. This paper proposes a solution for generating BPMN models from natural language descriptions through a multi-layered pipeline that integrates transformer-based architectures, Large Language Models and ontology population. The proposed method starts with natural language descriptions and separates textual processing, control-flow relation extraction, and structural validation into dedicated components. saefd0a36e0.summary: A multi-layered pipeline combining transformers, LLMs, and ontology population generates BPMN process diagrams from natural language descriptions.
saefd0a36e0.why: It offers an approach to automating business process modeling from text, though the summary gives few performance details.

sbb8f0e7140.title: NER-D: A cross-domain benchmark for German NER
sbb8f0e7140.description: arXiv:2611.18257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present NER-D, a cross-domain benchmark for German NER comprising 13 datasets spanning 9 domains, including General/Politics, Wikipedia, Legal, Medical, Historical, Financial, Agriculture and Archaeology. We examine the performance of both proprietary LLMs and state-of-the-art small open-source models using normal prompting and further examine the performance gains achievable via in-context learning and LoRA fine-tuning. s595f1b87ba.title: MamaReason: Unfinished Reasoning and Answer Recovery in Clinical Language Models
s595f1b87ba.description: arXiv:2611.18264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Answer continuation often returns a diagnosis already stated in unfinished clinical reasoning. se01a138c2b.description: arXiv:2611.18279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether a language model's answer is correct often depends on context: the same value can be right under one jurisdiction, date, or legal definition and wrong under another. se01a138c2b.summary: GT-FENG is a framework that checks language model answers against jurisdiction- and date-dependent rules to unify contextual correctness and rule-based error attribution.
se01a138c2b.why: Context-dependent correctness in law and policy domains is a practical evaluation problem for teams deploying LLMs in regulated settings.

sa24e8d5b5b.title: Learning Word-Level Explanations of Text Reuse in Latin Literature with Little Annotation
sa24e8d5b5b.description: arXiv:2611.18319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detecting an intertextual reference is only the first step; philologists also need to know how a later author reworked the source.
